A group of the scholars, including al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Abu Hanifa and his companions, al-Thawri and Abu Thawr, held that the jizya is not accepted except from the People of the Book.

Al-Awza'i and Malik said that the jizya is taken from all kinds of disbelievers, whoever they may be, and according to the first view the Magians are included among the People of the Book.

Ibn al-Mundhir said: I know of no disagreement that the jizya is taken from them.

The scholars differed concerning the amount of the jizya. 'Ata' said: there is no fixed amount for it; it is taken according to what they agreed upon in a settlement. Yahya ibn Adam, Abu 'Ubayd and Ibn Jarir also said this, except that the latter said: the least of it is one dinar, and its maximum has no limit.

Al-Shafi'i said: one dinar on the rich and the poor among free adult males, from which nothing is reduced. Abu Thawr also said this.

Al-Shafi'i said: and if they agree to more than one dinar, it is permitted, and if they increase it and their hearts are content with that, it is accepted from them.

Malik said: it is four dinars for the people of gold, and forty dirhams for the people of silver; the rich and the poor are equal, and even if he is a Magian it is neither increased nor decreased.

Abu Hanifa and his companions, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: twelve, twenty-four, and forty-eight (dirhams, according to the three classes of wealth).

The discussion of the jizya is established in its proper places, and the truth among these views we have established in our commentary on *al-Muntaqa* and in others of our works.

His saying: ﴿and they are humbled (*sagharun*)﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause, and *al-saghar* is abasement.

The meaning is: the dhimmi gives the jizya while in a state of humiliation. It has been said: this is that he brings it himself, on foot, not riding, and hands it over while standing, while the one receiving it is seated.

In sum, the one collecting the jizya should make the one handing it over, at the time of its collection, humbled and abased.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are impure﴾, the verse, that he said: except for a slave or one of the People of the Dhimma. It has also been reported as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report by another route.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related from Jabir, who said: the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "No polytheist shall enter this mosque of ours after this year of ours, except the people of the covenant and your servants."

Ibn Kathir said: Ahmad alone transmitted it as marfu', and the mawquf (traced only to a companion) version is more authentic.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: the polytheists used to come to the House, bringing food with them, trading with it. When they were forbidden to come to the House, the Muslims said: "From where will we get food?" So God revealed: ﴿And if you fear poverty, God will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills﴾. He said: so God sent down rain upon them, and their good increased when the polytheists departed from them.

Ibn Mardawayh related from him, who said: so God enriched them from His bounty, and commanded them to fight the People of the Book.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from 'Ikrima concerning His saying: ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾, that he said: it is destitution.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning His saying: ﴿then God will enrich you from His bounty﴾, that he said: through the jizya.

Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn al-Mundhir related from al-Dahhak something similar.

'Abd al-Razzaq related something similar from Qatada.

Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Hasan concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are impure﴾, that he said: filth (*qadhar*).

Abu al-Shaykh also related from him, who said: whoever shakes hands with them, let him perform ablution.

Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever shakes hands with a polytheist, let him perform ablution or wash his palms."

Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in God﴾, that he said: this verse was revealed when Muhammad ﷺ and his companions were commanded to the expedition of Tabuk.

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Shihab, who said: it was revealed concerning the disbelievers of Quraysh and the Arabs: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitna﴾, and it was revealed concerning the People of the Book: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in God﴾, the verse, up to His saying: ﴿until they give the jizya﴾. The first to give the jizya were the people of Najran.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 9, verse 28–29 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His words: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah﴾, meaning: those who do not affirm the Oneness of Allah; ﴿nor do they forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden﴾, meaning wine and silk; ﴿nor do they adopt the religion of truth﴾, meaning the religion of Islam; ﴿from among those who were given the Scripture, until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled﴾, meaning: subjugated.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, regarding His words: "willingly" (ʿan yadin), he said: "under compulsion" (ʿan qahrin).

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, regarding His words: "willingly" (ʿan yadin), he said: "from his own hand, and he should not send it through anyone else."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Abu Sinan, regarding His words: "willingly" (ʿan yadin), he said: "from a position of power" (ʿan qudrah).

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿while they are humbled﴾, he said: "they walk with it swaying from side to side" (mutaltilīn).

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, he said: "they are pushed/struck on the neck" (yulkazūn).

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Salman regarding the verse, he said: "not praiseworthy" (ghayru mahmudayn).

The words of God Most High: ﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of God."﴾ This is a fresh statement made to show the polytheism of the two groups of People of the Book. "Ezra" is the subject (mubtada', the grammatical subject) and "son of God" is its predicate (khabar). 'Asim and al-Kisa'i read "Ezra" with tanwin (nunation), while the rest read it without tanwin, because the word combines 'ujma (non-Arabic origin) and 'alamiyya (proper-name status).

Whoever reads it with tanwin has treated it as Arabic. It has also been said that the omission of tanwin does not mean the word is prohibited (from taking it), but is due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters (ijtima' al-sakinayn). An example of this is the reading of whoever reads: ﴿Say: He is God, One﴾ and ﴿God, the Eternal Refuge﴾ (al-Ikhlas: 1-2).

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said, and it is common in poetry, and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari recited:

"So that you find me, with the emir, dutiful, and with the spear, a commander, attacking,
When Ghutayf al-Sulami flees."

The apparent meaning of the words ﴿And the Jews say﴾ is that this statement belongs to all of them. It has also been said that it is a word that comes in general terms but whose meaning is specific, because only some of them said it.

Al-Naqqash said: No Jew remains who says it; rather, they have died out. It has also been said that a group of them said this to the Prophet (ﷺ), so the verse came including the reporting of that about the Jews, because the saying of some of them is binding upon all of them.

The words of God Most High: ﴿And the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of God."﴾ They said this when they saw his raising of the dead despite his having no father, and so that became a cause for this statement.

The better view is that it may be said: they made this statement because the Gospel describes him at times as "son of God" and at times as "son of man," as we see in several places in the Gospel. They did not understand that this was for the purpose of honour and dignity, or it did not become clear to them that this was a distortion by their predecessors for some corrupt aim. It has been said: this statement is only from some Christians, not from all of them.

The words of God Most High: ﴿That is their saying with their mouths.﴾ The reference is to what came from them of this false statement.

The meaning of "with their mouths," despite the knowledge that speech occurs only with the mouth, is that since this statement was plain, without clarification and not supported by proof, it was mere assertion with no meaning beneath it, empty, issuing from them like meaningless utterances whose only feature is that they come out of the mouths, not conveying any benefit worth considering. It has been said: the mention of mouths is for emphasis, as in "I wrote with my hand" and "I walked with my foot." From this is His saying: ﴿They write the Scripture with their own hands﴾ (al-Baqarah: 79), and His saying: ﴿Nor a bird that flies with its two wings﴾ (al-An'am: 38).

Some scholars said: God, glorified is He, never mentioned a saying linked with the mention of mouths and tongues except that it was a false saying, such as His saying: ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾ (Al 'Imran: 167), His saying: ﴿A word that comes out of their mouths﴾ (al-Kahf: 5), and His saying: ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾ (al-Fath: 11).

The words of God Most High: ﴿They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them.﴾ Al-Mudahaah means resemblance. It has been said that from this is the Arabic expression "a barren woman" (imra'ah dahya'), who is one who does not menstruate, because she resembles men.

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: whoever says "yudahi'un" is derived from their saying "imra'ah dahya'" is mistaken, because the hamzah in "dahha'a" is original, while in "dahya'" it is an added letter like in "hamra'" (red, feminine), and its root is "yudahi'un" and "imra'ah dahya'."

As for the meaning of their imitation of the saying of those who disbelieved, there are several views among the scholars. The first: they resembled with this statement the idol-worshippers in their saying "al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat are the daughters of God."

The second view: they resembled the statement of disbelievers who say that the angels are the daughters of God.

The third view: they resembled their predecessors who said that Ezra is the son of God and that the Messiah is the son of God.

The words of God Most High: ﴿May God fight them.﴾ This is a supplication against them for destruction, because whoever God fights is destroyed. It has been said: it is an expression of amazement at the abominable nature of their saying. It has also been said: the meaning of "May God fight them" is "May God curse them." From this is the saying of Aban ibn Tha'laba:

"May God fight her; she blames me, though she knows
That I am the one who ruins and sets right for myself."

Al-Naqqash related that the original meaning of "qatalahumu Allah" is supplication, but then it became common in their usage, to the point that they said it to express amazement at good and at evil, while not intending supplication. Al-Asma'i recited:

"O God fight Layla! How she amazes me,
And I tell people that I do not care for her."

﴿How are they turned away?﴾ That is, how are they diverted from the truth to falsehood?

The words of God Most High: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God.﴾ Al-Ahbar is the plural of habr, one who speaks well, and from this is the phrase "a garment adorned" (thawb muhabbar). It has also been said it is the plural of hibr with a kasra on the ha'.

Yunus said: I have only heard it with a kasra on the ha'.

Al-Farra' said: the fatha and the kasra are two dialects.

Ibn al-Sikkit said: al-hibr with a kasra means "the scholar," and al-habr with a fatha means "the learned one."

Al-Ruhban is the plural of rahib, derived from rahbah (awe), and they are the scholars of the Christians, just as al-Ahbar are the scholars of the Jews.

The meaning of the verse is that when they obeyed them in what they commanded and forbade, they were in the position of those who took them as lords, because they obeyed them as lords are obeyed.

The words of God Most High: ﴿And the Messiah, son of Mary.﴾ It is conjoined with "their monks": that is, the Christians took him as a worshipped lord. In this there is an indication that the Jews did not take Ezra as a worshipped lord.

In this verse there is something that restrains whoever has a heart, or who listens attentively while being a witness, from blind imitation (taqlid) in the religion of God, and from giving precedence to what the predecessors say over what is in the Noble Book and the purified Sunnah. The obedience of one who follows a school of law to one whose words he follows and whose path he takes from the scholars of this community, while that contradicts what the texts have brought and what the proofs of God and His evidences have established, and what His Books and Prophets have spoken, is like the Jews' and Christians' taking of rabbis and monks as lords besides God. This is because they did not worship them, but obeyed them, prohibiting what they prohibited and permitting what they permitted. This is the practice of the imitators of this community, and it resembles it more than one egg resembles another egg, or one date resembles another date, or water resembles water. So: O servants of God, and O followers of Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah! What is the matter with you that you have abandoned the Book and the Sunnah to one side, and have turned to men who are like you in worshipping God by them and in His requiring them to act upon what they indicate and convey, and you have acted upon the opinions they brought, which were not founded on the pillar of truth nor supported by the support of religion and the texts of the Book and the Sunnah, while they call out with the most eloquent call and proclaim with the loudest voice what opposes and contradicts that? You have turned deaf ears to the two, and hearts that are sealed, and minds that are sick, and intellects that are broken, and thoughts that are dulled, and impulses that are feeble. You have recited with the tongue of the situation:

"I am only of the tribe of Ghazziyya: if they go astray, I go astray, and if Ghazziyya is guided, I am guided."

So leave aside, may God guide you and me, the books that your dead predecessors wrote for you, and exchange them for the Book of God, your Creator and theirs, your Worshipped One and theirs, and exchange the sayings of those you call your imams, and what they brought you of opinion, for the sayings of your Imam and theirs, your Exemplar and theirs, who is the first Imam, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah (ﷺ):

"Leave every saying in favour of the saying of Muhammad,
For no one who breaks faith in his religion is like one who risks it."

O God, guide of the one who has strayed, director of the one who is lost, clarifier of the path, guide us to the truth, direct us to what is right, and make clear to us the method of guidance.

The words of God Most High: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship one God.﴾ This clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal). That is: they took their rabbis and monks as lords, while the case is that they were only commanded to worship God alone. Or it means: those who took them as lords from among the rabbis and monks were only commanded to do that. So how could they be fit for what they qualified them for, of taking them as lords?

The words of God Most High: ﴿There is no god but He.﴾ This is a second description of "one God." ﴿Glory be to Him above what they associate.﴾ That is, exalted above association in His obedience and worship.

The words of God Most High: ﴿They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths.﴾ This statement includes the mention of another kind of their misguidance and remoteness from the truth, which is what they sought of nullifying the truth with their false sayings, which are merely plain words and false disputations. This is a parable of their condition in attempting to nullify the religion of truth and the prophethood of the Prophet of truth, by the condition of one who wishes to blow upon a great light by which the world has been illuminated and the darkness dispersed, in order to extinguish it and remove its brightness. ﴿But God refuses except to perfect His light﴾: that is, His upright religion. It has been said: how did the exceptive particle "illa" enter upon "yaba" (refuses), when one cannot say "I hated or disliked except Zayd"?

Al-Farra' said: it entered because there is an element of negation in the speech.

Al-Zajjaj said: the Arabs omit with "aba," and the implied meaning is "and God refuses everything except to perfect His light."

'Ali ibn Sulayman said: this was permitted with "aba" because it is a prohibition or refusal, so it resembles negation.

Al-Nahhas said: this is the best view, as the poet said:

"And do I have another mother than her, if I abandon her?
God refuses except that I be a son to her."

The author of al-Kashshaf said: "aba" has been treated as "lam yurid" (did not want), meaning: "and he does not want except to perfect His light."

The words of God Most High: ﴿Though the disbelievers hate it.﴾ This is conjoined to a clause before it that is implied: that is, God refuses except to perfect His light, even if the disbelievers do not hate that, and even if they do hate it.

Then He emphasised this with His saying: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance﴾: that is, with what guides people by way of proofs, miracles, and rulings which God has legislated for His servants, "and the religion of truth", which is Islam, "to make it prevail": that is, to make His Messenger prevail, or the religion of truth to prevail through what it contains of proofs and evidences. This has occurred, and to God is the praise. ﴿Though the polytheists hate it.﴾ The discussion regarding it is like the discussion regarding ﴿Though the disbelievers hate it,﴾ as we have already mentioned.

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Salam ibn Mishkam, Nu'man ibn Awfa, Abu Anas, Shas ibn Qays, and Malik ibn al-Sayf came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: 'How can we follow you when you have abandoned our qibla, and you do not claim that Ezra is the son of God?' So God revealed: ﴿And the Jews say, 'Ezra is the son of God'﴾," the verse.

Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him (Ibn 'Abbas) that he said: "The women of the Children of Israel used to gather at night, pray, withdraw, and mention what God had favoured the Children of Israel with and what He had given them. Then God empowered over them the worst of His creation, Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar), who burned the Torah and destroyed Bayt al-Maqdis. Ezra was then a boy. Ezra said: 'Was this?' So he joined the mountains and wild animals and began to worship there, and would not mix with people. One day he came upon a woman at a grave, weeping. He said: 'O mother, fear God, seek reward and be patient. Do you not know that the path of people is toward death?' She said: 'O Ezra, do you forbid me to weep while you have left the Children of Israel behind and joined the mountains and wild animals?' Then she said: 'I am not a woman, but I am the world. Soon a spring will gush out at your place of prayer, and a tree will grow. Drink from the water of the spring and eat from the fruit of the tree. Two angels will come to you; leave them to do what they wish.' When the next day came, the spring gushed forth and the tree grew. He drank from the water of the spring and ate from the fruit of the tree. Two angels came with them a flask containing light, and they poured into him what was in it. God then inspired him with the Torah, and he came and dictated it to the people. At that point they said: 'Ezra is the son of God.' Exalted is God above that."

Ibn Abi Hatim also related from him (Ibn 'Abbas), mentioning a story in which: 'Uzayr asked God, after God had made the Children of Israel forget the Torah and removed it from their hearts, that He return to him what had been removed from his heart. While he was praying, a light from God, Mighty and Majestic is He, descended and entered his inner self, and what had gone from his inner self of the Torah returned to him. He then called out to his people and said: "O people, God has given me the Torah and returned it to me."

Abu al-Shaykh related from Ka'b, who said: 'Uzayr's supplication to his Lord was that the Torah, as it had been sent down to Moses, be placed in his heart, and God sent it down to him. After that they said: "'Uzayr is the son of God."

Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "There are three things about which I am in doubt: I do not know whether 'Uzayr was a prophet or not; I do not know whether Tubba' (a title of the Himyarite kings of Yemen) was cursed or not." He said: "And I have forgotten the third."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him concerning His words ﴿يُضاهِئُونَ﴾ (yudahi'un, "they imitate"): he said: "They resemble," meaning "they are similar to."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from him concerning His words ﴿قاتَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ (qatalahumu Allah, "may God fight them"): he said: "May God curse them." And everything in the Qur'an that uses qatl (killing) is a curse.

Ibn Sa'd, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, who graded it as hasan (good), Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: "I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was reciting in Surat Bara'a (al-Tawba): ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾. He said: 'As for them, they did not worship them. But when they made something lawful for them, they regarded it as lawful, and when they made something unlawful for them, they regarded it as unlawful.'"

Ahmad and Ibn Jarir also related it.

'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Abu al-Bakhtari, who said: "A man asked Hudhayfa: 'Have you considered His words ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾? Did they worship them?' He said: 'No, but when they made something lawful for them, they regarded it as lawful, and when they made something unlawful for them, they regarded it as unlawful.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Dahhak, who said: "Their rabbis (ahbar, religious scholars of the Jews) are their readers, and their monks (ruhban, ascetics) are their scholars."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Jurayj, who said: "The rabbis are from among the Jews, and the monks are from among the Christians."

Ibn Abi Hatim related the same from al-Suddi.

He also related from al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, who said: "The rabbis are the scholars, and the monks are the worshippers."

(p-569) He also related from al-Suddi concerning His words ﴿They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths﴾, he said: "They want to extinguish Islam with their words."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Dahhak concerning His words ﴿They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths﴾, he said: "They mean: they want Muhammad and his companions to perish."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Qatada concerning the verse, he said: "They are the Jews and the Christians."

Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi concerning ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance﴾, he said: "That is, with monotheism (tawhid), Islam and the Qur'an."

The words of God Most High: ﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of God."﴾ This is a fresh statement made to show the polytheism of the two groups of People of the Book. "Ezra" is the subject (mubtada', the grammatical subject) and "son of God" is its predicate (khabar). Whoever reads it with tanwin has treated it as Arabic. It has also been said that the omission of tanwin does not mean the word is prohibited (from taking it), but is due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters (ijtima' al-sakinayn). An example of this is the reading of whoever reads: ﴿Say: He is God, One﴾ and ﴿God, the Eternal Refuge﴾ (al-Ikhlas: 1-2).

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said, and it is common in poetry, and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari recited:

"So that you find me, with the emir, dutiful, and with the spear, a commander, attacking,
When Ghutayf al-Sulami flees."

Al-Naqqash said: No Jew remains who says it; rather, they have died out. It has also been said that a group of them said this to the Prophet (ﷺ), so the verse came including the reporting of that about the Jews, because the saying of some of them is binding upon all of them.

The words of God Most High: ﴿And the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of God."﴾ They said this when they saw his raising of the dead despite his having no father, and so that became a cause for this statement.

The better view is that it may be said: they made this statement because the Gospel describes him at times as "son of God" and at times as "son of man," as we see in several places in the Gospel. They did not understand that this was for the purpose of honour and dignity, or it did not become clear to them that this was a distortion by their predecessors for some corrupt aim. It has been said: this statement is only from some Christians, not from all of them.

The meaning of "with their mouths," despite the knowledge that speech occurs only with the mouth, is that since this statement was plain, without clarification and not supported by proof, it was mere assertion with no meaning beneath it, empty, issuing from them like meaningless utterances whose only feature is that they come out of the mouths, not conveying any benefit worth considering. It has been said: the mention of mouths is for emphasis, as in "I wrote with my hand" and "I walked with my foot." From this is His saying: ﴿They write the Scripture with their own hands﴾ (al-Baqarah: 79), and His saying: ﴿Nor a bird that flies with its two wings﴾ (al-An'am: 38).

Some scholars said: God, glorified is He, never mentioned a saying linked with the mention of mouths and tongues except that it was a false saying, such as His saying: ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾ (Al 'Imran: 167), His saying: ﴿A word that comes out of their mouths﴾ (al-Kahf: 5), and His saying: ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾ (al-Fath: 11).

The words of God Most High: ﴿They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them.﴾ Al-Mudahaah means resemblance. It has been said that from this is the Arabic expression "a barren woman" (imra'ah dahya'), who is one who does not menstruate, because she resembles men.

As for the meaning of their imitation of the saying of those who disbelieved, there are several views among the scholars. The first: they resembled with this statement the idol-worshippers in their saying "al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat are the daughters of God."

The second view: they resembled the statement of disbelievers who say that the angels are the daughters of God.

The third view: they resembled their predecessors who said that Ezra is the son of God and that the Messiah is the son of God.

The words of God Most High: ﴿May God fight them.﴾ This is a supplication against them for destruction, because whoever God fights is destroyed. It has been said: it is an expression of amazement at the abominable nature of their saying. It has also been said: the meaning of "May God fight them" is "May God curse them." From this is the saying of Aban ibn Tha'laba:

"May God fight her; she blames me, though she knows
That I am the one who ruins and sets right for myself."

Al-Naqqash related that the original meaning of "qatalahumu Allah" is supplication, but then it became common in their usage, to the point that they said it to express amazement at good and at evil, while not intending supplication. Al-Asma'i recited:

"O God fight Layla! How she amazes me,
And I tell people that I do not care for her."

﴿How are they turned away?﴾ That is, how are they diverted from the truth to falsehood?

The words of God Most High: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God.﴾ Al-Ahbar is the plural of habr, one who speaks well, and from this is the phrase "a garment adorned" (thawb muhabbar). It has also been said it is the plural of hibr with a kasra on the ha'.

Yunus said: I have only heard it with a kasra on the ha'.

Al-Farra' said: the fatha and the kasra are two dialects.

Ibn al-Sikkit said: al-hibr with a kasra means "the scholar," and al-habr with a fatha means "the learned one."

Al-Ruhban is the plural of rahib, derived from rahbah (awe), and they are the scholars of the Christians, just as al-Ahbar are the scholars of the Jews.

The meaning of the verse is that when they obeyed them in what they commanded and forbade, they were in the position of those who took them as lords, because they obeyed them as lords are obeyed.

The words of God Most High: ﴿And the Messiah, son of Mary.﴾ It is conjoined with "their monks": that is, the Christians took him as a worshipped lord. In this there is an indication that the Jews did not take Ezra as a worshipped lord.

In this verse there is something that restrains whoever has a heart, or who listens attentively while being a witness, from blind imitation (taqlid) in the religion of God, and from giving precedence to what the predecessors say over what is in the Noble Book and the purified Sunnah. The obedience of one who follows a school of law to one whose words he follows and whose path he takes from the scholars of this community, while that contradicts what the texts have brought and what the proofs of God and His evidences have established, and what His Books and Prophets have spoken, is like the Jews' and Christians' taking of rabbis and monks as lords besides God. This is because they did not worship them, but obeyed them, prohibiting what they prohibited and permitting what they permitted. This is the practice of the imitators of this community, and it resembles it more than one egg resembles another egg, or one date resembles another date, or water resembles water. So: O servants of God, and O followers of Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah! What is the matter with you that you have abandoned the Book and the Sunnah to one side, and have turned to men who are like you in worshipping God by them and in His requiring them to act upon what they indicate and convey, and you have acted upon the opinions they brought, which were not founded on the pillar of truth nor supported by the support of religion and the texts of the Book and the Sunnah, while they call out with the most eloquent call and proclaim with the loudest voice what opposes and contradicts that? You have turned deaf ears to the two, and hearts that are sealed, and minds that are sick, and intellects that are broken, and thoughts that are dulled, and impulses that are feeble. You have recited with the tongue of the situation:

"I am only of the tribe of Ghazziyya: if they go astray, I go astray, and if Ghazziyya is guided, I am guided."

So leave aside, may God guide you and me, the books that your dead predecessors wrote for you, and exchange them for the Book of God, your Creator and theirs, your Worshipped One and theirs, and exchange the sayings of those you call your imams, and what they brought you of opinion, for the sayings of your Imam and theirs, your Exemplar and theirs, who is the first Imam, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah (ﷺ):

"Leave every saying in favour of the saying of Muhammad,
For no one who breaks faith in his religion is like one who risks it."

O God, guide of the one who has strayed, director of the one who is lost, clarifier of the path, guide us to the truth, direct us to what is right, and make clear to us the method of guidance.

The words of God Most High: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship one God.﴾ This clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal). That is: they took their rabbis and monks as lords, while the case is that they were only commanded to worship God alone. Or it means: those who took them as lords from among the rabbis and monks were only commanded to do that. So how could they be fit for what they qualified them for, of taking them as lords?

The words of God Most High: ﴿There is no god but He.﴾ This is a second description of "one God." ﴿Glory be to Him above what they associate.﴾ That is, exalted above association in His obedience and worship.

The words of God Most High: ﴿They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths.﴾ This statement includes the mention of another kind of their misguidance and remoteness from the truth, which is what they sought of nullifying the truth with their false sayings, which are merely plain words and false disputations. This is a parable of their condition in attempting to nullify the religion of truth and the prophethood of the Prophet of truth, by the condition of one who wishes to blow upon a great light by which the world has been illuminated and the darkness dispersed, in order to extinguish it and remove its brightness. ﴿But God refuses except to perfect His light﴾: that is, His upright religion. It has been said: how did the exceptive particle "illa" enter upon "yaba" (refuses), when one cannot say "I hated or disliked except Zayd"?

Al-Farra' said: it entered because there is an element of negation in the speech.

Al-Zajjaj said: the Arabs omit with "aba," and the implied meaning is "and God refuses everything except to perfect His light."

'Ali ibn Sulayman said: this was permitted with "aba" because it is a prohibition or refusal, so it resembles negation.

Al-Nahhas said: this is the best view, as the poet said:

"And do I have another mother than her, if I abandon her?
God refuses except that I be a son to her."

The author of al-Kashshaf said: "aba" has been treated as "lam yurid" (did not want), meaning: "and he does not want except to perfect His light."

The words of God Most High: ﴿Though the disbelievers hate it.﴾ This is conjoined to a clause before it that is implied: that is, God refuses except to perfect His light, even if the disbelievers do not hate that, and even if they do hate it.

Then He emphasised this with His saying: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance﴾: that is, with what guides people by way of proofs, miracles, and rulings which God has legislated for His servants, "and the religion of truth", which is Islam, "to make it prevail": that is, to make His Messenger prevail, or the religion of truth to prevail through what it contains of proofs and evidences. This has occurred, and to God is the praise. ﴿Though the polytheists hate it.﴾ The discussion regarding it is like the discussion regarding ﴿Though the disbelievers hate it,﴾ as we have already mentioned.

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Salam ibn Mishkam, Nu'man ibn Awfa, Abu Anas, Shas ibn Qays, and Malik ibn al-Sayf came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: 'How can we follow you when you have abandoned our qibla, and you do not claim that Ezra is the son of God?' So God revealed: ﴿And the Jews say, 'Ezra is the son of God'﴾," the verse.

Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him (Ibn 'Abbas) that he said: "The women of the Children of Israel used to gather at night, pray, withdraw, and mention what God had favoured the Children of Israel with and what He had given them. Then God empowered over them the worst of His creation, Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar), who burned the Torah and destroyed Bayt al-Maqdis. Ezra was then a boy. Ezra said: 'Was this?' So he joined the mountains and wild animals and began to worship there, and would not mix with people. One day he came upon a woman at a grave, weeping. He said: 'O mother, fear God, seek reward and be patient. Do you not know that the path of people is toward death?' She said: 'O Ezra, do you forbid me to weep while you have left the Children of Israel behind and joined the mountains and wild animals?' Then she said: 'I am not a woman, but I am the world. Soon a spring will gush out at your place of prayer, and a tree will grow. Drink from the water of the spring and eat from the fruit of the tree. Two angels will come to you; leave them to do what they wish.' When the next day came, the spring gushed forth and the tree grew. He drank from the water of the spring and ate from the fruit of the tree. Two angels came with them a flask containing light, and they poured into him what was in it. God then inspired him with the Torah, and he came and dictated it to the people. At that point they said: 'Ezra is the son of God.' Exalted is God above that."

Ibn Abi Hatim also related from him (Ibn 'Abbas), mentioning a story in which: 'Uzayr asked God, after God had made the Children of Israel forget the Torah and removed it from their hearts, that He return to him what had been removed from his heart. While he was praying, a light from God, Mighty and Majestic is He, descended and entered his inner self, and what had gone from his inner self of the Torah returned to him. He then called out to his people and said: "O people, God has given me the Torah and returned it to me."

Abu al-Shaykh related from Ka'b, who said: 'Uzayr's supplication to his Lord was that the Torah, as it had been sent down to Moses, be placed in his heart, and God sent it down to him. After that they said: "'Uzayr is the son of God."

Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "There are three things about which I am in doubt: I do not know whether 'Uzayr was a prophet or not; I do not know whether Tubba' (a title of the Himyarite kings of Yemen) was cursed or not." He said: "And I have forgotten the third."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him concerning His words ﴿يُضاهِئُونَ﴾ (yudahi'un, "they imitate"): he said: "They resemble," meaning "they are similar to."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from him concerning His words ﴿قاتَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ (qatalahumu Allah, "may God fight them"): he said: "May God curse them." And everything in the Qur'an that uses qatl (killing) is a curse.

Ibn Sa'd, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, who graded it as hasan (good), Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: "I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was reciting in Surat Bara'a (al-Tawba): ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾. He said: 'As for them, they did not worship them. But when they made something lawful for them, they regarded it as lawful, and when they made something unlawful for them, they regarded it as unlawful.'"

Ahmad and Ibn Jarir also related it.

'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Abu al-Bakhtari, who said: "A man asked Hudhayfa: 'Have you considered His words ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾? Did they worship them?' He said: 'No, but when they made something lawful for them, they regarded it as lawful, and when they made something unlawful for them, they regarded it as unlawful.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Dahhak, who said: "Their rabbis (ahbar, religious scholars of the Jews) are their readers, and their monks (ruhban, ascetics) are their scholars."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Jurayj, who said: "The rabbis are from among the Jews, and the monks are from among the Christians."

Ibn Abi Hatim related the same from al-Suddi.

He also related from al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, who said: "The rabbis are the scholars, and the monks are the worshippers."

(p-569) He also related from al-Suddi concerning His words ﴿They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths﴾, he said: "They want to extinguish Islam with their words."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Dahhak concerning His words ﴿They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths﴾, he said: "They mean: they want Muhammad and his companions to perish."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Qatada concerning the verse, he said: "They are the Jews and the Christians."

Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi concerning ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance﴾, he said: "That is, with monotheism (tawhid), Islam and the Qur'an."

The words of God Most High: ﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of God."﴾ This is a fresh statement made to show the polytheism of the two groups of People of the Book. "Ezra" is the subject (mubtada', the grammatical subject) and "son of God" is its predicate (khabar). 'Asim and al-Kisa'i read "Ezra" with tanwin (nunation), while the rest read it without tanwin, because the word combines 'ujma (non-Arabic origin) and 'alamiyya (proper-name status).

Whoever reads it with tanwin has treated it as Arabic. It has also been said that the omission of tanwin does not mean the word is prohibited (from taking it), but is due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters (ijtima' al-sakinayn). An example of this is the reading of whoever reads: ﴿Say: He is God, One﴾ and ﴿God, the Eternal Refuge﴾ (al-Ikhlas: 1-2).

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said, and it is common in poetry, and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari recited:

"So that you find me, with the emir, dutiful, and with the spear, a commander, attacking,
When Ghutayf al-Sulami flees."

The apparent meaning of the words ﴿And the Jews say﴾ is that this statement belongs to all of them. It has also been said that it is a word that comes in general terms but whose meaning is specific, because only some of them said it.

Al-Naqqash said: No Jew remains who says it; rather, they have died out. It has also been said that a group of them said this to the Prophet (ﷺ), so the verse came including the reporting of that about the Jews, because the saying of some of them is binding upon all of them.

The words of God Most High: ﴿And the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of God."﴾ They said this when they saw his raising of the dead despite his having no father, and so that became a cause for this statement.

The better view is that it may be said: they made this statement because the Gospel describes him at times as "son of God" and at times as "son of man," as we see in several places in the Gospel. They did not understand that this was for the purpose of honour and dignity, or it did not become clear to them that this was a distortion by their predecessors for some corrupt aim. It has been said: this statement is only from some Christians, not from all of them.

The words of God Most High: ﴿That is their saying with their mouths.﴾ The reference is to what came from them of this false statement.

The meaning of "with their mouths," despite the knowledge that speech occurs only with the mouth, is that since this statement was plain, without clarification and not supported by proof, it was mere assertion with no meaning beneath it, empty, issuing from them like meaningless utterances whose only feature is that they come out of the mouths, not conveying any benefit worth considering. It has been said: the mention of mouths is for emphasis, as in "I wrote with my hand" and "I walked with my foot." From this is His saying: ﴿They write the Scripture with their own hands﴾ (al-Baqarah: 79), and His saying: ﴿Nor a bird that flies with its two wings﴾ (al-An'am: 38).

Some scholars said: God, glorified is He, never mentioned a saying linked with the mention of mouths and tongues except that it was a false saying, such as His saying: ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾ (Al 'Imran: 167), His saying: ﴿A word that comes out of their mouths﴾ (al-Kahf: 5), and His saying: ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾ (al-Fath: 11).

The words of God Most High: ﴿They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them.﴾ Al-Mudahaah means resemblance. It has been said that from this is the Arabic expression "a barren woman" (imra'ah dahya'), who is one who does not menstruate, because she resembles men.

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: whoever says "yudahi'un" is derived from their saying "imra'ah dahya'" is mistaken, because the hamzah in "dahha'a" is original, while in "dahya'" it is an added letter like in "hamra'" (red, feminine), and its root is "yudahi'un" and "imra'ah dahya'."

As for the meaning of their imitation of the saying of those who disbelieved, there are several views among the scholars. The first: they resembled with this statement the idol-worshippers in their saying "al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat are the daughters of God."

The second view: they resembled the statement of disbelievers who say that the angels are the daughters of God.

The third view: they resembled their predecessors who said that Ezra is the son of God and that the Messiah is the son of God.

The words of God Most High: ﴿May God fight them.﴾ This is a supplication against them for destruction, because whoever God fights is destroyed. It has been said: it is an expression of amazement at the abominable nature of their saying. It has also been said: the meaning of "May God fight them" is "May God curse them." From this is the saying of Aban ibn Tha'laba:

"May God fight her; she blames me, though she knows
That I am the one who ruins and sets right for myself."

Al-Naqqash related that the original meaning of "qatalahumu Allah" is supplication, but then it became common in their usage, to the point that they said it to express amazement at good and at evil, while not intending supplication. Al-Asma'i recited:

"O God fight Layla! How she amazes me,
And I tell people that I do not care for her."

﴿How are they turned away?﴾ That is, how are they diverted from the truth to falsehood?

The words of God Most High: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God.﴾ Al-Ahbar is the plural of habr, one who speaks well, and from this is the phrase "a garment adorned" (thawb muhabbar). It has also been said it is the plural of hibr with a kasra on the ha'.

Yunus said: I have only heard it with a kasra on the ha'.

Al-Farra' said: the fatha and the kasra are two dialects.

Ibn al-Sikkit said: al-hibr with a kasra means "the scholar," and al-habr with a fatha means "the learned one."

Al-Ruhban is the plural of rahib, derived from rahbah (awe), and they are the scholars of the Christians, just as al-Ahbar are the scholars of the Jews.

The meaning of the verse is that when they obeyed them in what they commanded and forbade, they were in the position of those who took them as lords, because they obeyed them as lords are obeyed.

The words of God Most High: ﴿And the Messiah, son of Mary.﴾ It is conjoined with "their monks": that is, the Christians took him as a worshipped lord. In this there is an indication that the Jews did not take Ezra as a worshipped lord.

This is because they did not worship them, but obeyed them, prohibiting what they prohibited and permitting what they permitted. This is the practice of the imitators of this community, and it resembles it more than one egg resembles another egg, or one date resembles another date, or water resembles water. So: O servants of God, and O followers of Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah! What is the matter with you that you have abandoned the Book and the Sunnah to one side, and have turned to men who are like you in worshipping God by them and in His requiring them to act upon what they indicate and convey, and you have acted upon the opinions they brought, which were not founded on the pillar of truth nor supported by the support of religion and the texts of the Book and the Sunnah, while they call out with the most eloquent call and proclaim with the loudest voice what opposes and contradicts that? You have turned deaf ears to the two, and hearts that are sealed, and minds that are sick, and intellects that are broken, and thoughts that are dulled, and impulses that are feeble. So leave aside, may God guide you and me, the books that your dead predecessors wrote for you, and exchange them for the Book of God, your Creator and theirs, your Worshipped One and theirs, and exchange the sayings of those you call your imams, and what they brought you of opinion, for the sayings of your Imam and theirs, your Exemplar and theirs, who is the first Imam, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah (ﷺ):

O God, guide of the one who has strayed, director of the one who is lost, clarifier of the path, guide us to the truth, direct us to what is right, and make clear to us the method of guidance.

That is: they took their rabbis and monks as lords, while the case is that they were only commanded to worship God alone. Or it means: those who took them as lords from among the rabbis and monks were only commanded to do that. So how could they be fit for what they qualified them for, of taking them as lords?

While he was praying, a light from God, Mighty and Majestic is He, descended and entered his inner self, and what had gone from his inner self of the Torah returned to him. He said: "And I have forgotten the third."
