He said: 'As for them, they did not worship them. But when they made something lawful for them, they regarded it as lawful, and when they made something unlawful for them, they regarded it as unlawful.'"

Ahmad and Ibn Jarir also related it.

'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Abu al-Bakhtari, who said: "A man asked Hudhayfa: 'Have you considered His words ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾? Did they worship them?' He said: 'No, but when they made something lawful for them, they regarded it as lawful, and when they made something unlawful for them, they regarded it as unlawful.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Dahhak, who said: "Their rabbis (ahbar, religious scholars of the Jews) are their readers, and their monks (ruhban, ascetics) are their scholars."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Jurayj, who said: "The rabbis are from among the Jews, and the monks are from among the Christians."

Ibn Abi Hatim related the same from al-Suddi.

He also related from al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, who said: "The rabbis are the scholars, and the monks are the worshippers."

(p-569) He also related from al-Suddi concerning His words ﴿They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths﴾, he said: "They want to extinguish Islam with their words."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Dahhak concerning His words ﴿They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths﴾, he said: "They mean: they want Muhammad and his companions to perish."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Qatada concerning the verse, he said: "They are the Jews and the Christians."

Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi concerning ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance﴾, he said: "That is, with monotheism (tawhid), Islam and the Qur'an."

The words of God Most High: ﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of God."﴾ This is a fresh statement made to show the polytheism of the two groups of People of the Book. "Ezra" is the subject (mubtada', the grammatical subject) and "son of God" is its predicate (khabar). 'Asim and al-Kisa'i read "Ezra" with tanwin (nunation), while the rest read it without tanwin, because the word combines 'ujma (non-Arabic origin) and 'alamiyya (proper-name status).

Whoever reads it with tanwin has treated it as Arabic. It has also been said that the omission of tanwin does not mean the word is prohibited (from taking it), but is due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters (ijtima' al-sakinayn). An example of this is the reading of whoever reads: ﴿Say: He is God, One﴾ and ﴿God, the Eternal Refuge﴾ (al-Ikhlas: 1-2).

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said, and it is common in poetry, and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari recited:

"So that you find me, with the emir, dutiful, and with the spear, a commander, attacking,
When Ghutayf al-Sulami flees."

The apparent meaning of the words ﴿And the Jews say﴾ is that this statement belongs to all of them. It has also been said that it is a word that comes in general terms but whose meaning is specific, because only some of them said it.

Al-Naqqash said: No Jew remains who says it; rather, they have died out. It has also been said that a group of them said this to the Prophet (ﷺ), so the verse came including the reporting of that about the Jews, because the saying of some of them is binding upon all of them.

The words of God Most High: ﴿And the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of God."﴾ They said this when they saw his raising of the dead despite his having no father, and so that became a cause for this statement.

The better view is that it may be said: they made this statement because the Gospel describes him at times as "son of God" and at times as "son of man," as we see in several places in the Gospel. They did not understand that this was for the purpose of honour and dignity, or it did not become clear to them that this was a distortion by their predecessors for some corrupt aim. It has been said: this statement is only from some Christians, not from all of them.

The words of God Most High: ﴿That is their saying with their mouths.﴾ The reference is to what came from them of this false statement.

The meaning of "with their mouths," despite the knowledge that speech occurs only with the mouth, is that since this statement was plain, without clarification and not supported by proof, it was mere assertion with no meaning beneath it, empty, issuing from them like meaningless utterances whose only feature is that they come out of the mouths, not conveying any benefit worth considering. It has been said: the mention of mouths is for emphasis, as in "I wrote with my hand" and "I walked with my foot." From this is His saying: ﴿They write the Scripture with their own hands﴾ (al-Baqarah: 79), and His saying: ﴿Nor a bird that flies with its two wings﴾ (al-An'am: 38).

Some scholars said: God, glorified is He, never mentioned a saying linked with the mention of mouths and tongues except that it was a false saying, such as His saying: ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾ (Al 'Imran: 167), His saying: ﴿A word that comes out of their mouths﴾ (al-Kahf: 5), and His saying: ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾ (al-Fath: 11).

The words of God Most High: ﴿They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them.﴾ Al-Mudahaah means resemblance. It has been said that from this is the Arabic expression "a barren woman" (imra'ah dahya'), who is one who does not menstruate, because she resembles men.

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: whoever says "yudahi'un" is derived from their saying "imra'ah dahya'" is mistaken, because the hamzah in "dahha'a" is original, while in "dahya'" it is an added letter like in "hamra'" (red, feminine), and its root is "yudahi'un" and "imra'ah dahya'."

As for the meaning of their imitation of the saying of those who disbelieved, there are several views among the scholars. The first: they resembled with this statement the idol-worshippers in their saying "al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat are the daughters of God."

The second view: they resembled the statement of disbelievers who say that the angels are the daughters of God.

The third view: they resembled their predecessors who said that Ezra is the son of God and that the Messiah is the son of God.

The words of God Most High: ﴿May God fight them.﴾ This is a supplication against them for destruction, because whoever God fights is destroyed. It has been said: it is an expression of amazement at the abominable nature of their saying. It has also been said: the meaning of "May God fight them" is "May God curse them." From this is the saying of Aban ibn Tha'laba:

"May God fight her; she blames me, though she knows
That I am the one who ruins and sets right for myself."

Al-Naqqash related that the original meaning of "qatalahumu Allah" is supplication, but then it became common in their usage, to the point that they said it to express amazement at good and at evil, while not intending supplication. Al-Asma'i recited:

"O God fight Layla! How she amazes me,
And I tell people that I do not care for her."

﴿How are they turned away?﴾ That is, how are they diverted from the truth to falsehood?

The words of God Most High: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God.﴾ Al-Ahbar is the plural of habr, one who speaks well, and from this is the phrase "a garment adorned" (thawb muhabbar). It has also been said it is the plural of hibr with a kasra on the ha'.

Yunus said: I have only heard it with a kasra on the ha'.

Al-Farra' said: the fatha and the kasra are two dialects.

Ibn al-Sikkit said: al-hibr with a kasra means "the scholar," and al-habr with a fatha means "the learned one."

Al-Ruhban is the plural of rahib, derived from rahbah (awe), and they are the scholars of the Christians, just as al-Ahbar are the scholars of the Jews.

The meaning of the verse is that when they obeyed them in what they commanded and forbade, they were in the position of those who took them as lords, because they obeyed them as lords are obeyed.

The words of God Most High: ﴿And the Messiah, son of Mary.﴾ It is conjoined with "their monks": that is, the Christians took him as a worshipped lord. In this there is an indication that the Jews did not take Ezra as a worshipped lord.

In this verse there is something that restrains whoever has a heart, or who listens attentively while being a witness, from blind imitation (taqlid) in the religion of God, and from giving precedence to what the predecessors say over what is in the Noble Book and the purified Sunnah. The obedience of one who follows a school of law to one whose words he follows and whose path he takes from the scholars of this community, while that contradicts what the texts have brought and what the proofs of God and His evidences have established, and what His Books and Prophets have spoken, is like the Jews' and Christians' taking of rabbis and monks as lords besides God. This is because they did not worship them, but obeyed them, prohibiting what they prohibited and permitting what they permitted. This is the practice of the imitators of this community, and it resembles it more than one egg resembles another egg, or one date resembles another date, or water resembles water. So: O servants of God, and O followers of Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah! What is the matter with you that you have abandoned the Book and the Sunnah to one side, and have turned to men who are like you in worshipping God by them and in His requiring them to act upon what they indicate and convey, and you have acted upon the opinions they brought, which were not founded on the pillar of truth nor supported by the support of religion and the texts of the Book and the Sunnah, while they call out with the most eloquent call and proclaim with the loudest voice what opposes and contradicts that? You have turned deaf ears to the two, and hearts that are sealed, and minds that are sick, and intellects that are broken, and thoughts that are dulled, and impulses that are feeble. You have recited with the tongue of the situation:

"I am only of the tribe of Ghazziyya: if they go astray, I go astray, and if Ghazziyya is guided, I am guided."

So leave aside, may God guide you and me, the books that your dead predecessors wrote for you, and exchange them for the Book of God, your Creator and theirs, your Worshipped One and theirs, and exchange the sayings of those you call your imams, and what they brought you of opinion, for the sayings of your Imam and theirs, your Exemplar and theirs, who is the first Imam, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah (ﷺ):

"Leave every saying in favour of the saying of Muhammad,
For no one who breaks faith in his religion is like one who risks it."

O God, guide of the one who has strayed, director of the one who is lost, clarifier of the path, guide us to the truth, direct us to what is right, and make clear to us the method of guidance.

The words of God Most High: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship one God.﴾ This clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal). That is: they took their rabbis and monks as lords, while the case is that they were only commanded to worship God alone. Or it means: those who took them as lords from among the rabbis and monks were only commanded to do that. So how could they be fit for what they qualified them for, of taking them as lords?

The words of God Most High: ﴿There is no god but He.﴾ This is a second description of "one God." ﴿Glory be to Him above what they associate.﴾ That is, exalted above association in His obedience and worship.

The words of God Most High: ﴿They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths.﴾ This statement includes the mention of another kind of their misguidance and remoteness from the truth, which is what they sought of nullifying the truth with their false sayings, which are merely plain words and false disputations. This is a parable of their condition in attempting to nullify the religion of truth and the prophethood of the Prophet of truth, by the condition of one who wishes to blow upon a great light by which the world has been illuminated and the darkness dispersed, in order to extinguish it and remove its brightness. ﴿But God refuses except to perfect His light﴾: that is, His upright religion. It has been said: how did the exceptive particle "illa" enter upon "yaba" (refuses), when one cannot say "I hated or disliked except Zayd"?

Al-Farra' said: it entered because there is an element of negation in the speech.

Al-Zajjaj said: the Arabs omit with "aba," and the implied meaning is "and God refuses everything except to perfect His light."

'Ali ibn Sulayman said: this was permitted with "aba" because it is a prohibition or refusal, so it resembles negation.

Al-Nahhas said: this is the best view, as the poet said:

"And do I have another mother than her, if I abandon her?
God refuses except that I be a son to her."

The author of al-Kashshaf said: "aba" has been treated as "lam yurid" (did not want), meaning: "and he does not want except to perfect His light."

The words of God Most High: ﴿Though the disbelievers hate it.﴾ This is conjoined to a clause before it that is implied: that is, God refuses except to perfect His light, even if the disbelievers do not hate that, and even if they do hate it.

Then He emphasised this with His saying: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance﴾: that is, with what guides people by way of proofs, miracles, and rulings which God has legislated for His servants, "and the religion of truth", which is Islam, "to make it prevail": that is, to make His Messenger prevail, or the religion of truth to prevail through what it contains of proofs and evidences. This has occurred, and to God is the praise. ﴿Though the polytheists hate it.﴾ The discussion regarding it is like the discussion regarding ﴿Though the disbelievers hate it,﴾ as we have already mentioned.

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Salam ibn Mishkam, Nu'man ibn Awfa, Abu Anas, Shas ibn Qays, and Malik ibn al-Sayf came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: 'How can we follow you when you have abandoned our qibla, and you do not claim that Ezra is the son of God?' So God revealed: ﴿And the Jews say, 'Ezra is the son of God'﴾," the verse.

Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him (Ibn 'Abbas) that he said: "The women of the Children of Israel used to gather at night, pray, withdraw, and mention what God had favoured the Children of Israel with and what He had given them. Then God empowered over them the worst of His creation, Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar), who burned the Torah and destroyed Bayt al-Maqdis. Ezra was then a boy. Ezra said: 'Was this?' So he joined the mountains and wild animals and began to worship there, and would not mix with people. One day he came upon a woman at a grave, weeping. He said: 'O mother, fear God, seek reward and be patient. Do you not know that the path of people is toward death?' She said: 'O Ezra, do you forbid me to weep while you have left the Children of Israel behind and joined the mountains and wild animals?' Then she said: 'I am not a woman, but I am the world. Soon a spring will gush out at your place of prayer, and a tree will grow. Drink from the water of the spring and eat from the fruit of the tree. Two angels will come to you; leave them to do what they wish.' When the next day came, the spring gushed forth and the tree grew. He drank from the water of the spring and ate from the fruit of the tree. Two angels came with them a flask containing light, and they poured into him what was in it. God then inspired him with the Torah, and he came and dictated it to the people. At that point they said: 'Ezra is the son of God.' Exalted is God above that."

Ibn Abi Hatim also related from him (Ibn 'Abbas), mentioning a story in which: 'Uzayr asked God, after God had made the Children of Israel forget the Torah and removed it from their hearts, that He return to him what had been removed from his heart. While he was praying, a light from God, Mighty and Majestic is He, descended and entered his inner self, and what had gone from his inner self of the Torah returned to him. He then called out to his people and said: "O people, God has given me the Torah and returned it to me."

Abu al-Shaykh related from Ka'b, who said: 'Uzayr's supplication to his Lord was that the Torah, as it had been sent down to Moses, be placed in his heart, and God sent it down to him. After that they said: "'Uzayr is the son of God."

Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "There are three things about which I am in doubt: I do not know whether 'Uzayr was a prophet or not; I do not know whether Tubba' (a title of the Himyarite kings of Yemen) was cursed or not." He said: "And I have forgotten the third."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him concerning His words ﴿يُضاهِئُونَ﴾ (yudahi'un, "they imitate"): he said: "They resemble," meaning "they are similar to."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from him concerning His words ﴿قاتَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ (qatalahumu Allah, "may God fight them"): he said: "May God curse them." And everything in the Qur'an that uses qatl (killing) is a curse.

Ibn Sa'd, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, who graded it as hasan (good), Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: "I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was reciting in Surat Bara'a (al-Tawba): ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾. He said: 'As for them, they did not worship them. But when they made something lawful for them, they regarded it as lawful, and when they made something unlawful for them, they regarded it as unlawful.'"

Ahmad and Ibn Jarir also related it.

'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Abu al-Bakhtari, who said: "A man asked Hudhayfa: 'Have you considered His words ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾? Did they worship them?' He said: 'No, but when they made something lawful for them, they regarded it as lawful, and when they made something unlawful for them, they regarded it as unlawful.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Dahhak, who said: "Their rabbis (ahbar, religious scholars of the Jews) are their readers, and their monks (ruhban, ascetics) are their scholars."

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Jurayj, who said: "The rabbis are from among the Jews, and the monks are from among the Christians."

Ibn Abi Hatim related the same from al-Suddi.

He also related from al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, who said: "The rabbis are the scholars, and the monks are the worshippers."

(p-569) He also related from al-Suddi concerning His words ﴿They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths﴾, he said: "They want to extinguish Islam with their words."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Dahhak concerning His words ﴿They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths﴾, he said: "They mean: they want Muhammad and his companions to perish."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Qatada concerning the verse, he said: "They are the Jews and the Christians."

Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Suddi concerning ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance﴾, he said: "That is, with monotheism (tawhid), Islam and the Qur'an."

When He - glory be to Him - finished mentioning the condition of the followers of the rabbis and monks, who took them as lords, He mentioned the condition of those who were followed, saying: ﴿Indeed, many of the rabbis...﴾ to the end of the verse. The meaning of their "devouring people's wealth falsely" is that they take it by illegitimate means, such as bribery. He affirmed this of the many among them, because some of them were not involved in it, but remained upon what their religion required, without distortion, alteration, or inclination toward the trash of this world. Many scholars of Islam have followed these rabbis and monks, in number beyond counting in every age, and to God is the help sought.

﴿And who bar from the way of God﴾: that is, from the path to Him, which is the religion of Islam; or from what was true in their law before its abrogation (naskh), through their devouring people's wealth falsely.

His saying: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾. It is said that they are the rabbis and monks previously mentioned, and that they used to do this. It is also said that they are those Muslims who do this. The better view is to take the verse in the general sense of its wording, for it is broader than that. The root meaning of *kanz* (hoarding) in the language is gathering and collecting, and it is not restricted to gold and silver.

Ibn Jarir said: *kanz* is every thing gathered, one part upon another, whether in the belly of the earth or upon its surface. End of quote.

From this comes *naqatun kinaz*, meaning a she-camel of firm flesh, and *iktanaza al-shay'*, meaning the thing gathered together.

The scholars differed concerning wealth whose zakat has been paid: is it called a hoard or not? Some said it is a hoard; others said it is not a hoard.

Among those who held the first view was Abu Dharr, who restricted it to what exceeds need.

Among those who held the second view were Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Jabir, Abu Hurayrah, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, and others. This is the truth, because of the evidences that will come, which clearly state that wealth whose zakat has been paid is not a hoard.

His saying: ﴿And do not spend it in the way of God﴾.

Scholars differed about the reason the pronoun is singular when the things mentioned before it are two, namely gold and silver. Ibn al-Anbari said: it intends the more general and more prevalent, which is silver. He said: a similar example is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is a great burden﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:45), where the pronoun returns to prayer because it is more general. A similar example is His saying: ﴿But when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush to it﴾ (al-Jumu'ah 62:11), where the pronoun returns to trade because it is the more important. It is also said that the pronoun refers to gold and silver, the second being joined to the first, and the Arabs make gold feminine and masculine. It is also said that the pronoun refers to the hoards indicated by His saying "they hoard." It is also said that it refers to the wealth, or to zakat. It is also said that he suffices with the pronoun of one of them instead of the pronoun of the other, with the meaning understood, and this is common in the speech of the Arabs. Sibawayh recited:

*We are content with what we have, and you are content with what you have, though opinions differ.*

He did not say "contented" in the plural. A similar example is the words of another:

*He threw me with a matter from which I and my father were innocent, and from the sake of hunger he threw me.*

He did not say "two innocent." A similar example is the words of Hassan:

*Indeed the bloom of youth and the hair, when they have not been tempered, were madness.*

He did not say "tempered" in the dual. It is also said that the singular pronoun is by way of going to the meaning rather than the wording, because each of gold and silver is a complete category and a great quantity, dinars and dirhams. This is like His saying: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾ (al-Hujurat 49:9). The gold and silver were singled out for mention rather than the rest of the wealth because they are the prices of things and what is most commonly hoarded, although other things have the same ruling as them regarding the prohibition of hoarding.

His saying: ﴿So give them good tidings of a painful punishment﴾. This is the predicate of the relative clause, and it is in the mode of mockery toward them, as in the words:

*Their greeting among them is a painful striking.*

It is also said that good tidings is the news that changes the color of the skin because of its effect on the heart, whether it is in joy or in grief.

The meaning of ﴿On the Day it will be heated in the fire of Hell﴾ is that the fire will be kindled upon them, and it is of intense heat and fierceness. Had He said "On the Day they will be heated," meaning the hoards, this meaning would not be given. So He made the heating belong to the fire as an exaggeration, then He omitted the fire and attributed the verb to the preposition phrase, as you say: "I raised the matter to the emir," and if you do not mention the matter you say: "It was raised to the emir."

Ibn Amir read *tuhma* with a feminine (second-person) prefix.

Abu Haywah read *fayukwa* with a masculine (third-person) prefix.

He singled out the foreheads, sides, and backs because the pain of their branding is more severe, owing to the noble organs within them. It is also said: so that the branding is on the four directions, from the front, the back, the right, and the left. It is also said: because beauty is in the face, and strength in the back and the sides, and a person seeks wealth for beauty and strength. It is also said other things, which do not avoid being strained.

His saying: ﴿This is what you hoarded for yourselves﴾. That is, it will be said to them: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves," that is, you hoarded it so that you might benefit from it, so this is its benefit, in the manner of mockery and reproach. ﴿So taste what you used to hoard﴾. The *ma* is either verbal (the infinitive) or relative: that is, taste its evil, the wickedness of its outcome, the ugliness of its consequence, and the ill of its fruit.

Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, many of the rabbis and monks﴾, meaning the scholars of the Jews and Christians, ﴿devour people's wealth falsely﴾: the falsehood is books they wrote that God did not send down, and with them they devoured people's wealth. This is the saying of God, exalted: ﴿So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands, then say, "This is from God"﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:79).

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾, that he said: these are the ones who do not pay zakat from their wealth. Every wealth whose zakat is not paid, whether it is on the surface of the earth or in its belly, is a hoard, and every wealth whose zakat is paid is not a hoard, whether it is on the surface of the earth or in its belly.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh related it from him by another route.

Malik, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh related something similar from Ibn Umar.

Ibn Mardawayh related something similar from him, raised (marfu') to the Prophet.

Ibn Adi and al-Khatib related something similar from Jabir, also raised.

Ibn Abi Shaybah related it from him as a statement of a Companion (mawquf).

Ahmad in al-Zuhd, al-Bukhari, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Ibn Umar concerning the verse that he said: "This was only before zakat was revealed. When zakat was revealed, God made it a purification for wealth." Then he said: "I would not mind if I had gold equal to Mount Uhud, whose number I know, and I pay its zakat and act with it in obedience to God."

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu al-Shaykh related from Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said: "What has had its zakat paid is not a hoard."

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi related something similar from Umm Salamah, raised to the Prophet.

Ibn Abi Shaybah in his Musnad, Abu Dawud, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Ibn Abbas, who said: "When this verse was revealed, ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾, it was grievous to the Muslims, and they said: 'None of us can leave to his child what will not remain after him.' Umar said: 'I will relieve you of this.' So Umar set out, and Thawban followed him, and he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'O Prophet of God, this verse has been grievous to your Companions.' He said: 'Indeed God did not prescribe zakat except to purify with it what remains of your wealth, and He prescribed inheritance from wealth that will remain after you.' Umar exclaimed 'Allahu akbar.' Then the Prophet ﷺ said to him: 'Shall I not tell you the best thing a man can hoard? A righteous woman, who when he looks at her delights him, when he commands her she obeys him, and when he is absent from her she guards him.'"

Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), and Ibn Majah related it from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd by more than one route, from Thawban.

Al-Bukhari related that Salim did not hear it from Thawban.

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾, that he said: "They are the People of the Book," and he said: "It is both specific and general."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from Ali ibn Abi Talib that he said: "Four thousand and what is below it is expenditure, and what is above it is a hoard."

Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani related from Abu Umamah that he said: "The sword-ornaments are among the hoards. I do not tell you except what I have heard."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from Iraq ibn Malik and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz that they both said concerning His saying: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾ that it was abrogated by the other verse: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾ (al-Tawbah 9:103), and the rest of the verse.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others related from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "No owner of gold or silver who does not pay its zakat will have it, but on the Day of Resurrection plates will be made for it, then they will be heated in the fire of Hell, and with them his side, his forehead, and his back will be branded, on a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people, and he sees his path, either to Paradise or to the Fire."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Bukhari, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh related from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: "I passed by Abu Dharr at al-Zubdah, and I said: 'What brought you to this land?' He said: 'We were in Syria, and I recited: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾ to the end of the verse. Mu'awiyah said: "What is this about us? This is only about the People of the Book." I said: "It is about us and about them."'"

When He - glory be to Him - finished mentioning the condition of the followers of the rabbis and monks, who took them as lords, He mentioned the condition of those who were followed, saying: ﴿Indeed, many of the rabbis...﴾ to the end of the verse. The meaning of their "devouring people's wealth falsely" is that they take it by illegitimate means, such as bribery. He affirmed this of the many among them, because some of them were not involved in it, but remained upon what their religion required, without distortion, alteration, or inclination toward the trash of this world. Many scholars of Islam have followed these rabbis and monks, in number beyond counting in every age, and to God is the help sought.

﴿And who bar from the way of God﴾: that is, from the path to Him, which is the religion of Islam; or from what was true in their law before its abrogation (naskh), through their devouring people's wealth falsely.

His saying: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾. It is said that they are the rabbis and monks previously mentioned, and that they used to do this. It is also said that they are those Muslims who do this. The better view is to take the verse in the general sense of its wording, for it is broader than that. The root meaning of *kanz* (hoarding) in the language is gathering and collecting, and it is not restricted to gold and silver.

Ibn Jarir said: *kanz* is every thing gathered, one part upon another, whether in the belly of the earth or upon its surface. End of quote.

From this comes *naqatun kinaz*, meaning a she-camel of firm flesh, and *iktanaza al-shay'*, meaning the thing gathered together.

The scholars differed concerning wealth whose zakat has been paid: is it called a hoard or not? Some said it is a hoard; others said it is not a hoard.

Among those who held the first view was Abu Dharr, who restricted it to what exceeds need.

Among those who held the second view were Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Jabir, Abu Hurayrah, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, and others. This is the truth, because of the evidences that will come, which clearly state that wealth whose zakat has been paid is not a hoard.

His saying: ﴿And do not spend it in the way of God﴾.

Scholars differed about the reason the pronoun is singular when the things mentioned before it are two, namely gold and silver. Ibn al-Anbari said: it intends the more general and more prevalent, which is silver. He said: a similar example is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is a great burden﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:45), where the pronoun returns to prayer because it is more general. A similar example is His saying: ﴿But when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush to it﴾ (al-Jumu'ah 62:11), where the pronoun returns to trade because it is the more important. It is also said that the pronoun refers to gold and silver, the second being joined to the first, and the Arabs make gold feminine and masculine. It is also said that the pronoun refers to the hoards indicated by His saying "they hoard." It is also said that it refers to the wealth, or to zakat. It is also said that he suffices with the pronoun of one of them instead of the pronoun of the other, with the meaning understood, and this is common in the speech of the Arabs. Sibawayh recited:

*We are content with what we have, and you are content with what you have, though opinions differ.*

He did not say "contented" in the plural. A similar example is the words of another:

*He threw me with a matter from which I and my father were innocent, and from the sake of hunger he threw me.*

He did not say "two innocent." A similar example is the words of Hassan:

*Indeed the bloom of youth and the hair, when they have not been tempered, were madness.*

He did not say "tempered" in the dual. It is also said that the singular pronoun is by way of going to the meaning rather than the wording, because each of gold and silver is a complete category and a great quantity, dinars and dirhams. This is like His saying: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾ (al-Hujurat 49:9). The gold and silver were singled out for mention rather than the rest of the wealth because they are the prices of things and what is most commonly hoarded, although other things have the same ruling as them regarding the prohibition of hoarding.

His saying: ﴿So give them good tidings of a painful punishment﴾. This is the predicate of the relative clause, and it is in the mode of mockery toward them, as in the words:

*Their greeting among them is a painful striking.*

It is also said that good tidings is the news that changes the color of the skin because of its effect on the heart, whether it is in joy or in grief.

The meaning of ﴿On the Day it will be heated in the fire of Hell﴾ is that the fire will be kindled upon them, and it is of intense heat and fierceness. Had He said "On the Day they will be heated," meaning the hoards, this meaning would not be given. So He made the heating belong to the fire as an exaggeration, then He omitted the fire and attributed the verb to the preposition phrase, as you say: "I raised the matter to the emir," and if you do not mention the matter you say: "It was raised to the emir."

Ibn Amir read *tuhma* with a feminine (second-person) prefix.

Abu Haywah read *fayukwa* with a masculine (third-person) prefix.

He singled out the foreheads, sides, and backs because the pain of their branding is more severe, owing to the noble organs within them. It is also said: so that the branding is on the four directions, from the front, the back, the right, and the left. It is also said: because beauty is in the face, and strength in the back and the sides, and a person seeks wealth for beauty and strength. It is also said other things, which do not avoid being strained.

His saying: ﴿This is what you hoarded for yourselves﴾. That is, it will be said to them: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves," that is, you hoarded it so that you might benefit from it, so this is its benefit, in the manner of mockery and reproach. ﴿So taste what you used to hoard﴾. The *ma* is either verbal (the infinitive) or relative: that is, taste its evil, the wickedness of its outcome, the ugliness of its consequence, and the ill of its fruit.

Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, many of the rabbis and monks﴾, meaning the scholars of the Jews and Christians, ﴿devour people's wealth falsely﴾: the falsehood is books they wrote that God did not send down, and with them they devoured people's wealth. This is the saying of God, exalted: ﴿So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands, then say, "This is from God"﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:79).

Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾, that he said: these are the ones who do not pay zakat from their wealth. Every wealth whose zakat is not paid, whether it is on the surface of the earth or in its belly, is a hoard, and every wealth whose zakat is paid is not a hoard, whether it is on the surface of the earth or in its belly.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh related it from him by another route.

Malik, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh related something similar from Ibn Umar.

Ibn Mardawayh related something similar from him, raised (marfu') to the Prophet.

Ibn Adi and al-Khatib related something similar from Jabir, also raised.

Ibn Abi Shaybah related it from him as a statement of a Companion (mawquf).

Ahmad in al-Zuhd, al-Bukhari, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Ibn Umar concerning the verse that he said: "This was only before zakat was revealed. When zakat was revealed, God made it a purification for wealth." Then he said: "I would not mind if I had gold equal to Mount Uhud, whose number I know, and I pay its zakat and act with it in obedience to God."

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu al-Shaykh related from Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said: "What has had its zakat paid is not a hoard."

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi related something similar from Umm Salamah, raised to the Prophet.

Ibn Abi Shaybah in his Musnad, Abu Dawud, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Ibn Abbas, who said: "When this verse was revealed, ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾, it was grievous to the Muslims, and they said: 'None of us can leave to his child what will not remain after him.' Umar said: 'I will relieve you of this.' So Umar set out, and Thawban followed him, and he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'O Prophet of God, this verse has been grievous to your Companions.' He said: 'Indeed God did not prescribe zakat except to purify with it what remains of your wealth, and He prescribed inheritance from wealth that will remain after you.' Umar exclaimed 'Allahu akbar.' Then the Prophet ﷺ said to him: 'Shall I not tell you the best thing a man can hoard? A righteous woman, who when he looks at her delights him, when he commands her she obeys him, and when he is absent from her she guards him.'"

Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), and Ibn Majah related it from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd by more than one route, from Thawban.

Al-Bukhari related that Salim did not hear it from Thawban.

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾, that he said: "They are the People of the Book," and he said: "It is both specific and general."

He said: 'We were in Syria, and I recited: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾ to the end of the verse. Mu'awiyah said: "What is this about us? This is only about the People of the Book." I said: "It is about us and about them."'"

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 9, verses 36–37:

His saying: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months﴾. This is a new statement that includes mention of another type of the ugly deeds of the disbelievers. That is because Allah, glorified is He, when He had decreed for each time a specific ruling, they changed those times by means of the nasi' (intercalation) and the kabisah (the intercalary month), so Allah informed us of what His ruling is, and said: ﴿Indeed, the number of months﴾, that is, the number of the months of the year, ﴿with Allah﴾ in His judgment, His decree and His wisdom, ﴿is twelve months﴾.

His saying: ﴿in the Book of Allah﴾, that is, in what He has established in His Book.

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: It is not permissible to connect "in the Book of Allah" with His saying "the number of months," because of the separation by a foreign element, which is the predicate, namely "twelve months." So His saying "in the Book of Allah" and His saying "the day He created" are a substitution (badal) for His saying "with Allah," and the construction is: Indeed, the number of months with Allah, in the Book of Allah, the day He created the heavens and the earth. The benefit of the two substitutions is to fix the statement in minds, because it is known from it that this number is obligatory with Allah, in the Book of Allah, and established in His knowledge from the very first moment Allah created the world.

It is also permissible that "in the Book of Allah" be a description of "twelve": that is, twelve, established in the Book of Allah, which is the Preserved Tablet.

In this verse there is a clarification that Allah, glorified is He, set these months and named them by their names in this well-known order on the day He created the heavens and the earth, and that this is what the prophets brought and what the Books revealed, and that there is no consideration for what is found among the non-Arabs, the Romans and the Copts of months which they agree upon, making some of them thirty days, some more, and some fewer.

His saying: ﴿Of them, four are sacred﴾. They are: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, al-Muharram, and Rajab; three consecutive and one solitary, as the explanation of this has come in the purified Sunnah.

His saying: ﴿That is the upright religion﴾, that is: the state of these months being as such, and that of them four are sacred, is the upright religion, the correct reckoning, and the complete count.

His saying: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾, that is: in these sacred months, by initiating fighting in them and violating their sanctity. It has been said that the pronoun refers to all the months, sacred and otherwise, and that Allah forbade wronging within them; but the first is preferable.

A group of the people of knowledge held that the prohibition of fighting (p-571) in the sacred months is established and muhkam (definitive), not abrogated, based on this verse, and on His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah, nor the sacred month﴾ (al-Ma'idah: 2), and on His saying: ﴿Then when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists﴾ (al-Tawbah: 5), and so on.

Another group held that the prohibition of fighting in the sacred months is abrogated by the verse of the sword.

This is answered by saying that the command to kill the polytheists and fight them is restricted by the passing of the sacred months, as in the verse mentioned, so all the other verses containing the command to fight are restricted by what has come concerning the prohibition of fighting in the sacred months, just as they are restricted by the prohibition of fighting in the Sacred Precinct, due to the evidences that have come regarding the prohibition of fighting in it. As for what they cited, that "he (ﷺ) besieged the people of al-Ta'if in a sacred month, which is Dhu al-Qa'dah," as is established in the Two Sahihs and others, it has been answered that he did not begin their siege in Dhu al-Qa'dah but in Shawwal, and what is prohibited is only beginning fighting in the sacred months, not completing it; and with this the reconciliation is achieved.

His saying: ﴿And fight the polytheists all together﴾, that is, all of them; it is a verbal noun (masdar) in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal).

al-Zajjaj said: Such nouns as 'ammah and khassah are not made dual or plural. ﴿As they fight you all together﴾, that is, all of them.

In this is evidence for the obligation of fighting the polytheists, and that it is an individual obligation (fard 'ayn) if some do not carry it out. ﴿And know that Allah is with the righteous﴾, that is, He helps them and makes them firm; and whoever Allah is with is the victor, and to him belong the final outcome and the victory.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief﴾.

Nafi', in the narration of Warsh from him, read "al-Nasiyy" with a shaddah on the ya' without a hamzah.

The rest read with a ya' followed by a hamzah.

al-Nahhas said: No one narrated this reading from Nafi' except Warsh alone, and it is derived from nasa'ahu and ansa'ahu: when he postponed it. al-Kisa'i related this.

al-Jawhari said: al-Nasi' is fa'il in the sense of maf'ul, from your saying: nasa'tu al-shay' so it is mansu': when you postponed it; then mansu' was changed into nasi' just as maqtul was changed into qatil.

Ibn Jarir said: In al-nasi' with the hamzah is the meaning of increase; it is said: nasa'a yansa'u: when he increased. He said: And it does not come without the hamzah except from forgetting (nisyan), as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾. He rejected Nafi''s reading.

The Arabs used to forbid fighting in the aforementioned sacred months; when they needed to fight in them, they fought in them and made other months sacred instead. When they fought in al-Muharram, they made Safar sacred in its place, and so on for the rest. What drove them to this was that many of them lived by raiding one another and plundering what they could of the property of those they raided, and fighting would arise between them because of that. The three consecutive sacred months would harm them by their succession, their need would intensify and their poverty would grow, so they would make one of them lawful and make sacred another month in its place of equal count from outside the sacred months. This is the meaning of the nasi' they practised.

There has been disagreement about who first did this. It was said: he was a man from the Banu Kinanah called Hudhayfah ibn 'Ataid, known as al-Qalammas, and to him the poet Kumayt alludes with his saying:

Are we not the ones who postpone (the months) over Ma'add, making the months of lawfulness sacred?

And of him one of them said:

And among us is the postponer of the month, al-Qalammas.

It was also said: he was 'Amr ibn Luhayy; and it was said: he was Nu'aym ibn Tha'labah of the Banu Kinanah. Allah, glorified is He, called the nasi' an increase in disbelief because it is a kind of their disbelief, and one of their acts of disobedience joined to their disbelief in Allah, His Books, His messengers and the Last Day.

His saying: ﴿By it those who disbelieve are led astray﴾.

The people of the two Sanctuaries, Abu 'Amr and Ibn 'Amir read "yudall" with the active form (yaḍillu).

The Kufans read it in the passive form. The meaning of the first reading is that the disbelievers go astray by what they do of the nasi'; the meaning of the second reading is that the one who established that for them makes them go astray by this evil practice. Abu Hatim chose the first reading, and Abu 'Ubayd chose the second.

al-Hasan, Abu Raja' and Ya'qub read "yuḍillu" with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the ḍad, the subject being the relative pronoun and the object omitted; and it is permissible that its subject be Allah, glorified is He, and its object the relative pronoun.

It was also read with a fatha on the ya' and the ḍad from ḍalla yaḍallu.

It was read nuḍillu with the nun.

His saying: ﴿They make it lawful one year and make it sacred another year﴾. The pronoun refers to the nasi': that is, they make the nasi' lawful one year and make it sacred another year; or it refers to the month which they postpone and fight in: that is, they make it lawful one year by substituting another month of the lawful months for it, and "they make it sacred another year": that is, they observe it and do not make fighting lawful in it, but keep it in its sanctity.

His saying: ﴿So that they may conform to the number of what Allah has forbidden﴾, that is, so that they may agree, and al-mu'atha'ah is agreement; it is said: "they agreed upon such-and-such," meaning they concurred and gathered upon it.

The meaning: they did not make one month lawful without making another month sacred, so that the sacred months would remain four.

Qutrub said: its meaning is that they targeted Safar and added it to the sacred months and paired it with al-Muharram in the prohibition; and al-Tabari said likewise.

His saying: ﴿So that they make lawful what Allah has forbidden﴾, that is, of the sacred months which they replaced with others. ﴿The evil of their deeds is made attractive to them﴾, that is: Satan made attractive to them the evil deeds they were doing, and among them the nasi'.

It was read in the active form. ﴿And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾, that is, those who persist in their disbelief and remain upon it; so He does not guide them with a guidance that brings them to the desired goal. As for guidance in the sense of indicating the truth and directing to it, Allah, glorified is He, has set that for all His servants.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others have related from the hadith of Abu Bakrah that the Prophet (ﷺ) delivered a sermon during his pilgrimage and said: "Indeed, time has returned to its form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, of which four are sacred: three consecutive ones—Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and al-Muharram—and Rajab of Mudar, which lies between Jumada and Sha'ban."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related something similar from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar. Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related something similar from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.

al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh also related something similar from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.

Ahmad and Ibn Mardawayh related it from the hadith of Abu Hurrah al-Raqashi from his uncle, marfu', in a lengthier form.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿Of them four are sacred﴾ that they are: al-Muharram, Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'dah and Dhu al-Hijjah.

Abu al-Shaykh related from al-Dahhak that he said: They were only called sacred so that there would be no fighting in them.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab related from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah﴾, then He singled out from that four months and made them sacred, magnified their sanctities, and made the religion in them greater, and righteous deeds and reward greater. ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾: he said, "in all of them." ﴿And fight the polytheists all together﴾: he said, "all of them."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from Muqatil regarding His saying: ﴿And fight the polytheists all together﴾ that he said: This verse abrogated every verse that contained a concession.

al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh related from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "The Arabs used to make one month lawful in one year and two months in another year, and they would reach the Hajj only once every year, and once every twenty years—and this is the nasi' which Allah mentioned in His Book. When the year of Abu Bakr's Hajj with the people came, that year coincided, so Allah named it 'the greatest Hajj.' Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed Hajj in the following year, and the people faced the new moons correctly, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, time has returned to its form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh related from Ibn 'Umar who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood at al-'Aqabah and said: 'Indeed, the nasi' is from Satan, an increase in disbelief, by which those who disbelieve are led astray: they make it lawful one year and make it sacred another year.' So they would make al-Muharram sacred one year and treat Safar as lawful, and make Safar sacred another year and treat al-Muharram as lawful. This is the nasi'."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Janadah ibn 'Awf al-Kinani used to attend the season every year, and he was called Abu Thumamah. He would proclaim: "Behold, Abu Thumamah is not to be refuted nor reproached. Behold, the first Safar this year is lawful," so he would make it lawful for the people, and then he would make Safar sacred one year and make al-Muharram sacred another year. That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief﴾, and so on.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from him regarding the verse, he said: They used to call al-Muharram "Safar," and Safar they would say there are two Safars, the first and the last; so it would be lawful for them once as the first, and once as the last.

Ibn Mardawayh related from him who said: The Nassa'ah was a tribe of the Banu Malik of the Kinanah, of the Banu Fuqaym; and the last of them was a man called al-Qalammas, and he it was who postponed al-Muharram.
