He said: 'Woe to you, O Tha'labah! A little of which you render its thanks is better than a lot which you cannot bear.' He said: 'O Messenger of God, pray to God that He give me wealth.' He said: 'Woe to you, O Tha'labah! Do you not wish to be like me? By Him in whose hand is my soul, if my Lord were to make these mountains move with me as gold, they would move.' He said: 'O Messenger of God, pray to God that He give me wealth. By Him who sent you with the truth, if God gives me wealth I will surely give to everyone with a right his right.' He said: 'Woe to you, O Tha'labah! A little of which you can render its thanks is better than a lot which you cannot bear.' He said: 'O Messenger of God, pray to God, may He be exalted.' So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'O God, give him wealth.' He said: 'So he acquired sheep, and they grew as worms grow, until Medina became too cramped for them, so he moved away with them. He used to attend prayer during the day with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) but not at night. Then they grew as worms grow, and he moved away with them, and he did not attend prayer by night or by day, except from one Friday to another Friday with the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Then they grew as worms grow, and his place became too cramped for him, so he moved away with them, and he did not attend Friday prayer or any funeral with the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He began to meet the riders and ask them for news. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) missed him and asked about him, and they informed him that he had bought sheep, that Medina had become too cramped for him, and they told him his story. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'Woe to Tha'labah ibn Hatib! Woe to Tha'labah ibn Hatib!' Then God, may He be exalted, commanded His Messenger to take the charities, and revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾ [At-Tawbah 9:103], and so on. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent two men, a man from Juhaynah and a man from Banu Salimah, to take the charities, and he wrote for them the ages of camels and sheep, how they should take them and their specifications, and ordered them to pass by Tha'labah ibn Hatib and by a man from Banu Sulaym. They set out and passed by Tha'labah and asked for the charity. He said: 'Show me your letter.' He looked at it and said: 'This is nothing but a jizyah (poll tax). Go on until I consider my opinion.' They went on until they reached Medina. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) saw them, before they spoke to him he said: 'Woe to Tha'labah ibn Hatib!' and he invoked blessing upon the Sulami man. God revealed: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with God﴾ [At-Tawbah 9:75], the three verses. A relative of Tha'labah heard this, came to Tha'labah, and said: 'Woe to you, O Tha'labah, such-and-such has been revealed concerning you.' So Tha'labah came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of God, this is the charity of my wealth.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'God has forbidden me to accept it from you.' So he began to weep and throw dust on his head. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'This is your own doing; I commanded you but you did not obey me.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not accept it from him until he died. Then he came to Abu Bakr and said: 'O Abu Bakr, [p. 588] accept my charity, for you know my standing among the Ansar.' Abu Bakr said: 'The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not accept it, so shall I accept it?' And Abu Bakr did not accept it. Then 'Umar ibn al-Khattab took office, and he came to him and said: 'O Abu Hafs, O Commander of the Believers, accept my charity.' He (the narrator) said: 'It weighed upon him with the Muhajirun and the Ansar and the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ).' 'Umar said: 'The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not accept it, nor did Abu Bakr; shall I accept it?' So he refused to accept it. Then 'Uthman took office, and he asked him to accept his charity. He said: 'The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not accept it, nor Abu Bakr, nor 'Umar, and I should accept it from you?!' So he did not accept it from him. He said: "And that was concerning the charity." He said that this is ﴿because they broke their promise to God in what they had promised Him, and because they used to lie﴾.

So ﴿Those who criticise the volunteers﴾, the verse, was revealed." There are many other narrations on this subject.

He said: 'Woe to you, O Tha'labah! Do you not wish to be like me? By Him in whose hand is my soul, if my Lord were to make these mountains move with me as gold, they would move.' He said: 'Woe to you, O Tha'labah! A little of which you can render its thanks is better than a lot which you cannot bear.' He said: 'O Messenger of God, pray to God, may He be exalted.' So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'O God, give him wealth.' He said: 'So he acquired sheep, and they grew as worms grow, until Medina became too cramped for them, so he moved away with them. He used to attend prayer during the day with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) but not at night. Then they grew as worms grow, and he moved away with them, and he did not attend prayer by night or by day, except from one Friday to another Friday with the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Then they grew as worms grow, and his place became too cramped for him, so he moved away with them, and he did not attend Friday prayer or any funeral with the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He began to meet the riders and ask them for news. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) missed him and asked about him, and they informed him that he had bought sheep, that Medina had become too cramped for him, and they told him his story. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'Woe to Tha'labah ibn Hatib! Woe to Tha'labah ibn Hatib!' Then God, may He be exalted, commanded His Messenger to take the charities, and revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾ [At-Tawbah 9:103], and so on. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent two men, a man from Juhaynah and a man from Banu Salimah, to take the charities, and he wrote for them the ages of camels and sheep, how they should take them and their specifications, and ordered them to pass by Tha'labah ibn Hatib and by a man from Banu Sulaym. They set out and passed by Tha'labah and asked for the charity. He said: 'Show me your letter.' He looked at it and said: 'This is nothing but a jizyah (poll tax). Go on until I consider my opinion.' They went on until they reached Medina. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) saw them, before they spoke to him he said: 'Woe to Tha'labah ibn Hatib!' and he invoked blessing upon the Sulami man. God revealed: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with God﴾ [At-Tawbah 9:75], the three verses. A relative of Tha'labah heard this, came to Tha'labah, and said: 'Woe to you, O Tha'labah, such-and-such has been revealed concerning you.' So Tha'labah came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of God, this is the charity of my wealth.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'God has forbidden me to accept it from you.' So he began to weep and throw dust on his head. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'This is your own doing; I commanded you but you did not obey me.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not accept it from him until he died. Then he came to Abu Bakr and said: 'O Abu Bakr, [p. 588] accept my charity, for you know my standing among the Ansar.' Abu Bakr said: 'The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not accept it, so shall I accept it?' And Abu Bakr did not accept it. Then 'Umar ibn al-Khattab took office, and he came to him and said: 'O Abu Hafs, O Commander of the Believers, accept my charity.' He (the narrator) said: 'It weighed upon him with the Muhajirun and the Ansar and the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ).' 'Umar said: 'The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not accept it, nor did Abu Bakr; shall I accept it?' So he refused to accept it. Then 'Uthman took office, and he asked him to accept his charity. He said: 'The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not accept it, nor Abu Bakr, nor 'Umar, and I should accept it from you?!' So he did not accept it from him. The "ب" (ba') in ﴿بِمَا أَخْلَفُوا اللَّهَ مَا وَعَدُوهُ﴾ ("because they broke their promise to God in what they had promised Him") indicates causation: that is, because of their breaking what they had promised of giving charity and righteousness. Likewise the "ب" in ﴿وَبِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ﴾ ("and because they used to lie") means: and because of their denial of what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) brought.

Then He rebuked them, saying: ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا﴾ ("Did they not know?"), meaning the hypocrites. It is also read with the second person (ta'), addressing the believers. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ سِرَّهُمْ وَنَجْوَاهُم﴾ ("that God knows their secret and their private counsel") means all that they conceal of hypocrisy and all that they confide to one another in private, of defamation of the Prophet (ﷺ), of his companions, and of the religion of Islam. ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ﴾ ("and that God is the Knower of the unseen") means nothing is hidden from Him of the hidden things, whatever they may be, and among that is what proceeds from the hypocrites.

On His saying, ﴿الَّذِينَ يَلْمِزُونَ الْمُطَّوِّعِينَ﴾ ("those who criticise those who give voluntarily"): the relative clause (al-mawsul) is in the accusative position, or in the nominative by way of censure (al-dhamm), or in the genitive as a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in "سِرَّهُمْ وَنَجْوَاهُم" ("their secret and their private counsel"). The meaning of "يَلْمِزُونَ" is "they find fault with," and its explanation has already been given. "الْمُطَّوِّعِينَ" means "those who volunteer" (al-mutatawwi'in), and "tatawwu'" means voluntary giving.

The meaning is: the hypocrites used to find fault with the Muslims when they volunteered something of their wealth and brought it out for charity. They would say: "God has no need of this!" and they would say: "They only did this for show (riya')," and it was not purely for God. And "فِي الصَّدَقَاتِ" ("concerning the charities") is connected to "يَلْمِزُونَ": that is, they find fault with them regarding it.

On His saying, ﴿وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ إِلَّا جُهْدَهُمْ﴾ ("and those who find nothing but their effort"): it is conjoined to "الْمُطَّوِّعِينَ": that is, they find fault with the volunteers and with those who find nothing but their effort. It has also been said that it is conjoined to "الْمُؤْمِنِينَ" ("the believers"): that is, they find fault with the volunteers from among the believers, and with those who find nothing but their effort. It is also read "جَهْدَهُمْ" with a fatha on the jim. "الْجُهْد" with a damma means capacity, and with a fatha means hardship. It has been said that both are dialects with one meaning, and this has already been explained.

The meaning is: the hypocrites used to find fault with the poor believers who gave from what exceeded their sufficiency.

On His saying, ﴿فَيَسْخَرُونَ مِنْهُمْ﴾ ("and they mock them"): it is conjoined to "يَلْمِزُونَ": that is, they ridicule them because of the paltriness of what they brought out in charity, although that was the utmost effort of the poor man and the most he could afford and manage.

On His saying, ﴿سَخِرَ اللَّهُ مِنْهُمْ﴾ ("God mocks them"): that is, He repaid them for their mockery of the believers with the like of it. So God mocked them by humiliating them, debasing them, and punishing them. The expression of this is by way of mushakalah (the figure of answering like with like), as in other places. It has also been said that it is a supplication against them, that God should mock them as they mocked the Muslims. ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ ("and for them is a painful punishment") means lasting, established, severely painful.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Askari in al-Amthal, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mandah, al-Barudi, Abu Nu'aym, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi, and Ibn 'Asakir reported from Abu Umamah al-Bahili, who said: "Tha'labah ibn Hatib came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of God, pray to God that He give me wealth.' He said: 'Woe to you, O Tha'labah! A little of which you render its thanks is better than a lot which you cannot bear.' He said: 'O Messenger of God, pray to God that He give me wealth.' He said: 'Woe to you, O Tha'labah! Do you not wish to be like me? By Him in whose hand is my soul, if my Lord were to make these mountains move with me as gold, they would move.' He said: 'O Messenger of God, pray to God that He give me wealth. By Him who sent you with the truth, if God gives me wealth I will surely give to everyone with a right his right.' He said: 'Woe to you, O Tha'labah! A little of which you can render its thanks is better than a lot which you cannot bear.' He said: 'O Messenger of God, pray to God, may He be exalted.' So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'O God, give him wealth.' He said: 'So he acquired sheep, and they grew as worms grow, until Medina became too cramped for them, so he moved away with them. He used to attend prayer during the day with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) but not at night. Then they grew as worms grow, and he moved away with them, and he did not attend prayer by night or by day, except from one Friday to another Friday with the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Then they grew as worms grow, and his place became too cramped for him, so he moved away with them, and he did not attend Friday prayer or any funeral with the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He began to meet the riders and ask them for news. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) missed him and asked about him, and they informed him that he had bought sheep, that Medina had become too cramped for him, and they told him his story. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'Woe to Tha'labah ibn Hatib! Woe to Tha'labah ibn Hatib!' Then God, may He be exalted, commanded His Messenger to take the charities, and revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾ [At-Tawbah 9:103], and so on. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent two men, a man from Juhaynah and a man from Banu Salimah, to take the charities, and he wrote for them the ages of camels and sheep, how they should take them and their specifications, and ordered them to pass by Tha'labah ibn Hatib and by a man from Banu Sulaym. They set out and passed by Tha'labah and asked for the charity. He said: 'Show me your letter.' He looked at it and said: 'This is nothing but a jizyah (poll tax). Go on until I consider my opinion.' They went on until they reached Medina. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) saw them, before they spoke to him he said: 'Woe to Tha'labah ibn Hatib!' and he invoked blessing upon the Sulami man. God revealed: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with God﴾ [At-Tawbah 9:75], the three verses. A relative of Tha'labah heard this, came to Tha'labah, and said: 'Woe to you, O Tha'labah, such-and-such has been revealed concerning you.' So Tha'labah came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of God, this is the charity of my wealth.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'God has forbidden me to accept it from you.' So he began to weep and throw dust on his head. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'This is your own doing; I commanded you but you did not obey me.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not accept it from him until he died. Then he came to Abu Bakr and said: 'O Abu Bakr, [p. 588] accept my charity, for you know my standing among the Ansar.' Abu Bakr said: 'The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not accept it, so shall I accept it?' And Abu Bakr did not accept it. Then 'Umar ibn al-Khattab took office, and he came to him and said: 'O Abu Hafs, O Commander of the Believers, accept my charity.' He (the narrator) said: 'It weighed upon him with the Muhajirun and the Ansar and the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ).' 'Umar said: 'The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not accept it, nor did Abu Bakr; shall I accept it?' So he refused to accept it. Then 'Uthman took office, and he asked him to accept his charity. He said: 'The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not accept it, nor Abu Bakr, nor 'Umar, and I should accept it from you?!' So he did not accept it from him. He died during the caliphate of 'Uthman, and concerning him was revealed: ﴿Those who criticise those of the believers who give voluntarily in the charities﴾.'" He said: "And that was concerning the charity." This hadith is narrated through Mu'adh ibn Rifa'ah, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, client of 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah, from Abu Umamah al-Bahili.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il reported from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with God﴾, the verse. The reason was that a man called Tha'labah from the Ansar came to a gathering and called them to witness, saying: "If God gives me of His bounty, I will surely give to everyone with a right his right, and I will give charity from it, and I will set aside some of it for relatives." God tested him: He gave him of His bounty, but he broke what he had promised. So God was angered by his breaking of what he had promised, and God related his story in the Qur'an.

Abu al-Shaykh reported from al-Hasan that a man from the Ansar was the one who said this. A paternal cousin of his died and left him wealth, but he was stingy with it and did not fulfil what he had covenanted with God. So God caused hypocrisy to follow him in his heart until he met Him. He said that this is ﴿because they broke their promise to God in what they had promised Him, and because they used to lie﴾.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others reported from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "When the verse on charity was revealed, we used to carry loads on our backs (to earn what we would give). A man came and gave a large amount in charity, and they said: 'He is showing off!' Then Abu 'Aqil came with half a sa'. The hypocrites said: 'God has no need of this man's charity!' So ﴿Those who criticise the volunteers﴾, the verse, was revealed." There are many other narrations on this subject.

Abu al-Shaykh reported from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿Those who criticise the volunteers﴾, meaning: they slander those who volunteer.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 9, verses 80–83:

Allah informed His Messenger ﷺ that his asking forgiveness for the hypocrites and his not doing so are equal, because they are not people deserving of his seeking forgiveness for them, nor of Allah's forgiveness for them. This is like His saying: ﴿Say: "Spend willingly or unwillingly; it will never be accepted from you."﴾ Then He said: ﴿Even if you seek forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them.﴾ In this is a clarification that Allah will not forgive the hypocrites, even if the Prophet ﷺ asks forgiveness for them much. The intended meaning is not that if he exceeded seventy it would be accepted, as in the rest of the implications of numbers; rather, the intended meaning is to stress the extent of non-acceptance.

The Arabs used this as a proverbial expression in their speech when they wished to express abundance. The meaning is: Allah will not forgive them, even if you ask forgiveness for them in an extremely abundant manner.

Some jurists held that restricting the matter to this specific number implies that more than it would be accepted, and what will come from the Prophet ﷺ supports this, that he said: "I will certainly add more than seventy."

Some scholars mentioned a reason for specifying seventy, saying: The number seven is noble, because it is the number of the heavens, the earths, the seas, the climes, the wandering planets, the limbs, and the days of the week. So each of the seven was multiplied to ten, because the good deed is rewarded tenfold.

It was also said: seventy was singled out for mention because the Prophet ﷺ pronounced takbir over his uncle Hamzah seventy times. So it is as if He said: "If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, in return for your takbirs over Hamzah."

The accusative of seventy is as an absolute object (masdar), like the saying of them: "I struck him twenty strikes."

Then He gave the reason for their not being forgiven, saying: ﴿That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger.﴾ That is, that refusal is due to their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger. ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiant people.﴾ That is, the rebellious ones who are out of obedience and transgress its limits. What is meant here is guidance that leads to the desired goal, not the guidance meaning mere indication and showing the way.

Then Allah mentioned another kind of the hypocrites' ugly conduct, saying: ﴿Those who were left behind rejoiced in their staying behind, contrary to the Messenger of Allah.﴾ "Those left behind" means those who were abandoned, and they are those hypocrites who sought permission from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he permitted them and left them behind in Madinah during the expedition of Tabuk; or those whom Allah left behind and discouraged; or Satan; or those who made them lazy; or the believers. The meaning of "in their staying behind" is in their sitting; it is said: qa'ada qu'udan and maq'adan, meaning he sat, and his being made to sit by another, as al-Jawhari mentioned. So it is connected to "rejoiced": those left behind rejoiced in their sitting. And "contrary to the Messenger of Allah" is in the accusative as an adverbial complement to "their staying behind."

Al-Akhfash and Yunus said: "al-khilaf" means "al-khalf," that is, after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, because the direction a person intends in front is opposed by the direction behind.

Qutrub and al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "contrary to the Messenger of Allah" is opposition to the Messenger when he set out and they remained. So its accusative is as an object of purpose, that is, they sat for the sake of opposition; or as a circumstantial accusative, like the phrase "and he sent her in the rush," meaning opposing him. The reading of Abu Haywah, "khalfa rasul Allah," supports what al-Akhfash and Yunus said.

His saying: ﴿And they disliked striving with their wealth and their selves in the way of Allah.﴾ The cause of that is stinginess with wealth and selves, the absence of the motive of faith and the call of sincerity, and the presence of what diverts from that, which is the hypocrisy they are in. This contains an allusion to the believers who spend their wealth and selves in the way of Allah, since the motive is present with them and the diverting factor is absent from them. ﴿And they said: "Do not go forth in the heat."⟩ That is, the hypocrites said this statement to their brethren, to discourage them, break their enthusiasm, and urge one another to oppose the command of Allah and His Messenger. Then Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to say to them: ﴿The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if they only understood.﴾ The meaning is: O hypocrites, how do you flee from this slight heat, when the Fire of Hell which you will enter, abiding in it forever, is more intense in heat than what you fled from? You fled from a slight heat for a short time, and fell into a great heat for a long time, indeed an endless heat for everlasting ages and eternal eras.

"So you were like one who hastens to a well, seeking shelter from the paths of the thunderer."

The answer to "if" in ﴿if they understood⟩ is omitted: that is, if they understood that it is so, they would not have done what they did.

His saying: ﴿So let them laugh little and let them weep much.⟩ These two imperatives mean a report, and the meaning is: they will laugh little and weep much. These were phrased in the form of a command only to show that this is a decreed matter that cannot be otherwise. "Little" and "much" are in the accusative as either a verbal noun or an adverbial of time: that is, laughing little and weeping much, or a little time and a long time. ﴿As a recompense for what they used to earn.⟩ That is, as a recompense for what they used to earn of sins. The accusative of "recompense" is as a verbal noun: that is, they will be recompensed a recompense.

﴿So if Allah returns you to a group of them⟩: "al-raj'" is transitive like "al-radd," while "al-ruju'" is intransitive. The "fa" marks the consequence of what follows from what precedes. He said "to a group" because not all who remained in Madinah were hypocrites; among them were others of the believers who had valid excuses, and among the believers were some who had no excuse. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pardoned them, and Allah accepted their repentance, like the three who were left behind, and the explanation of that will come.

It was also said: He said "a group" because some of them repented of hypocrisy and regretted staying behind. ﴿And they ask your permission to go forth with you⟩ in another expedition after this expedition of yours, then say to them: ﴿You will never go forth with me, ever, and you will never fight with me against an enemy.⟩ That is, say this to them as a punishment, and because of the corruption in taking them along, as was mentioned earlier in His saying: ﴿Had they gone forth among you, they would not have increased you except in corruption.⟩

It was read with the vowel "a" on the "ya'" of "ma'iya" in both places, and it was read with sukun on it in both. The clause ﴿Indeed, you were content with sitting the first time⟩ is causal: that is, you will never go forth with me nor fight, because you were content with sitting and staying behind the first time, which is the expedition of Tabuk. The "fa" in ﴿So sit with those who stay behind⟩ marks the consequence of what follows from what precedes. "Al-khalifin" is the plural of "khalif," as if they were the successors of those who went forth, and the intended meaning is those who stayed behind from going out.

It was also said: the meaning is: sit with the corrupt ones, from the saying: "so-and-so opposed his household" when he was corrupt among them, from the saying: "the milk spoiled" (khalafa al-laban), meaning it became spoiled by long staying in the waterskin, as al-Asma'i mentioned.

It was read as "fa'qud al-khalifin" with "khalif" as well, and al-Farra' said: its meaning is "al-mukhalifin" (those who oppose).

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Urwah that Abdullah ibn Ubayy said: "Were it not that you spend upon Muhammad and his companions, they would have dispersed from around him." He was the one who said: ﴿The mightier will surely expel the meaner from it⟩ [al-Munafiqun: 8]. So Allah revealed: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them⟩, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "I will certainly add more than seventy," so Allah revealed: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them⟩ [al-Munafiqun: 6].

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated similarly from Mujahid.

Ibn Jarir narrated similarly from Ibn Abbas.

Ahmad, al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Nahhas, Ibn Hibban, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: I heard Umar say: When Abdullah ibn Ubayy died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was called to pray over him, so he stood over him. When he stood, I said: "Over the enemy of Allah, Abdullah ibn Ubayy, who said such-and-such and such-and-such?" I counted his days, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled, until when I had said much, he said: "O Umar, step back from me. I have been given a choice. It has been said to me: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them.⟩ If I knew that if I added beyond seventy he would be forgiven, I would have added to it." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over him and walked with him until he stood at his grave until he was finished with it. I was amazed at myself and my boldness toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah and His Messenger know best. By Allah, it was not long before these two verses were revealed: ﴿And do not pray over any of them who has died, nor stand at his grave⟩ [al-Tawbah: 84]. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not pray over a hypocrite after that, until Allah took him, the Mighty and Majestic.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Those who were left behind rejoiced⟩ the verse, that he said: about the expedition of Tabuk.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded the people to set out with him, and that was in the summer. Some men said: "O Messenger of Allah, the heat is severe and we cannot go forth, so do not go forth in the heat." Allah said: ﴿Say: "The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if they only understood."⟩ Then He commanded him to go forth.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated similarly from Jabir ibn Abdullah.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So let them laugh little and let them weep much⟩, he said: They are the hypocrites and the disbelievers who took their religion as mockery and play. Allah says: let them laugh little in this world and weep much in the Hereafter.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿So if Allah returns you to a group of them⟩, he said: It was mentioned to us that they were twelve men from the hypocrites, and concerning them was said what was said.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So sit with those who stay behind⟩, he said: They are the men who stayed behind from the expedition.

The intended meaning is not that if he exceeded seventy it would be accepted, as in the rest of the implications of numbers; rather, the intended meaning is to stress the extent of non-acceptance.

The Arabs used this as a proverbial expression in their speech when they wished to express abundance. The meaning is: Allah will not forgive them, even if you ask forgiveness for them in an extremely abundant manner.

Some jurists held that restricting the matter to this specific number implies that more than it would be accepted, and what will come from the Prophet ﷺ supports this, that he said: "I will certainly add more than seventy."

Some scholars mentioned a reason for specifying seventy, saying: The number seven is noble, because it is the number of the heavens, the earths, the seas, the climes, the wandering planets, the limbs, and the days of the week. So each of the seven was multiplied to ten, because the good deed is rewarded tenfold.

It was also said: seventy was singled out for mention because the Prophet ﷺ pronounced takbir over his uncle Hamzah seventy times. So it is as if He said: "If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, in return for your takbirs over Hamzah."

The accusative of seventy is as an absolute object (masdar), like the saying of them: "I struck him twenty strikes."

What is meant here is guidance that leads to the desired goal, not the guidance meaning mere indication and showing the way.

His words, "(ماتَ) is an adjective modifying *aḥad* (anyone), and (أبَدًا) is an adverb of time (ẓarf) indicating the perpetuity of the negation."

It was also said that its meaning is: do not undertake the tasks of repairing his grave. The clause ﴿for they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger﴾ is a reason (ta'līl) for the prohibition. Then He mentioned the benefits of *jihad*, saying: ﴿And those, they are the good things﴾. *Khayrat* (good things) is the plural of *khayr*, so it includes the benefits of this world and the religion. It has been said that what is meant by it is the beautiful women, as in His words, exalted is He: ﴿In them are good [women], beautiful﴾. Its singular is *khayyira*, with a doubled letter, which was then lightened, as in *hayyina* and *hayna*.

The meaning of *falah* (success) has already been stated, and what is meant by it here is those who attain the sought-after goal. The repetition of the demonstrative is to glorify their status and magnify their affair.

*Jannat* (gardens) are orchards. The flowing of the rivers beneath them, and the eternity and the triumph, have already been explained.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 9, verse 90:

Al-A'raj and al-Dahhak read "al-mu'dhirun" (المُعْذِرُونَ) with a light vowelling (takhfif), from a'dhara. Abu Kurayb related it from Abu Bakr, from 'Asim, and the transmitters of the readings (ashab al-qira'at) related it from Ibn 'Abbas.

In al-Sihah [of al-Jawhari] it is said: Ibn 'Abbas used to read: "wa-ja'a al-mu'dhirun" with a light vowelling, from a'dhara, and he would say: "By Allah, thus was it revealed."

Al-Nahhas said: However, its transmission rests on al-Kalbi. It is from a'dhara, meaning he went to the utmost in making excuses (idha bala'a fi al-'udhr). From this comes: "Whoever warns has indeed made the case clear" (man andhara faqad a'dhara), i.e., he went to the utmost in giving excuse.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read ﴿al-mu'addhirun﴾ with emphasis (tashdid), and in it there are two aspects. The first is that its original form is al-mu'tadhirun, and the ta' was assimilated into the dhal, and they are those who have a genuine excuse. From this is the verse of Labid:

"Until a year has passed, then peace be upon you both; and whoever weeps for a full year has indeed made an excuse (i'tadhar)."

So al-mu'addhirun, on this view, are those who are truthful in their making excuses.

This has been related from al-Farra', al-Zajjaj and Ibn al-Anbari. It was also said that it is from 'adhdhara, meaning one who makes excuses while having no excuse. One says 'adhdhara in the matter when he falls short and makes an excuse with what is not an excuse. This was mentioned by al-Jawhari and the author of al-Kashshaf. So al-mu'addhirun, on this view, are the falsifiers (al-mubtilun), because they made excuses with false pretexts that have no basis.

It has been related from al-Akhfash, al-Farra', Abu Hatim and Abu 'Ubayda that it is permissible to vowel the 'ayn with kasra because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters (iltiqa' al-sakinayn), and with damma by assimilation (al-itba').

The meaning is: these Bedouins came with the excuses they brought, whether true or false, on both explanations, so that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would grant them permission to stay behind from the expedition. Another group did not make excuses at all, but sat back from the expedition without any excuse; they are the hypocrites among the Bedouins who lied to Allah and His Messenger, and did not believe nor were truthful. Then Allah, glorified is He, threatened them, saying: ﴿Those of them who disbelieve will be struck by a painful punishment﴾, i.e., among the Bedouins, and they are those who made excuses with false pretexts, and those who did not make excuses but lied to Allah and His Messenger. ﴿A painful punishment﴾, i.e., greatly painful, so it applies to the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter.

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And the excusers among the Bedouins came﴾, i.e., those of them who had a genuine excuse.

Ibn Abi Hatim related similar to this from him.

Ibn al-Anbari also transmitted in Kitab al-Adad from him that he used to say: "May Allah curse the excusers (al-mu'addhirin)," and he would read with emphasis, as if in his view al-mu'addhir with emphasis is one who displays an excuse by pretext without reality.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from Ibn Ishaq, regarding His saying: ﴿And the excusers among the Bedouins came﴾, that he said: It was mentioned to me that they were a group from the Banu Ghifar who came and made excuses, among them Khafaf ibn Ima'; and it was said that they were the kinsmen of 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl. They said: "If we go out with you, the Bedouins of Tayy will raid our families and our livestock."

When Allah, glorified is He, mentioned those who make excuses, He next mentioned those with valid excuses that exempt them from going out to battle. He began with the excuse rooted in natural creation, saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak﴾, meaning those afflicted with disability, old age, blindness, lameness and the like. Then He mentioned the excuse that arises incidentally, saying: ﴿Nor upon the sick﴾. By "sickness" is meant everything to which the name of sickness applies, linguistically or in the Sharia. It was also said that blindness and lameness and the like are included under sickness.

Then He mentioned the excuse relating to wealth rather than to the body, saying: ﴿Nor upon those who find nothing to spend﴾, meaning they have no property to spend on what they need for equipping themselves for jihad. Allah, glorified is He, thus removed blame from these people and made clear that jihad is dropped from them despite these excuses, and is not obligatory upon them, provided that the condition stated in His words is met: ﴿when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger﴾. The root meaning of *nush* (sincere advice, *nuṣḥ*) is to purify an act from deceit, and from it comes the phrase *tawbah naṣūḥ* (sincere repentance).

The first view is preferable.

His saying *tawallaw* (they turned away) is the response of *idhā* (when). The clause ﴿while their eyes overflow with tears﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause: i.e., they turned away from you when you told them, "I cannot find anything to mount you on," their state being that they were weeping. *Ḥazanan* (in grief) is in the accusative as a verbal noun (*maṣdariyyah*), or as a purpose clause (*'illiyyah*, giving a reason), or as a circumstantial clause (*ḥāliyyah*). *Allā yajidū* (that they should not find) is an object of purpose (*maf'ūl lahu*), and its governing word is *ḥazanan*.

Al-Farra' said: "*An lā*" carries the meaning of *laysa* (not), i.e., grieving that they do not find [anything]. It was also said the meaning is: grieving over their not finding [anything]. It was also said the meaning is: grieving that they do not find what they could spend, neither with themselves nor with you.

Then Allah, glorified is He, mentioned those upon whom the way [of blame] lies among those who stayed behind, saying: ﴿The way [of blame] is only against those who ask your permission﴾, i.e., the path of punishment and censure, ﴿[to stay behind from the raid]﴾, while in fact they are wealthy, meaning they have what would carry them and what they could equip themselves with. The clause ﴿They are content to be with those who remain behind﴾ is a new (*mustaˀnafah*) sentence, as if it were said: what is their situation that they asked permission while they were wealthy? The explanation of *al-khawālif* (those who remain behind) has already been given shortly before.

The clause ﴿And Allah has sealed their hearts﴾ is conjoined to "they are content", meaning: the cause of asking permission despite wealth is two matters. One is contentment with the losing bargain, which is to be with those who remain behind. The second is the sealing by Allah upon their hearts; because of this sealing they do not know what profit is in it for them, so as to choose it over the loss in it.

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Daraqutni in *al-Afrad*, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "I used to write for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and [when] *Bara'ah* [Surah al-Tawbah] was revealed, I was writing down what was revealed to him. I was placing the pen behind my ear when we were commanded to fight. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began looking at what was being revealed to him, when a blind man came and said: 'What about me, O Messenger of Allah, when I am blind?' So there was revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak﴾ to the end of the verse."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, who said: "This verse was revealed concerning Abid ibn Umar al-Muzani."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid, who said: "From His saying ﴿Allah pardon you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 43] down to His saying ﴿There is no way against the good-doers, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾ was revealed concerning the hypocrites."

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying ﴿There is no way against the good-doers﴾, that he said: "There is no way against these people, because they were sincere to Allah and His Messenger, and were unable to endure jihad. So Allah excused them and gave them the same reward as the mujahidin. Have you not heard that Allah says: ﴿Those who sit [at home] among the believers, other than those with a [legitimate] excuse, are not equal to those who strive﴾ [al-Nisa': 95]? So Allah granted to those whom He excused among the weak and those with harm, and to those who find nothing to spend, a reward like that which He granted to the mujahidin."

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿There is no way against the good-doers﴾, that he said: "By Allah, for the people of wrongdoing there is Forgiving and Merciful [God]." 

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Nor upon those who, when they came to you﴾ to the end of the verse, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded [the people] to set out fighting with him. A group of his companions came, among them 'Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal al-Muzani, and they said: 'O Messenger of Allah, carry us.' He said: 'By Allah, I cannot find anything to carry you on.' So they turned away while they were weeping, and it was grievous to them that they should sit out of jihad while they found no expense or mount. So Allah revealed their excuse: ﴿Nor upon those who, when they came to you﴾ to the end of the verse."

Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal, who said: "I do not find the group that Allah mentioned: ﴿Nor upon those who, when they came to you that you might provide them with mounts﴾ to the end of the verse."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: "They were seven men: from Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, Salim ibn 'Umayr; from Banu Waqif, Hirmi ibn 'Amr; from Banu Mazin ibn al-Najjar, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b, known as Abu Layla; from Banu al-Mu'alla, Salman ibn Sakhr; from Banu Harithah, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, Abu 'Abalah; from Banu Salamah, 'Amr ibn Ghanamah and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr al-Muzani." The narrators agreed on some of these seven and differed on others, and lengthy elaboration on this brings little benefit.

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from al-Zuhri, Yazid ibn Ruman, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah and others, that "some men from the Muslims came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they were the weepers. They were seven men from the Ansar and others," then they mentioned their names. In it: "They asked the Messenger of Allah for mounts, and they were people in need. He said: ﴿I cannot find anything to carry you on﴾."

Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from al-Hasan, who said: "Ma'qil ibn Yasar was among the weepers about whom Allah said: ﴿Nor upon those who, when they came to you that you might provide them with mounts﴾ to the end of the verse."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Anas ibn Malik regarding His saying ﴿I cannot find anything to carry you on﴾, that he said: "Water and provisions."

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from 'Ali ibn Salih, who said: "Some elders of Juhaynah told me: 'We met those who asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for mounts, and they said: We only asked him for mounts [in the form of] sandals.'"

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibrahim ibn Adham, from someone who narrated to him, regarding His saying ﴿Nor upon those who, when they came to you that you might provide them with mounts﴾, that he said: "They asked him for nothing but sandals, not for riding beasts."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Hasan ibn Salih regarding the verse, that he said: "They asked him for sandals."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿The way [of blame] is only against those who ask your permission﴾, that he said: "It and what follows it, down to His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah does not approve of the defiantly disobedient people﴾ [al-Tawbah: 96], was revealed concerning the hypocrites."

[p. 592]

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿يَعْتَذِرُونَ إلَيْكُمْ﴾ إخْبارٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ عَنِ المُنافِقِينَ المُتَعَذِّرِينَ بِالباطِلِ بِأنَّهم يَعْتَذِرُونَ إلى المُؤْمِنِينَ إذا رَجَعُوا مِنَ الغَزْوِ، وهَذا كَلامٌ مُسْتَأْنَفٌ.

وإنَّما قالَ: إلَيْهِمْ أيْ إلى المُعْتَذِرِينَ بِالباطِلِ ولَمْ يَقُلْ إلى المَدِينَةِ، لِأنَّ مَدارَ الِاعْتِذارِ هو الرُّجُوعُ إلَيْهِمْ لا الرُّجُوعُ إلى المَدِينَةِ، ورُبَّما يَقَعُ الِاعْتِذارُ عِنْدَ المُلاقاةِ قَبْلَ الوُصُولِ إلَيْها، ثُمَّ أخْبَرَ اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ رَسُولَهُ (ﷺ) بِما يُجِيبُ بِهِ عَلَيْهِمْ، فَقالَ: (p-٥٩٣) ﴿قُلْ لا تَعْتَذِرُوا لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكُمْ﴾ فَنَهاهم أوَّلًا عَنِ الِاعْتِذارِ بِالباطِلِ، ثُمَّ عَلَّلَهُ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكُمْ﴾ أيْ لَنْ نُصَدِّقَكم، كَأنَّهُمُ ادَّعَوْا أنَّهم صادِقُونَ في اعْتِذارِهِمْ، لِأنَّ غَرَضَ المُعْتَذِرِ أنْ يُصَدَّقَ فِيما يَعْتَذِرُ بِهِ، فَإذا عَرَفَ أنَّهُ لا يُصَدَّقُ تَرَكَ الِاعْتِذارَ، وجُمْلَةُ ﴿قَدْ نَبَّأنا اللَّهُ مِن أخْبارِكُمْ﴾ تَعْلِيلِيَّةٌ لِلَّتِي قَبْلَها: أيْ لا يَقَعُ مِنّا تَصْدِيقٌ لَكم لِأنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أعْلَمَنا بِالوَحْيِ ما هو مُنافٍ لِصِدْقِ اعْتِذارِكم، وإنَّما خَصَّ الرَّسُولَ (ﷺ) بِالجَوابِ عَلَيْهِمْ، فَقالَ: ﴿قُلْ لا تَعْتَذِرُوا﴾ مَعَ أنَّ الِاعْتِذارَ مِنهم كائِنٌ إلى جَمِيعِ المُؤْمِنِينَ، لِأنَّهُ (ﷺ) رَأْسُهم، والمُتَوَلِّي لِما يَرِدُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِن جِهَةِ الغَيْرِ، ويُحْتَمَلُ أنْ يَكُونَ المُرادُ بِالضَّمِيرِ في قَوْلِهِ: إلَيْكم هو الرَّسُولَ (ﷺ) عَلى التَّأْوِيلِ المَشْهُورِ في مِثْلِ هَذا.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وسَيَرى اللَّهُ عَمَلَكُمْ﴾ أيْ ما سَتَفْعَلُونَهُ مِنَ الأعْمالِ فِيما بَعْدُ هَلْ تُقْلِعُونَ عَمّا أنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ الآنَ مِنَ الشَّرِّ أمْ تَبْقُونَ عَلَيْهِ؟

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿ورَسُولِهِ﴾ مَعْطُوفٌ عَلى الِاسْمِ الشَّرِيفِ، ووَسَّطَ مَفْعُولَ الرُّؤْيَةِ إيذانًا، بِأنَّ رُؤْيَةَ اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ لِما سَيَفْعَلُونَهُ مِن خَيْرٍ أوْ شَرٍّ هي الَّتِي يَدُورُ عَلَيْها الإثابَةُ أوِ العُقُوبَةُ، وفي جُمْلَةِ ﴿ثُمَّ تُرَدُّونَ إلى عالِمِ الغَيْبِ﴾ إلى آخِرِها تَخْوِيفٌ شَدِيدٌ، لِما هي مُشْتَمِلَةٌ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ التَّهْدِيدِ، ولا سِيَّما ما اشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ مِن وضْعِ الظّاهِرِ مَوْضِعَ المُضْمَرِ، لِإشْعارِ ذَلِكَ بِإحاطَتِهِ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ يَقَعُ مِنهم مِمّا يَكْتُمُونَهُ ويَتَظاهَرُونَ بِهِ، وإخْبارِهِ لَهم بِهِ ومُجازاتِهِمْ عَلَيْهِ.

ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ أنَّ هَؤُلاءِ المُعْتَذِرِينَ بِالباطِلِ سَيُؤَكِّدُونَ ما جاءُوا بِهِ مِنَ الأعْذارِ الباطِلَةِ بِالحَلِفِ عِنْدَ رُجُوعِ المُؤْمِنِينَ إلَيْهِمْ مِنَ الغَزْوِ، وغَرَضُهم مِن هَذا التَّأْكِيدِ هو أنْ يُعْرِضَ المُؤْمِنُونَ عَنْهم فَلا يُوَبِّخُونَهم ولا يُؤاخِذُونَهم بِالتَّخَلُّفِ ويُظْهِرُونَ الرِّضا عَنْهم كَما يُفِيدُهُ ذِكْرُ الرِّضا مِن بَعْدُ، وحَذْفُ المَحْلُوفِ عَلَيْهِ لِكَوْنِ الكَلامِ يَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ، وهو اعْتِذارُهُمُ الباطِلُ، وأمْرُ المُؤْمِنِينَ بِالإعْراضِ عَنْهُمُ المُرادُ بِهِ تَرْكُهم والمُهاجَرَةُ لَهم، لا الرِّضا عَنْهم والصَّفْحُ عَنْ ذُنُوبِهِمْ، كَما تُفِيدُهُ جُمْلَةُ ﴿إنَّهم رِجْسٌ﴾ الواقِعَةُ عِلَّةً لِلْأمْرِ بِالإعْراضِ.

والمَعْنى: أنَّهم في أنْفُسِهِمْ رِجْسٌ لِكَوْنِ جَمِيعِ أعْمالِهِمْ نَجِسَةٌ، فَكَأنَّها قَدْ صَيَّرَتْ ذَواتِهِمْ رِجْسًا، أوْ أنَّهم ذَوُو رِجْسٍ: أيْ ذَوُو أعْمالٍ قَبِيحَةٍ، ومِثْلُهُ ﴿إنَّما المُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ﴾ وهَؤُلاءِ لَمّا كانُوا هَكَذا كانُوا غَيْرَ مُتَأهِّلِينَ لِقَبُولِ الإرْشادِ إلى الخَيْرِ والتَّحْذِيرِ مِنَ الشَّرِّ، فَلَيْسَ لَهم إلّا التَّرْكُ.

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿ومَأْواهم جَهَنَّمُ﴾ مِن تَمامِ التَّعْلِيلِ، فَإنَّ مَن كانَ مِن أهْلِ النّارِ لا يُجْدِي فِيهِ الدُّعاءُ إلى الخَيْرِ، والمَأْوى كُلُّ مَكانٍ يَأْوِي إلَيْهِ الشَّيْءُ لَيْلًا أوْ نَهارًا.

وقَدْ أوى فُلانٌ إلى مَنزِلِهِ يَأْوِي أُوِيًّا وإيواءً، وجَزاءً مَنصُوبٌ عَلى المَصْدَرِيَّةِ، أوْ عَلى العِلِّيَّةِ، والباءُ في ﴿بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ لِلسَّبَبِيَّةِ.

وجُمْلَةُ ﴿يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ﴾ بَدَلٌ مِمّا تَقَدَّمَ.

وحُذِفَ هُنا المَحْلُوفُ بِهِ لِكَوْنِهِ مَعْلُومًا مِمّا سَبَقَ، والمَحْلُوفُ عَلَيْهِ لِمِثْلِ ما تَقَدَّمَ، وبَيَّنَ سُبْحانَهُ أنَّ مَقْصِدَهم بِهَذا الحَلِفِ هو رِضا المُؤْمِنِينَ عَنْهم، ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ ما يُفِيدُ أنَّهُ لا يَجُوزُ الرِّضا عَنْ هَؤُلاءِ المُعْتَذِرِينَ بِالباطِلِ، فَقالَ: ﴿فَإنْ تَرْضَوْا عَنْهُمْ﴾ كَما هو مَطْلُوبُهم مُساعَدَةً لَهم ﴿فَإنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَرْضى عَنِ القَوْمِ الفاسِقِينَ﴾ وإذا كانَ هَذا هو ما يُرِيدُهُ اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ مِن عَدَمِ الرِّضا عَلى هَؤُلاءِ الفَسَقَةِ العُصاةِ، فَيَنْبَغِي لَكم أيُّها المُؤْمِنُونَ أنْ لا تَفْعَلُوا خِلافَ ذَلِكَ، بَلْ واجِبٌ عَلَيْكم أنْ لا تَرْضَوْا عَنْهم عَلى أنَّ رِضاكم عَنْهم لَوْ وقَعَ لَكانَ غَيْرَ مُعْتَدٍّ بِهِ ولا مُفِيدٍ لَهم، والمَقْصُودُ مِن إخْبارِ اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ بِعَدَمِ رِضاهُ عَنْهم نَهْيُ المُؤْمِنِينَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، لِأنَّ الرِّضا عَلى مَن لا يَرْضى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ مِمّا لا يَفْعَلُهُ مُؤْمِنٌ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿الأعْرابُ أشَدُّ كُفْرًا ونِفاقًا﴾ لَمّا ذَكَرَ اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ أحْوالَ المُنافِقِينَ بِالمَدِينَةِ، ذَكَرَ حالَ مَن كانَ خارِجًا عَنْها مِنَ الأعْرابِ، وبَيَّنَ أنَّ كُفْرَهم ونِفاقَهم أشَدُّ مِن كُفْرِ غَيْرِهِمْ ومِن نِفاقِ غَيْرِهِمْ، لِأنَّهم أقْسى قَلْبًا وأغْلَظُ طَبْعًا وأجْفى قَوْلًا، وأبْعَدُ عَنْ سَماعِ كُتُبِ اللَّهِ وما جاءَتْ بِهِ رُسُلُهُ، والأعْرابُ: هم مَن سَكَنَ البَوادِيَ بِخِلافِ العَرَبِ، فَإنَّهُ عامٌّ لِهَذا النَّوْعِ مِن بَنِي آدَمَ سَواءٌ سَكَنُوا البَوادِيَ أوِ القُرى، هَكَذا قالَ أهْلُ اللُّغَةِ، ولِهَذا قالَ سِيبَوَيْهِ: إنَّ الأعْرابَ صِيغَةُ جَمْعٍ ولَيْسَتْ بِصِيغَةِ جَمْعٍ العَرَبُ.

قالَ النَّيْسابُورِيُّ: قالَ أهْلُ اللُّغَةِ: رَجُلٌ عَرَبِيٌّ إذا كانَ نَسَبُهُ إلى العَرَبِ ثابِتًا، وجَمْعُهُ عَرَبٌ، كالمَجُوسِيِّ والمَجُوسِ، واليَهُودِيِّ واليَهُودِ، فالأعْرابِيُّ إذا قِيلَ لَهُ: يا عَرَبِيُّ فَرِحَ، وإذا قِيلَ لِلْعَرَبِيِّ: يا أعْرابِيُّ غَضِبَ، وذَلِكَ أنَّ مَنِ اسْتَوْطَنَ القُرى العَرَبِيَّةَ فَهو عَرَبِيٌّ، ومَن نَزَلَ البادِيَةَ فَهو أعْرابِيٌّ، ولِهَذا لا يَجُوزُ أنْ يُقالَ لِلْمُهاجِرِينَ والأنْصارِ أعْرابٌ، وإنَّما هم عَرَبٌ.

قالَ: قِيلَ: إنَّما سُمِّيَ العَرَبُ عَرَبًا لِأنَّ أوْلادَ إسْماعِيلَ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ) نَشَئُوا بِالعَرَبِ، وهي مِن تِهامَةَ فَنُسِبُوا إلى بَلَدِهِمْ، وكُلُّ مَن يَسْكُنُ جَزِيرَةَ العَرَبِ ويَنْطِقُ بِلِسانِهِمْ فَهو مِنهم، وقِيلَ: لِأنَّ ألْسُنَهم مُعْرِبَةٌ عَمّا في ضَمائِرِهِمْ، ولِما في لِسانِهِمْ مِنَ الفَصاحَةِ والبَلاغَةِ انْتَهى.

وأجْدَرُ مَعْطُوفٌ عَلى (أشَدُّ)، ومَعْناهُ أخْلَقُ، يُقالُ: فُلانٌ جَدِيرٌ بِكَذا: أيْ خَلِيقٌ بِهِ، وأنْتَ جَدِيرٌ أنْ تَفْعَلَ كَذا، والجَمْعُ جُدُرٌ أوْ جَدِيرُونَ، وأصْلُهُ مِن جَدْرِ الحائِطِ، وهو رَفْعُهُ بِالبِناءِ.

والمَعْنى: أنَّهم أحَقُّ وأخْلَقُ بِـ﴿أَلّا يَعْلَمُوا حُدُودَ ما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ مِنَ الشَّرائِعِ والأحْكامِ، لِبُعْدِهِمْ عَنْ مَواطِنِ الأنْبِياءِ ودِيارِ التَّنْزِيلِ ﴿واللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾ بِأحْوالِ مَخْلُوقاتِهِ عَلى العُمُومِ، وهَؤُلاءِ مِنهم ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ فِيما يُجازِيهِمْ بِهِ مِن خَيْرٍ وشَرٍّ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ومِنَ الأعْرابِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ ما يُنْفِقُ مَغْرَمًا﴾ هَذا تَنْوِيعٌ لِجِنْسٍ أوْ نَوْعَيْنِ، الأوَّلُ هَؤُلاءِ، والثّانِي ﴿ومِنَ الأعْرابِ مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ﴾ والمَغْرَمُ الغَرامَةُ والخُسْرانُ، وأصْلُ الغُرْمِ والغَرامَةِ: ما يُنْفِقُهُ الرَّجُلُ ولَيْسَ بِلازِمٍ لَهُ في اعْتِقادِهِ ولَكِنَّهُ يُنْفِقُهُ لِلرِّياءِ والتَّقِيَّةِ، وقِيلَ: أصْلُ الغُرْمِ اللُّزُومُ كَأنَّهُ اعْتَقَدَ أنَّهُ يَلْزَمُهُ لِأمْرٍ خارِجٍ لا تَنْبَعِثُ لَهُ النَّفْسُ.

والدَّوائِرَ جُمَعُ دائِرَةٍ، وهي الحالَةُ المُنْقَلِبَةُ عَنِ النِّعْمَةِ إلى البَلِيَّةِ، وأصْلُها ما يُحِيطُ بِالشَّيْءِ، ودَوائِرُ الزَّمانِ: نُوَبُهُ وتَصارِيفُهُ ودُوَلُهُ، وكَأنَّها لا تُسْتَعْمَلُ إلّا في المَكْرُوهِ، ثُمَّ دَعا سُبْحانَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ دائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ﴾ وجَعَلَ ما دَعا بِهِ عَلَيْهِمْ مُماثِلًا لِما (p-٥٩٤) أرادُوهُ بِالمُسْلِمِينَ، والسَّوْءُ بِالفَتْحِ عِنْدَ جُمْهُورِ القُرّاءِ مَصْدَرٌ أُضِيفَتْ إلَيْهِ الدّائِرَةُ لِلْمُلابَسَةِ كَقَوْلِكَ: رَجُلُ صِدْقٍ.

وقَرَأ أبُو عَمْرٍو وابْنُ كَثِيرٍ بِضَمِّ السِّينِ، وهو المَكْرُوهُ.

قالَ الأخْفَشُ: أيْ عَلَيْهِمْ دائِرَةُ الهَزِيمَةِ والشَّرِّ.

وقالَ الفَرّاءُ: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ دائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ﴾ العَذابُ والبَلاءُ.

قالَ: والسَّوْءُ بِالفَتْحِ مَصْدَرُ سُؤْتُهُ سَوْءًا ومَساءَةً، وبِالضَّمِّ اسْمٌ لا مَصْدَرَ، وهو كَقَوْلِكَ دائِرَةُ البَلاءِ والمَكْرُوهِ. ﴿واللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ﴾ لِما يَقُولُونَهُ ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ بِما يُضْمِرُونَهُ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ومِنَ الأعْرابِ مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ﴾ هَذا النَّوْعُ الثّانِي مِن أنْواعِ الأعْرابِ كَما تَقَدَّمَ: أيْ يُصَدِّقُ بِهِما ﴿ويَتَّخِذُ ما يُنْفِقُ﴾ أيْ يَجْعَلُ ما يُنْفِقُهُ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ قُرُباتٍ وهي جَمْعُ قُرْبَةٍ، وهي: ما يُتَقَرَّبُ بِهِ إلى اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ، تَقُولُ مِنهُ قَرَّبْتُ لِلَّهِ قُرْبانًا، والجَمْعُ قُرَبٌ وقُرُباتٌ.

والمَعْنى: أنَّهُ يَجْعَلُ ما يُنْفِقُهُ سَبَبًا لِحُصُولِ القُرُباتِ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وسَبَبًا لِ﴿صَلَواتِ الرَّسُولِ﴾ أيْ لِدَعَواتِ الرَّسُولِ لَهم، لِأنَّهُ (ﷺ) كانَ يَدْعُو لِلْمُتَصَدِّقِينَ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ إنَّ صَلاتَكَ سَكَنٌ لَهُمْ﴾ [التوبة: ١٠٣]، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ (ﷺ): «اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلى آلِ أبِي أوْفى». ثُمَّ إنَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ بَيَّنَ بِأنَّ ما يُنْفِقُهُ هَذا النَّوْعُ مِنَ الأعْرابِ تَقَرُّبًا إلى اللَّهِ مَقْبُولٌ واقِعٌ عَلى الوَجْهِ الَّذِي أرادُوهُ فَقالَ: ﴿ألا إنَّها قُرْبَةٌ لَهُمْ﴾ فَأخْبَرَ سُبْحانَهُ بِقَبُولِها خَبَرًا مُؤَكَّدًا بِأِسْمِيَّةِ الجُمْلَةِ وحَرْفَيِ التَّنْبِيهِ والتَّحْقِيقِ، وفي هَذا مِنَ التَّطْيِيبِ لِخَواطِرِهِمْ والتَّطْمِينِ لِقُلُوبِهِمْ ما لا يُقادَرُ قَدْرُهُ مَعَ ما يَتَضَمَّنُهُ مِنَ النَّعْيِ عَلى مَن يَتَّخِذُ ما يُنْفِقُ مَغْرَمًا، والتَّوْبِيخِ لَهُ بِأبْلَغِ وجْهٍ، والضَّمِيرُ في ﴿إنَّها﴾ راجِعٌ إلى ما في ﴿ما يُنْفِقُ﴾ وتَأْنِيثُهُ بِاعْتِبارِ الخَبَرِ.

وقَرَأ نافِعٌ، في رِوايَةٍ عَنْهُ ﴿قُرُبَةٌ﴾ بِضَمِّ الرّاءِ، وقَرَأ الباقُونَ بِسُكُونِها تَخْفِيفًا، ثُمَّ فَسَّرَ سُبْحانَهُ القُرْبَةَ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿سَيُدْخِلُهُمُ اللَّهُ في رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ والسِّينُ لِتَحْقِيقِ الوَعْدِ.

وقَدْ أخْرَجَ ابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ، وأبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنِ السُّدِّيِّ، في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿قَدْ نَبَّأنا اللَّهُ مِن أخْبارِكُمْ﴾ قالَ: أخْبَرَنا أنَّكم لَوْ خَرَجْتُمْ ما زِدْتُمُونا إلّا خَبالًا، وفي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَأعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمْ﴾ قالَ: «لَمّا رَجَعَ النَّبِيُّ (ﷺ) قالَ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: لا تُكَلِّمُوهم ولا تُجالِسُوهم، فَأعْرَضُوا عَنْهم كَما أمَرَ اللَّهُ».

وأخْرَجَ أبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنْهُ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿لِتُعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمْ﴾ قالَ: لِتُجاوِزُوا عَنْهم.

وأخْرَجَ أبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنْهُ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿الأعْرابُ أشَدُّ كُفْرًا ونِفاقًا﴾ قالَ: مِن مُنافِقِي المَدِينَةِ ﴿وأجْدَرُ ألّا يَعْلَمُوا حُدُودَ ما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ﴾ يَعْنِي الفَرائِضَ، وما أمَرَ بِهِ مِنَ الجِهادِ.

وأخْرَجَ أبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنِ الكَلْبِيِّ، أنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ نَزَلَتْ في أسَدٍ وغَطَفانَ.

وأخْرَجَ أحْمَدُ، وأبُو داوُدَ والتِّرْمِذِيُّ، والنَّسائِيُّ، والبَيْهَقِيُّ في شُعَبِ الإيمانِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ) قالَ: «مَن سَكَنَ البادِيَةَ جَفا، ومَنِ اتَّبَعَ الصَّيْدَ غَفَلَ، ومَن أتى السُّلْطانَ افْتُتِنَ». وإسْنادُ (isnad: chain of narration) أحْمَدَ هَكَذا: حَدَّثَنا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ مَهْدِيٍّ، حَدَّثَنا سُفْيانُ، عَنْ أبِي مُوسى، عَنْ وهْبِ بْنِ مُنَبِّهٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ) فَذَكَرَهُ.

قالَ في التَّقْرِيبِ (al-Taqrib): وأبُو مُوسى عَنْ وهْبِ بْنِ مُنَبِّهٍ مَجْهُولٌ مِنَ السّادِسَةِ، ووَهِمَ مَن قالَ: إنَّهُ إسْرائِيلُ بْنُ مُوسى، وقالَ التِّرْمِذِيُّ بَعْدَ إخْراجِهِ: حَسَنٌ غَرِيبٌ لا نَعْرِفُهُ إلّا مِن حَدِيثِ الثَّوْرِيِّ.

وأخْرَجَ أبُو داوُدَ والبَيْهَقِيُّ مِن حَدِيثِ أبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قالَ: قالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ): «مَن بَدا جَفا، ومَنِ اتَّبَعَ الصَّيْدَ غَفَلَ، ومَن أتى أبْوابَ السُّلْطانِ افْتُتِنَ، وما ازْدادَ أحَدٌ مِن سُلْطانِهِ قُرْبًا إلّا ازْدادَ مِنَ اللَّهِ بُعْدًا».

وأخْرَجَ أبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنِ الضَّحّاكِ، في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿ومِنَ الأعْرابِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ ما يُنْفِقُ مَغْرَمًا﴾ قالَ: يَعْنِي بِالمَغْرَمِ أنَّهُ لا يَرْجُو لَهُ ثَوابًا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ ولا مُجازاةً، وإنَّما يُعْطِي مَن يُعْطِي مِنَ الصَّدَقاتِ كَرْهًا ﴿ويَتَرَبَّصُ بِكُمُ الدَّوائِرَ﴾ الهِلْكاتِ.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Zayd concerning the verse, he said: "These are the hypocrites among the Bedouins (al-A'rab), who spend only for show (riya'), out of fear that they will be made to go on raids, fight and battle, and they regard their expenditures as a burden (maghram)."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿And among the Bedouins is one who believes in Allah﴾, he said: "They are the Banu Muqarrin of Muzayna, and they are the ones about whom Allah said: ﴿Nor is there blame upon those who came to you that you might provide them with mounts﴾ [al-Tawbah: 92], and so on, the verse."

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'qil, who said: "We were ten sons of Muqarrin, and the verse ﴿And among the Bedouins is one who believes in Allah﴾, and so on, was revealed concerning us."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿and the prayers of the Messenger﴾, that it means the Prophet's (ﷺ) seeking of forgiveness (istighfar).

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿يَعْتَذِرُونَ إلَيْكُمْ﴾ إخْبارٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ عَنِ المُنافِقِينَ المُتَعَذِّرِينَ بِالباطِلِ بِأنَّهم يَعْتَذِرُونَ إلى المُؤْمِنِينَ إذا رَجَعُوا مِنَ الغَزْوِ، وهَذا كَلامٌ مُسْتَأْنَفٌ.

وإنَّما قالَ: إلَيْهِمْ أيْ إلى المُعْتَذِرِينَ بِالباطِلِ ولَمْ يَقُلْ إلى المَدِينَةِ، لِأنَّ مَدارَ الِاعْتِذارِ هو الرُّجُوعُ إلَيْهِمْ لا الرُّجُوعُ إلى المَدِينَةِ، ورُبَّما يَقَعُ الِاعْتِذارُ عِنْدَ المُلاقاةِ قَبْلَ الوُصُولِ إلَيْها، ثُمَّ أخْبَرَ اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ رَسُولَهُ (ﷺ) بِما يُجِيبُ بِهِ عَلَيْهِمْ، فَقالَ: (p-٥٩٣) ﴿قُلْ لا تَعْتَذِرُوا لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكُمْ﴾ فَنَهاهم أوَّلًا عَنِ الِاعْتِذارِ بِالباطِلِ، ثُمَّ عَلَّلَهُ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكُمْ﴾ أيْ لَنْ نُصَدِّقَكم، كَأنَّهُمُ ادَّعَوْا أنَّهم صادِقُونَ في اعْتِذارِهِمْ، لِأنَّ غَرَضَ المُعْتَذِرِ أنْ يُصَدَّقَ فِيما يَعْتَذِرُ بِهِ، فَإذا عَرَفَ أنَّهُ لا يُصَدَّقُ تَرَكَ الِاعْتِذارَ، وجُمْلَةُ ﴿قَدْ نَبَّأنا اللَّهُ مِن أخْبارِكُمْ﴾ تَعْلِيلِيَّةٌ لِلَّتِي قَبْلَها: أيْ لا يَقَعُ مِنّا تَصْدِيقٌ لَكم لِأنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أعْلَمَنا بِالوَحْيِ ما هو مُنافٍ لِصِدْقِ اعْتِذارِكم، وإنَّما خَصَّ الرَّسُولَ (ﷺ) بِالجَوابِ عَلَيْهِمْ، فَقالَ: ﴿قُلْ لا تَعْتَذِرُوا﴾ مَعَ أنَّ الِاعْتِذارَ مِنهم كائِنٌ إلى جَمِيعِ المُؤْمِنِينَ، لِأنَّهُ (ﷺ) رَأْسُهم، والمُتَوَلِّي لِما يَرِدُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِن جِهَةِ الغَيْرِ، ويُحْتَمَلُ أنْ يَكُونَ المُرادُ بِالضَّمِيرِ في قَوْلِهِ: إلَيْكم هو الرَّسُولَ (ﷺ) عَلى التَّأْوِيلِ المَشْهُورِ في مِثْلِ هَذا.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وسَيَرى اللَّهُ عَمَلَكُمْ﴾ أيْ ما سَتَفْعَلُونَهُ مِنَ الأعْمالِ فِيما بَعْدُ هَلْ تُقْلِعُونَ عَمّا أنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ الآنَ مِنَ الشَّرِّ أمْ تَبْقُونَ عَلَيْهِ؟

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿ورَسُولِهِ﴾ مَعْطُوفٌ عَلى الِاسْمِ الشَّرِيفِ، ووَسَّطَ مَفْعُولَ الرُّؤْيَةِ إيذانًا، بِأنَّ رُؤْيَةَ اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ لِما سَيَفْعَلُونَهُ مِن خَيْرٍ أوْ شَرٍّ هي الَّتِي يَدُورُ عَلَيْها الإثابَةُ أوِ العُقُوبَةُ، وفي جُمْلَةِ ﴿ثُمَّ تُرَدُّونَ إلى عالِمِ الغَيْبِ﴾ إلى آخِرِها تَخْوِيفٌ شَدِيدٌ، لِما هي مُشْتَمِلَةٌ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ التَّهْدِيدِ، ولا سِيَّما ما اشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ مِن وضْعِ الظّاهِرِ مَوْضِعَ المُضْمَرِ، لِإشْعارِ ذَلِكَ بِإحاطَتِهِ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ يَقَعُ مِنهم مِمّا يَكْتُمُونَهُ ويَتَظاهَرُونَ بِهِ، وإخْبارِهِ لَهم بِهِ ومُجازاتِهِمْ عَلَيْهِ.

ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ أنَّ هَؤُلاءِ المُعْتَذِرِينَ بِالباطِلِ سَيُؤَكِّدُونَ ما جاءُوا بِهِ مِنَ الأعْذارِ الباطِلَةِ بِالحَلِفِ عِنْدَ رُجُوعِ المُؤْمِنِينَ إلَيْهِمْ مِنَ الغَزْوِ، وغَرَضُهم مِن هَذا التَّأْكِيدِ هو أنْ يُعْرِضَ المُؤْمِنُونَ عَنْهم فَلا يُوَبِّخُونَهم ولا يُؤاخِذُونَهم بِالتَّخَلُّفِ ويُظْهِرُونَ الرِّضا عَنْهم كَما يُفِيدُهُ ذِكْرُ الرِّضا مِن بَعْدُ، وحَذْفُ المَحْلُوفِ عَلَيْهِ لِكَوْنِ الكَلامِ يَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ، وهو اعْتِذارُهُمُ الباطِلُ، وأمْرُ المُؤْمِنِينَ بِالإعْراضِ عَنْهُمُ المُرادُ بِهِ تَرْكُهم والمُهاجَرَةُ لَهم، لا الرِّضا عَنْهم والصَّفْحُ عَنْ ذُنُوبِهِمْ، كَما تُفِيدُهُ جُمْلَةُ ﴿إنَّهم رِجْسٌ﴾ الواقِعَةُ عِلَّةً لِلْأمْرِ بِالإعْراضِ.

والمَعْنى: أنَّهم في أنْفُسِهِمْ رِجْسٌ لِكَوْنِ جَمِيعِ أعْمالِهِمْ نَجِسَةٌ، فَكَأنَّها قَدْ صَيَّرَتْ ذَواتِهِمْ رِجْسًا، أوْ أنَّهم ذَوُو رِجْسٍ: أيْ ذَوُو أعْمالٍ قَبِيحَةٍ، ومِثْلُهُ ﴿إنَّما المُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ﴾ وهَؤُلاءِ لَمّا كانُوا هَكَذا كانُوا غَيْرَ مُتَأهِّلِينَ لِقَبُولِ الإرْشادِ إلى الخَيْرِ والتَّحْذِيرِ مِنَ الشَّرِّ، فَلَيْسَ لَهم إلّا التَّرْكُ.

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿ومَأْواهم جَهَنَّمُ﴾ مِن تَمامِ التَّعْلِيلِ، فَإنَّ مَن كانَ مِن أهْلِ النّارِ لا يُجْدِي فِيهِ الدُّعاءُ إلى الخَيْرِ، والمَأْوى كُلُّ مَكانٍ يَأْوِي إلَيْهِ الشَّيْءُ لَيْلًا أوْ نَهارًا.

وقَدْ أوى فُلانٌ إلى مَنزِلِهِ يَأْوِي أُوِيًّا وإيواءً، وجَزاءً مَنصُوبٌ عَلى المَصْدَرِيَّةِ، أوْ عَلى العِلِّيَّةِ، والباءُ في ﴿بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ لِلسَّبَبِيَّةِ.

وجُمْلَةُ ﴿يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ﴾ بَدَلٌ مِمّا تَقَدَّمَ.

وحُذِفَ هُنا المَحْلُوفُ بِهِ لِكَوْنِهِ مَعْلُومًا مِمّا سَبَقَ، والمَحْلُوفُ عَلَيْهِ لِمِثْلِ ما تَقَدَّمَ، وبَيَّنَ سُبْحانَهُ أنَّ مَقْصِدَهم بِهَذا الحَلِفِ هو رِضا المُؤْمِنِينَ عَنْهم، ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ ما يُفِيدُ أنَّهُ لا يَجُوزُ الرِّضا عَنْ هَؤُلاءِ المُعْتَذِرِينَ بِالباطِلِ، فَقالَ: ﴿فَإنْ تَرْضَوْا عَنْهُمْ﴾ كَما هو مَطْلُوبُهم مُساعَدَةً لَهم ﴿فَإنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَرْضى عَنِ القَوْمِ الفاسِقِينَ﴾ وإذا كانَ هَذا هو ما يُرِيدُهُ اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ مِن عَدَمِ الرِّضا عَلى هَؤُلاءِ الفَسَقَةِ العُصاةِ، فَيَنْبَغِي لَكم أيُّها المُؤْمِنُونَ أنْ لا تَفْعَلُوا خِلافَ ذَلِكَ، بَلْ واجِبٌ عَلَيْكم أنْ لا تَرْضَوْا عَنْهم عَلى أنَّ رِضاكم عَنْهم لَوْ وقَعَ لَكانَ غَيْرَ مُعْتَدٍّ بِهِ ولا مُفِيدٍ لَهم، والمَقْصُودُ مِن إخْبارِ اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ بِعَدَمِ رِضاهُ عَنْهم نَهْيُ المُؤْمِنِينَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، لِأنَّ الرِّضا عَلى مَن لا يَرْضى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ مِمّا لا يَفْعَلُهُ مُؤْمِنٌ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿الأعْرابُ أشَدُّ كُفْرًا ونِفاقًا﴾ لَمّا ذَكَرَ اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ أحْوالَ المُنافِقِينَ بِالمَدِينَةِ، ذَكَرَ حالَ مَن كانَ خارِجًا عَنْها مِنَ الأعْرابِ، وبَيَّنَ أنَّ كُفْرَهم ونِفاقَهم أشَدُّ مِن كُفْرِ غَيْرِهِمْ ومِن نِفاقِ غَيْرِهِمْ، لِأنَّهم أقْسى قَلْبًا وأغْلَظُ طَبْعًا وأجْفى قَوْلًا، وأبْعَدُ عَنْ سَماعِ كُتُبِ اللَّهِ وما جاءَتْ بِهِ رُسُلُهُ، والأعْرابُ: هم مَن سَكَنَ البَوادِيَ بِخِلافِ العَرَبِ، فَإنَّهُ عامٌّ لِهَذا النَّوْعِ مِن بَنِي آدَمَ سَواءٌ سَكَنُوا البَوادِيَ أوِ القُرى، هَكَذا قالَ أهْلُ اللُّغَةِ، ولِهَذا قالَ سِيبَوَيْهِ: إنَّ الأعْرابَ صِيغَةُ جَمْعٍ ولَيْسَتْ بِصِيغَةِ جَمْعٍ العَرَبُ.

قالَ النَّيْسابُورِيُّ: قالَ أهْلُ اللُّغَةِ: رَجُلٌ عَرَبِيٌّ إذا كانَ نَسَبُهُ إلى العَرَبِ ثابِتًا، وجَمْعُهُ عَرَبٌ، كالمَجُوسِيِّ والمَجُوسِ، واليَهُودِيِّ واليَهُودِ، فالأعْرابِيُّ إذا قِيلَ لَهُ: يا عَرَبِيُّ فَرِحَ، وإذا قِيلَ لِلْعَرَبِيِّ: يا أعْرابِيُّ غَضِبَ، وذَلِكَ أنَّ مَنِ اسْتَوْطَنَ القُرى العَرَبِيَّةَ فَهو عَرَبِيٌّ، ومَن نَزَلَ البادِيَةَ فَهو أعْرابِيٌّ، ولِهَذا لا يَجُوزُ أنْ يُقالَ لِلْمُهاجِرِينَ والأنْصارِ أعْرابٌ، وإنَّما هم عَرَبٌ.

قالَ: قِيلَ: إنَّما سُمِّيَ العَرَبُ عَرَبًا لِأنَّ أوْلادَ إسْماعِيلَ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ) نَشَئُوا بِالعَرَبِ، وهي مِن تِهامَةَ فَنُسِبُوا إلى بَلَدِهِمْ، وكُلُّ مَن يَسْكُنُ جَزِيرَةَ العَرَبِ ويَنْطِقُ بِلِسانِهِمْ فَهو مِنهم، وقِيلَ: لِأنَّ ألْسُنَهم مُعْرِبَةٌ عَمّا في ضَمائِرِهِمْ، ولِما في لِسانِهِمْ مِنَ الفَصاحَةِ والبَلاغَةِ انْتَهى.

وأجْدَرُ مَعْطُوفٌ عَلى (أشَدُّ)، ومَعْناهُ أخْلَقُ، يُقالُ: فُلانٌ جَدِيرٌ بِكَذا: أيْ خَلِيقٌ بِهِ، وأنْتَ جَدِيرٌ أنْ تَفْعَلَ كَذا، والجَمْعُ جُدُرٌ أوْ جَدِيرُونَ، وأصْلُهُ مِن جَدْرِ الحائِطِ، وهو رَفْعُهُ بِالبِناءِ.

والمَعْنى: أنَّهم أحَقُّ وأخْلَقُ بِـ﴿أَلّا يَعْلَمُوا حُدُودَ ما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ مِنَ الشَّرائِعِ والأحْكامِ، لِبُعْدِهِمْ عَنْ مَواطِنِ الأنْبِياءِ ودِيارِ التَّنْزِيلِ ﴿واللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾ بِأحْوالِ مَخْلُوقاتِهِ عَلى العُمُومِ، وهَؤُلاءِ مِنهم ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ فِيما يُجازِيهِمْ بِهِ مِن خَيْرٍ وشَرٍّ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ومِنَ الأعْرابِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ ما يُنْفِقُ مَغْرَمًا﴾ هَذا تَنْوِيعٌ لِجِنْسٍ أوْ نَوْعَيْنِ، الأوَّلُ هَؤُلاءِ، والثّانِي ﴿ومِنَ الأعْرابِ مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ﴾ والمَغْرَمُ الغَرامَةُ والخُسْرانُ، وأصْلُ الغُرْمِ والغَرامَةِ: ما يُنْفِقُهُ الرَّجُلُ ولَيْسَ بِلازِمٍ لَهُ في اعْتِقادِهِ ولَكِنَّهُ يُنْفِقُهُ لِلرِّياءِ والتَّقِيَّةِ، وقِيلَ: أصْلُ الغُرْمِ اللُّزُومُ كَأنَّهُ اعْتَقَدَ أنَّهُ يَلْزَمُهُ لِأمْرٍ خارِجٍ لا تَنْبَعِثُ لَهُ النَّفْسُ.

والدَّوائِرَ جُمَعُ دائِرَةٍ، وهي الحالَةُ المُنْقَلِبَةُ عَنِ النِّعْمَةِ إلى البَلِيَّةِ، وأصْلُها ما يُحِيطُ بِالشَّيْءِ، ودَوائِرُ الزَّمانِ: نُوَبُهُ وتَصارِيفُهُ ودُوَلُهُ، وكَأنَّها لا تُسْتَعْمَلُ إلّا في المَكْرُوهِ، ثُمَّ دَعا سُبْحانَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ دائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ﴾ وجَعَلَ ما دَعا بِهِ عَلَيْهِمْ مُماثِلًا لِما (p-٥٩٤) أرادُوهُ بِالمُسْلِمِينَ، والسَّوْءُ بِالفَتْحِ عِنْدَ جُمْهُورِ القُرّاءِ مَصْدَرٌ أُضِيفَتْ إلَيْهِ الدّائِرَةُ لِلْمُلابَسَةِ كَقَوْلِكَ: رَجُلُ صِدْقٍ.

وقَرَأ أبُو عَمْرٍو وابْنُ كَثِيرٍ بِضَمِّ السِّينِ، وهو المَكْرُوهُ.

قالَ الأخْفَشُ: أيْ عَلَيْهِمْ دائِرَةُ الهَزِيمَةِ والشَّرِّ.

وقالَ الفَرّاءُ: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ دائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ﴾ العَذابُ والبَلاءُ.

قالَ: والسَّوْءُ بِالفَتْحِ مَصْدَرُ سُؤْتُهُ سَوْءًا ومَساءَةً، وبِالضَّمِّ اسْمٌ لا مَصْدَرَ، وهو كَقَوْلِكَ دائِرَةُ البَلاءِ والمَكْرُوهِ. ﴿واللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ﴾ لِما يَقُولُونَهُ ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ بِما يُضْمِرُونَهُ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ومِنَ الأعْرابِ مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ﴾ هَذا النَّوْعُ الثّانِي مِن أنْواعِ الأعْرابِ كَما تَقَدَّمَ: أيْ يُصَدِّقُ بِهِما ﴿ويَتَّخِذُ ما يُنْفِقُ﴾ أيْ يَجْعَلُ ما يُنْفِقُهُ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ قُرُباتٍ وهي جَمْعُ قُرْبَةٍ، وهي: ما يُتَقَرَّبُ بِهِ إلى اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ، تَقُولُ مِنهُ قَرَّبْتُ لِلَّهِ قُرْبانًا، والجَمْعُ قُرَبٌ وقُرُباتٌ.

والمَعْنى: أنَّهُ يَجْعَلُ ما يُنْفِقُهُ سَبَبًا لِحُصُولِ القُرُباتِ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وسَبَبًا لِ﴿صَلَواتِ الرَّسُولِ﴾ أيْ لِدَعَواتِ الرَّسُولِ لَهم، لِأنَّهُ (ﷺ) كانَ يَدْعُو لِلْمُتَصَدِّقِينَ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ إنَّ صَلاتَكَ سَكَنٌ لَهُمْ﴾ [التوبة: ١٠٣]، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ (ﷺ): «اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلى آلِ أبِي أوْفى». ثُمَّ إنَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ بَيَّنَ بِأنَّ ما يُنْفِقُهُ هَذا النَّوْعُ مِنَ الأعْرابِ تَقَرُّبًا إلى اللَّهِ مَقْبُولٌ واقِعٌ عَلى الوَجْهِ الَّذِي أرادُوهُ فَقالَ: ﴿ألا إنَّها قُرْبَةٌ لَهُمْ﴾ فَأخْبَرَ سُبْحانَهُ بِقَبُولِها خَبَرًا مُؤَكَّدًا بِأِسْمِيَّةِ الجُمْلَةِ وحَرْفَيِ التَّنْبِيهِ والتَّحْقِيقِ، وفي هَذا مِنَ التَّطْيِيبِ لِخَواطِرِهِمْ والتَّطْمِينِ لِقُلُوبِهِمْ ما لا يُقادَرُ قَدْرُهُ مَعَ ما يَتَضَمَّنُهُ مِنَ النَّعْيِ عَلى مَن يَتَّخِذُ ما يُنْفِقُ مَغْرَمًا، والتَّوْبِيخِ لَهُ بِأبْلَغِ وجْهٍ، والضَّمِيرُ في ﴿إنَّها﴾ راجِعٌ إلى ما في ﴿ما يُنْفِقُ﴾ وتَأْنِيثُهُ بِاعْتِبارِ الخَبَرِ.

وقَرَأ نافِعٌ، في رِوايَةٍ عَنْهُ ﴿قُرُبَةٌ﴾ بِضَمِّ الرّاءِ، وقَرَأ الباقُونَ بِسُكُونِها تَخْفِيفًا، ثُمَّ فَسَّرَ سُبْحانَهُ القُرْبَةَ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿سَيُدْخِلُهُمُ اللَّهُ في رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ والسِّينُ لِتَحْقِيقِ الوَعْدِ.

وقَدْ أخْرَجَ ابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ، وأبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنِ السُّدِّيِّ، في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿قَدْ نَبَّأنا اللَّهُ مِن أخْبارِكُمْ﴾ قالَ: أخْبَرَنا أنَّكم لَوْ خَرَجْتُمْ ما زِدْتُمُونا إلّا خَبالًا، وفي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَأعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمْ﴾ قالَ: «لَمّا رَجَعَ النَّبِيُّ (ﷺ) قالَ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: لا تُكَلِّمُوهم ولا تُجالِسُوهم، فَأعْرَضُوا عَنْهم كَما أمَرَ اللَّهُ».

وأخْرَجَ أبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنْهُ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿لِتُعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمْ﴾ قالَ: لِتُجاوِزُوا عَنْهم.

وأخْرَجَ أبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنْهُ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿الأعْرابُ أشَدُّ كُفْرًا ونِفاقًا﴾ قالَ: مِن مُنافِقِي المَدِينَةِ ﴿وأجْدَرُ ألّا يَعْلَمُوا حُدُودَ ما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ﴾ يَعْنِي الفَرائِضَ، وما أمَرَ بِهِ مِنَ الجِهادِ.

وأخْرَجَ أبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنِ الكَلْبِيِّ، أنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ نَزَلَتْ في أسَدٍ وغَطَفانَ.

وأخْرَجَ أحْمَدُ، وأبُو داوُدَ والتِّرْمِذِيُّ، والنَّسائِيُّ، والبَيْهَقِيُّ في شُعَبِ الإيمانِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ) قالَ: «مَن سَكَنَ البادِيَةَ جَفا، ومَنِ اتَّبَعَ الصَّيْدَ غَفَلَ، ومَن أتى السُّلْطانَ افْتُتِنَ». وإسْنادُ (isnad: chain of narration) أحْمَدَ هَكَذا: حَدَّثَنا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ مَهْدِيٍّ، حَدَّثَنا سُفْيانُ، عَنْ أبِي مُوسى، عَنْ وهْبِ بْنِ مُنَبِّهٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ) فَذَكَرَهُ.

قالَ في التَّقْرِيبِ (al-Taqrib): وأبُو مُوسى عَنْ وهْبِ بْنِ مُنَبِّهٍ مَجْهُولٌ مِنَ السّادِسَةِ، ووَهِمَ مَن قالَ: إنَّهُ إسْرائِيلُ بْنُ مُوسى، وقالَ التِّرْمِذِيُّ بَعْدَ إخْراجِهِ: حَسَنٌ غَرِيبٌ لا نَعْرِفُهُ إلّا مِن حَدِيثِ الثَّوْرِيِّ.

وأخْرَجَ أبُو داوُدَ والبَيْهَقِيُّ مِن حَدِيثِ أبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قالَ: قالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ): «مَن بَدا جَفا، ومَنِ اتَّبَعَ الصَّيْدَ غَفَلَ، ومَن أتى أبْوابَ السُّلْطانِ افْتُتِنَ، وما ازْدادَ أحَدٌ مِن سُلْطانِهِ قُرْبًا إلّا ازْدادَ مِنَ اللَّهِ بُعْدًا».

وأخْرَجَ أبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنِ الضَّحّاكِ، في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿ومِنَ الأعْرابِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ ما يُنْفِقُ مَغْرَمًا﴾ قالَ: يَعْنِي بِالمَغْرَمِ أنَّهُ لا يَرْجُو لَهُ ثَوابًا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ ولا مُجازاةً، وإنَّما يُعْطِي مَن يُعْطِي مِنَ الصَّدَقاتِ كَرْهًا ﴿ويَتَرَبَّصُ بِكُمُ الدَّوائِرَ﴾ الهِلْكاتِ.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Zayd concerning the verse, he said: "These are the hypocrites among the Bedouins (al-A'rab), who spend only for show (riya'), out of fear that they will be made to go on raids, fight and battle, and they regard their expenditures as a burden (maghram)."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿And among the Bedouins is one who believes in Allah﴾, he said: "They are the Banu Muqarrin of Muzayna, and they are the ones about whom Allah said: ﴿Nor is there blame upon those who came to you that you might provide them with mounts﴾ [al-Tawbah: 92], and so on, the verse."

Ibn Jarir and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'qil, who said: "We were ten sons of Muqarrin, and the verse ﴿And among the Bedouins is one who believes in Allah﴾, and so on, was revealed concerning us."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿and the prayers of the Messenger﴾, that it means the Prophet's (ﷺ) seeking of forgiveness (istighfar).

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿يَعْتَذِرُونَ إلَيْكُمْ﴾ إخْبارٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ عَنِ المُنافِقِينَ المُتَعَذِّرِينَ بِالباطِلِ بِأنَّهم يَعْتَذِرُونَ إلى المُؤْمِنِينَ إذا رَجَعُوا مِنَ الغَزْوِ، وهَذا كَلامٌ مُسْتَأْنَفٌ.

وإنَّما قالَ: إلَيْهِمْ أيْ إلى المُعْتَذِرِينَ بِالباطِلِ ولَمْ يَقُلْ إلى المَدِينَةِ، لِأنَّ مَدارَ الِاعْتِذارِ هو الرُّجُوعُ إلَيْهِمْ لا الرُّجُوعُ إلى المَدِينَةِ، ورُبَّما يَقَعُ الِاعْتِذارُ عِنْدَ المُلاقاةِ قَبْلَ الوُصُولِ إلَيْها، ثُمَّ أخْبَرَ اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ رَسُولَهُ (ﷺ) بِما يُجِيبُ بِهِ عَلَيْهِمْ، فَقالَ: (p-٥٩٣) ﴿قُلْ لا تَعْتَذِرُوا لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكُمْ﴾ فَنَهاهم أوَّلًا عَنِ الِاعْتِذارِ بِالباطِلِ، ثُمَّ عَلَّلَهُ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكُمْ﴾ أيْ لَنْ نُصَدِّقَكم، كَأنَّهُمُ ادَّعَوْا أنَّهم صادِقُونَ في اعْتِذارِهِمْ، لِأنَّ غَرَضَ المُعْتَذِرِ أنْ يُصَدَّقَ فِيما يَعْتَذِرُ بِهِ، فَإذا عَرَفَ أنَّهُ لا يُصَدَّقُ تَرَكَ الِاعْتِذارَ، وجُمْلَةُ ﴿قَدْ نَبَّأنا اللَّهُ مِن أخْبارِكُمْ﴾ تَعْلِيلِيَّةٌ لِلَّتِي قَبْلَها: أيْ لا يَقَعُ مِنّا تَصْدِيقٌ لَكم لِأنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أعْلَمَنا بِالوَحْيِ ما هو مُنافٍ لِصِدْقِ اعْتِذارِكم، وإنَّما خَصَّ الرَّسُولَ (ﷺ) بِالجَوابِ عَلَيْهِمْ، فَقالَ: ﴿قُلْ لا تَعْتَذِرُوا﴾ مَعَ أنَّ الِاعْتِذارَ مِنهم كائِنٌ إلى جَمِيعِ المُؤْمِنِينَ، لِأنَّهُ (ﷺ) رَأْسُهم، والمُتَوَلِّي لِما يَرِدُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِن جِهَةِ الغَيْرِ، ويُحْتَمَلُ أنْ يَكُونَ المُرادُ بِالضَّمِيرِ في قَوْلِهِ: إلَيْكم هو الرَّسُولَ (ﷺ) عَلى التَّأْوِيلِ المَشْهُورِ في مِثْلِ هَذا.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وسَيَرى اللَّهُ عَمَلَكُمْ﴾ أيْ ما سَتَفْعَلُونَهُ مِنَ الأعْمالِ فِيما بَعْدُ هَلْ تُقْلِعُونَ عَمّا أنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ الآنَ مِنَ الشَّرِّ أمْ تَبْقُونَ عَلَيْهِ؟

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿ورَسُولِهِ﴾ مَعْطُوفٌ عَلى الِاسْمِ الشَّرِيفِ، ووَسَّطَ مَفْعُولَ الرُّؤْيَةِ إيذانًا، بِأنَّ رُؤْيَةَ اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ لِما سَيَفْعَلُونَهُ مِن خَيْرٍ أوْ شَرٍّ هي الَّتِي يَدُورُ عَلَيْها الإثابَةُ أوِ العُقُوبَةُ، وفي جُمْلَةِ ﴿ثُمَّ تُرَدُّونَ إلى عالِمِ الغَيْبِ﴾ إلى آخِرِها تَخْوِيفٌ شَدِيدٌ، لِما هي مُشْتَمِلَةٌ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ التَّهْدِيدِ، ولا سِيَّما ما اشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ مِن وضْعِ الظّاهِرِ مَوْضِعَ المُضْمَرِ، لِإشْعارِ ذَلِكَ بِإحاطَتِهِ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ يَقَعُ مِنهم مِمّا يَكْتُمُونَهُ ويَتَظاهَرُونَ بِهِ، وإخْبارِهِ لَهم بِهِ ومُجازاتِهِمْ عَلَيْهِ.

ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ أنَّ هَؤُلاءِ المُعْتَذِرِينَ بِالباطِلِ سَيُؤَكِّدُونَ ما جاءُوا بِهِ مِنَ الأعْذارِ الباطِلَةِ بِالحَلِفِ عِنْدَ رُجُوعِ المُؤْمِنِينَ إلَيْهِمْ مِنَ الغَزْوِ، وغَرَضُهم مِن هَذا التَّأْكِيدِ هو أنْ يُعْرِضَ المُؤْمِنُونَ عَنْهم فَلا يُوَبِّخُونَهم ولا يُؤاخِذُونَهم بِالتَّخَلُّفِ ويُظْهِرُونَ الرِّضا عَنْهم كَما يُفِيدُهُ ذِكْرُ الرِّضا مِن بَعْدُ، وحَذْفُ المَحْلُوفِ عَلَيْهِ لِكَوْنِ الكَلامِ يَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ، وهو اعْتِذارُهُمُ الباطِلُ، وأمْرُ المُؤْمِنِينَ بِالإعْراضِ عَنْهُمُ المُرادُ بِهِ تَرْكُهم والمُهاجَرَةُ لَهم، لا الرِّضا عَنْهم والصَّفْحُ عَنْ ذُنُوبِهِمْ، كَما تُفِيدُهُ جُمْلَةُ ﴿إنَّهم رِجْسٌ﴾ الواقِعَةُ عِلَّةً لِلْأمْرِ بِالإعْراضِ.

والمَعْنى: أنَّهم في أنْفُسِهِمْ رِجْسٌ لِكَوْنِ جَمِيعِ أعْمالِهِمْ نَجِسَةٌ، فَكَأنَّها قَدْ صَيَّرَتْ ذَواتِهِمْ رِجْسًا، أوْ أنَّهم ذَوُو رِجْسٍ: أيْ ذَوُو أعْمالٍ قَبِيحَةٍ، ومِثْلُهُ ﴿إنَّما المُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ﴾ وهَؤُلاءِ لَمّا كانُوا هَكَذا كانُوا غَيْرَ مُتَأهِّلِينَ لِقَبُولِ الإرْشادِ إلى الخَيْرِ والتَّحْذِيرِ مِنَ الشَّرِّ، فَلَيْسَ لَهم إلّا التَّرْكُ.

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿ومَأْواهم جَهَنَّمُ﴾ مِن تَمامِ التَّعْلِيلِ، فَإنَّ مَن كانَ مِن أهْلِ النّارِ لا يُجْدِي فِيهِ الدُّعاءُ إلى الخَيْرِ، والمَأْوى كُلُّ مَكانٍ يَأْوِي إلَيْهِ الشَّيْءُ لَيْلًا أوْ نَهارًا.

وقَدْ أوى فُلانٌ إلى مَنزِلِهِ يَأْوِي أُوِيًّا وإيواءً، وجَزاءً مَنصُوبٌ عَلى المَصْدَرِيَّةِ، أوْ عَلى العِلِّيَّةِ، والباءُ في ﴿بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ لِلسَّبَبِيَّةِ.

وجُمْلَةُ ﴿يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ﴾ بَدَلٌ مِمّا تَقَدَّمَ.

وحُذِفَ هُنا المَحْلُوفُ بِهِ لِكَوْنِهِ مَعْلُومًا مِمّا سَبَقَ، والمَحْلُوفُ عَلَيْهِ لِمِثْلِ ما تَقَدَّمَ، وبَيَّنَ سُبْحانَهُ أنَّ مَقْصِدَهم بِهَذا الحَلِفِ هو رِضا المُؤْمِنِينَ عَنْهم، ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ ما يُفِيدُ أنَّهُ لا يَجُوزُ الرِّضا عَنْ هَؤُلاءِ المُعْتَذِرِينَ بِالباطِلِ، فَقالَ: ﴿فَإنْ تَرْضَوْا عَنْهُمْ﴾ كَما هو مَطْلُوبُهم مُساعَدَةً لَهم ﴿فَإنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَرْضى عَنِ القَوْمِ الفاسِقِينَ﴾ وإذا كانَ هَذا هو ما يُرِيدُهُ اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ مِن عَدَمِ الرِّضا عَلى هَؤُلاءِ الفَسَقَةِ العُصاةِ، فَيَنْبَغِي لَكم أيُّها المُؤْمِنُونَ أنْ لا تَفْعَلُوا خِلافَ ذَلِكَ، بَلْ واجِبٌ عَلَيْكم أنْ لا تَرْضَوْا عَنْهم عَلى أنَّ رِضاكم عَنْهم لَوْ وقَعَ لَكانَ غَيْرَ مُعْتَدٍّ بِهِ ولا مُفِيدٍ لَهم، والمَقْصُودُ مِن إخْبارِ اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ بِعَدَمِ رِضاهُ عَنْهم نَهْيُ المُؤْمِنِينَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، لِأنَّ الرِّضا عَلى مَن لا يَرْضى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ مِمّا لا يَفْعَلُهُ مُؤْمِنٌ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿الأعْرابُ أشَدُّ كُفْرًا ونِفاقًا﴾ لَمّا ذَكَرَ اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ أحْوالَ المُنافِقِينَ بِالمَدِينَةِ، ذَكَرَ حالَ مَن كانَ خارِجًا عَنْها مِنَ الأعْرابِ، وبَيَّنَ أنَّ كُفْرَهم ونِفاقَهم أشَدُّ مِن كُفْرِ غَيْرِهِمْ ومِن نِفاقِ غَيْرِهِمْ، لِأنَّهم أقْسى قَلْبًا وأغْلَظُ طَبْعًا وأجْفى قَوْلًا، وأبْعَدُ عَنْ سَماعِ كُتُبِ اللَّهِ وما جاءَتْ بِهِ رُسُلُهُ، والأعْرابُ: هم مَن سَكَنَ البَوادِيَ بِخِلافِ العَرَبِ، فَإنَّهُ عامٌّ لِهَذا النَّوْعِ مِن بَنِي آدَمَ سَواءٌ سَكَنُوا البَوادِيَ أوِ القُرى، هَكَذا قالَ أهْلُ اللُّغَةِ، ولِهَذا قالَ سِيبَوَيْهِ: إنَّ الأعْرابَ صِيغَةُ جَمْعٍ ولَيْسَتْ بِصِيغَةِ جَمْعٍ العَرَبُ.

قالَ النَّيْسابُورِيُّ: قالَ أهْلُ اللُّغَةِ: رَجُلٌ عَرَبِيٌّ إذا كانَ نَسَبُهُ إلى العَرَبِ ثابِتًا، وجَمْعُهُ عَرَبٌ، كالمَجُوسِيِّ والمَجُوسِ، واليَهُودِيِّ واليَهُودِ، فالأعْرابِيُّ إذا قِيلَ لَهُ: يا عَرَبِيُّ فَرِحَ، وإذا قِيلَ لِلْعَرَبِيِّ: يا أعْرابِيُّ غَضِبَ، وذَلِكَ أنَّ مَنِ اسْتَوْطَنَ القُرى العَرَبِيَّةَ فَهو عَرَبِيٌّ، ومَن نَزَلَ البادِيَةَ فَهو أعْرابِيٌّ، ولِهَذا لا يَجُوزُ أنْ يُقالَ لِلْمُهاجِرِينَ والأنْصارِ أعْرابٌ، وإنَّما هم عَرَبٌ.

قالَ: قِيلَ: إنَّما سُمِّيَ العَرَبُ عَرَبًا لِأنَّ أوْلادَ إسْماعِيلَ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ) نَشَئُوا بِالعَرَبِ، وهي مِن تِهامَةَ فَنُسِبُوا إلى بَلَدِهِمْ، وكُلُّ مَن يَسْكُنُ جَزِيرَةَ العَرَبِ ويَنْطِقُ بِلِسانِهِمْ فَهو مِنهم، وقِيلَ: لِأنَّ ألْسُنَهم مُعْرِبَةٌ عَمّا في ضَمائِرِهِمْ، ولِما في لِسانِهِمْ مِنَ الفَصاحَةِ والبَلاغَةِ انْتَهى.

وأجْدَرُ مَعْطُوفٌ عَلى (أشَدُّ)، ومَعْناهُ أخْلَقُ، يُقالُ: فُلانٌ جَدِيرٌ بِكَذا: أيْ خَلِيقٌ بِهِ، وأنْتَ جَدِيرٌ أنْ تَفْعَلَ كَذا، والجَمْعُ جُدُرٌ أوْ جَدِيرُونَ، وأصْلُهُ مِن جَدْرِ الحائِطِ، وهو رَفْعُهُ بِالبِناءِ.

والمَعْنى: أنَّهم أحَقُّ وأخْلَقُ بِـ﴿أَلّا يَعْلَمُوا حُدُودَ ما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ مِنَ الشَّرائِعِ والأحْكامِ، لِبُعْدِهِمْ عَنْ مَواطِنِ الأنْبِياءِ ودِيارِ التَّنْزِيلِ ﴿واللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾ بِأحْوالِ مَخْلُوقاتِهِ عَلى العُمُومِ، وهَؤُلاءِ مِنهم ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ فِيما يُجازِيهِمْ بِهِ مِن خَيْرٍ وشَرٍّ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ومِنَ الأعْرابِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ ما يُنْفِقُ مَغْرَمًا﴾ هَذا تَنْوِيعٌ لِجِنْسٍ أوْ نَوْعَيْنِ، الأوَّلُ هَؤُلاءِ، والثّانِي ﴿ومِنَ الأعْرابِ مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ﴾ والمَغْرَمُ الغَرامَةُ والخُسْرانُ، وأصْلُ الغُرْمِ والغَرامَةِ: ما يُنْفِقُهُ الرَّجُلُ ولَيْسَ بِلازِمٍ لَهُ في اعْتِقادِهِ ولَكِنَّهُ يُنْفِقُهُ لِلرِّياءِ والتَّقِيَّةِ، وقِيلَ: أصْلُ الغُرْمِ اللُّزُومُ كَأنَّهُ اعْتَقَدَ أنَّهُ يَلْزَمُهُ لِأمْرٍ خارِجٍ لا تَنْبَعِثُ لَهُ النَّفْسُ.

والدَّوائِرَ جُمَعُ دائِرَةٍ، وهي الحالَةُ المُنْقَلِبَةُ عَنِ النِّعْمَةِ إلى البَلِيَّةِ، وأصْلُها ما يُحِيطُ بِالشَّيْءِ، ودَوائِرُ الزَّمانِ: نُوَبُهُ وتَصارِيفُهُ ودُوَلُهُ، وكَأنَّها لا تُسْتَعْمَلُ إلّا في المَكْرُوهِ، ثُمَّ دَعا سُبْحانَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ دائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ﴾ وجَعَلَ ما دَعا بِهِ عَلَيْهِمْ مُماثِلًا لِما (p-٥٩٤) أرادُوهُ بِالمُسْلِمِينَ، والسَّوْءُ بِالفَتْحِ عِنْدَ جُمْهُورِ القُرّاءِ مَصْدَرٌ أُضِيفَتْ إلَيْهِ الدّائِرَةُ لِلْمُلابَسَةِ كَقَوْلِكَ: رَجُلُ صِدْقٍ.

وقَرَأ أبُو عَمْرٍو وابْنُ كَثِيرٍ بِضَمِّ السِّينِ، وهو المَكْرُوهُ.

قالَ الأخْفَشُ: أيْ عَلَيْهِمْ دائِرَةُ الهَزِيمَةِ والشَّرِّ.

وقالَ الفَرّاءُ: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ دائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ﴾ العَذابُ والبَلاءُ.

قالَ: والسَّوْءُ بِالفَتْحِ مَصْدَرُ سُؤْتُهُ سَوْءًا ومَساءَةً، وبِالضَّمِّ اسْمٌ لا مَصْدَرَ، وهو كَقَوْلِكَ دائِرَةُ البَلاءِ والمَكْرُوهِ. ﴿واللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ﴾ لِما يَقُولُونَهُ ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ بِما يُضْمِرُونَهُ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ومِنَ الأعْرابِ مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ﴾ هَذا النَّوْعُ الثّانِي مِن أنْواعِ الأعْرابِ كَما تَقَدَّمَ: أيْ يُصَدِّقُ بِهِما ﴿ويَتَّخِذُ ما يُنْفِقُ﴾ أيْ يَجْعَلُ ما يُنْفِقُهُ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ قُرُباتٍ وهي جَمْعُ قُرْبَةٍ، وهي: ما يُتَقَرَّبُ بِهِ إلى اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ، تَقُولُ مِنهُ قَرَّبْتُ لِلَّهِ قُرْبانًا، والجَمْعُ قُرَبٌ وقُرُباتٌ.

والمَعْنى: أنَّهُ يَجْعَلُ ما يُنْفِقُهُ سَبَبًا لِحُصُولِ القُرُباتِ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وسَبَبًا لِ﴿صَلَواتِ الرَّسُولِ﴾ أيْ لِدَعَواتِ الرَّسُولِ لَهم، لِأنَّهُ (ﷺ) كانَ يَدْعُو لِلْمُتَصَدِّقِينَ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ إنَّ صَلاتَكَ سَكَنٌ لَهُمْ﴾ [التوبة: ١٠٣]، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ (ﷺ): «اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلى آلِ أبِي أوْفى». ثُمَّ إنَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ بَيَّنَ بِأنَّ ما يُنْفِقُهُ هَذا النَّوْعُ مِنَ الأعْرابِ تَقَرُّبًا إلى اللَّهِ مَقْبُولٌ واقِعٌ عَلى الوَجْهِ الَّذِي أرادُوهُ فَقالَ: ﴿ألا إنَّها قُرْبَةٌ لَهُمْ﴾ فَأخْبَرَ سُبْحانَهُ بِقَبُولِها خَبَرًا مُؤَكَّدًا بِأِسْمِيَّةِ الجُمْلَةِ وحَرْفَيِ التَّنْبِيهِ والتَّحْقِيقِ، وفي هَذا مِنَ التَّطْيِيبِ لِخَواطِرِهِمْ والتَّطْمِينِ لِقُلُوبِهِمْ ما لا يُقادَرُ قَدْرُهُ مَعَ ما يَتَضَمَّنُهُ مِنَ النَّعْيِ عَلى مَن يَتَّخِذُ ما يُنْفِقُ مَغْرَمًا، والتَّوْبِيخِ لَهُ بِأبْلَغِ وجْهٍ، والضَّمِيرُ في ﴿إنَّها﴾ راجِعٌ إلى ما في ﴿ما يُنْفِقُ﴾ وتَأْنِيثُهُ بِاعْتِبارِ الخَبَرِ.

وقَرَأ نافِعٌ، في رِوايَةٍ عَنْهُ ﴿قُرُبَةٌ﴾ بِضَمِّ الرّاءِ، وقَرَأ الباقُونَ بِسُكُونِها تَخْفِيفًا، ثُمَّ فَسَّرَ سُبْحانَهُ القُرْبَةَ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿سَيُدْخِلُهُمُ اللَّهُ في رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ والسِّينُ لِتَحْقِيقِ الوَعْدِ.

وقَدْ أخْرَجَ ابْنُ أبِي حاتِمٍ، وأبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنِ السُّدِّيِّ، في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿قَدْ نَبَّأنا اللَّهُ مِن أخْبارِكُمْ﴾ قالَ: أخْبَرَنا أنَّكم لَوْ خَرَجْتُمْ ما زِدْتُمُونا إلّا خَبالًا، وفي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَأعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمْ﴾ قالَ: «لَمّا رَجَعَ النَّبِيُّ (ﷺ) قالَ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: لا تُكَلِّمُوهم ولا تُجالِسُوهم، فَأعْرَضُوا عَنْهم كَما أمَرَ اللَّهُ».

وأخْرَجَ أبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنْهُ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿لِتُعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمْ﴾ قالَ: لِتُجاوِزُوا عَنْهم.

وأخْرَجَ أبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنْهُ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿الأعْرابُ أشَدُّ كُفْرًا ونِفاقًا﴾ قالَ: مِن مُنافِقِي المَدِينَةِ ﴿وأجْدَرُ ألّا يَعْلَمُوا حُدُودَ ما أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ﴾ يَعْنِي الفَرائِضَ، وما أمَرَ بِهِ مِنَ الجِهادِ.

وأخْرَجَ أبُو الشَّيْخِ، عَنِ الكَلْبِيِّ، أنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ نَزَلَتْ في أسَدٍ وغَطَفانَ.
