His saying: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants﴾. When Allah, glorified is He, accepted repentance from these people mentioned previously, Allah said: ﴿Do they not know﴾, that is, those who had not repented, or those who had repented before Allah accepted their repentance and accepted their charities, ﴿that it is Allah who accepts repentance﴾ because He is independent of the obedience of the obedient and does not care for the disobedience of the disobedient.

It has been read as "tu'lamu" (do you not know) with the second person, which is either addressed to the repentant ones, or to a group of believers. The meaning of ﴿and takes charities﴾ is: He accepts them from them. In attributing the taking to Him, glorified is He, after His command to His Messenger (ﷺ) to take them, there is great honor for this act of obedience and for those who perform it.

His saying: ﴿And that Allah is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful﴾ is conjoined to His saying: ﴿that Allah is the one who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, along with its inclusion of an emphasis of what the conjoined clause contains: that is, this is His, glorified is He, characteristic.

In the form of intensive emphasis in "al-Tawwab" (the Accepter of repentance) and "al-Rahim" (the Merciful), along with the placement of the separating pronoun and the emphasis, there is evident good news for His servants and encouragement for them.

His saying: ﴿And say: Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger and the believers﴾. In it is a warning and threat: that is, your deeds are not hidden from Allah, nor from His Messenger, nor from the believers. So hasten to deeds of goodness and make your deeds sincere for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. In it also is encouragement and enlivening: for whoever knows that his deed will not be hidden, whether good or bad, will be eager for deeds of goodness and will avoid deeds of evil. How excellent is the saying of Zuhayr:

The poem line is rendered as it stands:

"Whatever disposition a man may have, however well it is hidden from people, it will become known."

The meaning of "seeing" here is knowledge of the deeds that proceed from them. Then Allah, glorified is He, issued a severe warning, saying: ﴿And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed.﴾ That is, after death you will be returned to Allah, glorified is He, who knows what you conceal, what you disclose, what you hide and what you show. Placing "the unseen" before "the witnessed" indicates the vastness of His knowledge, glorified and exalted is He, that nothing is hidden from Him, and that every object of knowledge is equal to Him.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned what will happen after their return to Him, saying: ﴿then He will inform you﴾, that is, He will tell you ﴿of what you used to do﴾ in the world. He will then reward the good-doer for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil, and He bestows His grace upon whom He wills of His servants.

As for His saying ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah﴾: He, glorified is He, mentioned three categories among those who stayed behind. The first: the hypocrites who persisted in hypocrisy (marada, "became hardened in it"). The second: the penitent who acknowledged their sins. The third: those whose matter remained suspended in that state, and they are "those deferred to the command of Allah," from arjaytuhu and arja'tuhu, meaning "I postponed it."

Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Nafi' and Hafs read ﴿murjawna﴾ with a waw and without a hamza. The rest read it with a hamza after the jim, with a damma.

The meaning is that they are postponed in that state: no verdict is given for them regarding repentance or its absence, but they remain as Allah, glorified is He, will make clear regarding their situation. ﴿Either He will punish them﴾ if they remain in their present condition and do not repent, ﴿or He will accept their repentance﴾ if they repent with sincere repentance and devote themselves to it completely. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal), and the sense is: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah﴾ while they are either punished or forgiven. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of their circumstances, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in what He does to them, whether good or evil.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah report from Abu Musa that he was asked about His saying: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the emigrants and the helpers﴾, and he said: they are those who prayed towards both qiblahs (Jerusalem and the Ka'bah).

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu'aym report from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib the same.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu Nu'aym report from al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn Sirin the same as well.

Ibn Mardawayh reports from Ibn Abbas that he said: they are Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, Salman and Ammar ibn Yasir.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah report from al-Sha'bi that he said: they are those who attained the Pledge of Ridwan.

Ibn Abi Hatim reports from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿and those who followed them in goodness﴾, that he said: they are the Successors (tabi'un).

Ibn Abi Hatim reports from Ibn Zayd that he said: they are whoever remains of the people of Islam until the Hour is established.

Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Asakir report from Abu Sakhr Humayd ibn Ziyad, who said: I said to Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: "Tell me about the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," and I only meant the strife (that occurred among them). He said: Allah has indeed forgiven all the companions of the Prophet ﷺ and has made Paradise obligatory for them in His Book, both their good-doers and their wrong-doers. I said to him: "In which place did Allah make Paradise obligatory for them in His Book?" He said: "Do you not read His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the foremost, the first...﴾ to the end of the verse," and He made Paradise and His good pleasure obligatory for all the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and He stipulated a condition upon the Successors that He did not stipulate for them. I said: "And what condition did He stipulate upon them?" He said: "He stipulated upon them that they follow them in goodness," meaning: that they imitate them in their good deeds, and not imitate them in anything other than that.

Abu Sakhr said: "By Allah, it is as if I had never read it before, and I had not known its interpretation until Ibn Ka'b recited it to me."

Ibn Mardawayh reports through al-Awza'i, who said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, al-Qasim, Makhul, Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah and Hassan ibn Atiyyah told me that they heard a group of the companions of the Prophet ﷺ saying: "When this verse was revealed, ﴿And the foremost, the first...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and they are pleased with Him﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'This is for all my nation, and there is no displeasure after pleasure.'"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh report from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins﴾ up to the end of the verse, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up on a Friday to deliver a sermon, and said: 'Stand up, so-and-so, and leave, for you are a hypocrite. Leave, so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite.' He brought them out by their names and exposed them. Umar ibn al-Khattab had not attended that Friday prayer because of some need he had, so Umar met them as they were leaving the mosque, and he hid from them out of shame that he had not attended the Friday prayer. They assumed the people had dispersed, and they hid from Umar, thinking he had learned of their affair. Umar entered the mosque and found the people had not dispersed. A man said to him: 'Rejoice, O Umar, for Allah has today exposed the hypocrites.'" So that is the first punishment, and the second punishment is the punishment of the grave.

Ibn al-Mundhir reports from Ikrimah concerning His saying: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins﴾, that he said: they are Juhaynah, Muzaynah, Ash'a, Aslam and Ghifar.

Ibn Abi Hatim reports from Ibn Zayd concerning His saying: ﴿They became hardened in hypocrisy﴾, that he said: they persisted in it and did not repent as others repented.

Ibn al-Mundhir reports from Ibn Jurayj concerning the verse, that he said: they died upon it: Abdullah ibn Ubayy, Abu Amir the monk, and al-Jadd ibn Qays.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh report from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾, that he said: "with hunger and killing."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh report from Abu Malik, who said: "with hunger and the punishment of the grave."

Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi report from Qatadah, who said: "a punishment in the grave, and a punishment in the Fire."

Similar statements have been reported from a number of the early generations (salaf) regarding the identification of the two punishments, but the apparent meaning is what we have mentioned earlier.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il report from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And others who acknowledged their sins, having mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾, that he said: "They were ten men who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the Battle of Tabuk. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was about to return, seven of them tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque. The Prophet ﷺ used to pass by them when he returned. When he saw them he said: 'Who are these who have tied themselves up?' They said: 'This is Abu Lubabah and companions of his who stayed behind from you, O Messenger of Allah, until you release them and excuse them.' He said: 'And I swear by Allah I will not release them or excuse them until Allah is the One who releases them. They turned away from me and stayed behind from the expedition with the Muslims.' When this reached them, they said: 'And we will not release ourselves until Allah is the One who releases us.' So ﴿It may be that Allah will accept their repentance﴾ was revealed, and 'it may be' from Allah is binding. When it was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ sent for them, released them and excused them. They came with their wealth and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this is our wealth, so give it in charity on our behalf and ask forgiveness for us.' He said: 'I have not been commanded to take your wealth.' Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and invoke blessings upon them﴾, meaning: ask forgiveness for them. ﴿Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾, meaning: a mercy for them. So he took the charity from them and asked forgiveness for them. There were three men who had not tied themselves to the pillars, so they were deferred for a year, not knowing whether they would be punished or forgiven. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet﴾ [al-Tawbah: 117] to His saying: ﴿and to the three who were left behind﴾, to His saying: ﴿Then He turned to them that they might repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾ [al-Tawbah: 118], meaning: if they become upright."

Abu al-Shaykh reports from al-Dahhak the same, without difference.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il report from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿acknowledged their sins﴾, that he said: "It is Abu Lubabah, when he said to the Qurayzah what he said, and he gestured to his throat, meaning that Muhammad would slaughter you if you came down under his judgment." The story is mentioned in the books of biography (siyar).

Ibn Abi Hatim reports from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: ﴿they mixed a righteous deed﴾, that he said: "Their fighting alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." ﴿And another evil﴾: "Their staying behind from him."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh report from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿and invoke blessings upon them﴾, that he said: "Ask forgiveness for them for their sins which they had committed." ﴿Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾: "a mercy for them."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others report from Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, who said: "When charity was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would say: 'O Allah, bless the family of so-and-so.' My father brought him his charity, and he said: 'O Allah, bless the family of Abi Awfa.'"

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh report from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿Act, for Allah will see your deed, and so will His Messenger﴾, that he said: "This is a warning from Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Ahmad, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, and al-Diya in al-Mukhtarah report from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "If one of you were to work on a solid rock with no door or window, Allah would bring out his deed for the people, whatever it may be."

Ibn al-Mundhir reports from Ikrimah concerning His saying: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah﴾, that he said: "They are the three who were left behind."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh report from Mujahid concerning the verse, that he said: "They are Hilal ibn Umayyah, Murarah ibn al-Rabi' and Ka'b ibn Malik, from the Aws and the Khazraj."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh report from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: ﴿Either He will punish them﴾, that he said: "He will cause them to die in disobedience." ﴿Or He will accept their repentance﴾: "So He deferred their matter, then abrogated it (nasakha, the technical sense of naskh, abrogation of a ruling by a later revelation), saying: ﴿and [He turned] to the three who were left behind﴾ [al-Tawbah: 118]."

When Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the categories of the Bedouins, He mentioned the Emigrants (al-Muhajirun) and the Helpers (al-Ansar), and made clear that among them are those who were foremost to emigrate, and among them are those who follow them.

It is narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read "wa al-Ansaru" (and the Helpers) in the nominative case, as a conjunction with "wa al-sabiquna" (and the foremost). The rest of the reciters among the Companions and those after them read it in the genitive case.

Al-Akhfash said: The genitive in "al-Ansar" is the more preferred reading, because the foremost among them are included in the phrase "wa al-sabiquna," and the verse signifies the preference of the first foremost ones among the Emigrants and the Helpers. They are the ones who prayed towards both qiblas (the Jerusalem and the Ka'bah), according to the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and a group. Or they are those who witnessed the Pledge of al-Ridwan, which is the Pledge of al-Hudaybiyah, according to the view of al-Sha'bi. Or they are the people of Badr, according to the view of (p-595) Muhammad ibn Ka'b and Ata' ibn Yasar. There is no obstacle to applying the verse to all of these categories. Abu Mansur al-Baghdadi said: Our companions (scholars) are unanimously agreed that the most excellent of them are the Four Caliphs, then the six remaining (of the ten promised Paradise), then the people of Badr, then the companions of Uhud, then the people of the Pledge of al-Ridwan at al-Hudaybiyah.

His saying: ﴿And those who followed them in goodness﴾. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, read "alladhina ittaba'uhum" (those who followed them) without the waw, as a description of the Helpers according to his reading with the nominative "al-Ansar." Zayd ibn Thabit disputed this with him, so he asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who confirmed Zayd's view, and so Umar retracted from the aforementioned reading, as narrated by Abu Ubayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh. The meaning of "those who followed them in goodness" is: those who followed the first foremost ones among the Emigrants and the Helpers, namely those who came after them among the Companions and those who came after them until the Day of Resurrection. The intended meaning here is not the "Tabi'un" (Successors) in the technical sense, who are everyone who met the Companions but did not meet the Prophet (ﷺ). Rather, they are among those included under the verse. Thus "min" in his saying ﴿from the Emigrants﴾ is, on this view, for partitive (tab'id). It has also been said that it is for explanation (bayan), in which case the praise encompasses all the Companions, and the intended meaning of the Successors are those who came after them of the Ummah until the Day of Resurrection.

His saying: "in goodness" is a restriction on the Successors. That is: those who followed them while being characterized by goodness in deeds and words, emulating the first foremost ones.

His saying: ﴿Allah is pleased with them﴾ is the predicate of the subject and what is conjoined to it. The meaning of His pleasure, glorified is He, with them is that He accepted their acts of obedience, overlooked their faults, and was not angry with them. ﴿And they are pleased with Him﴾ for what He has given them of His bounty. Along with His pleasure with them, ﴿He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ in the Hereafter.

Ibn Kathir read "tajri tahtaha al-anharu" (beneath which rivers flow) with the addition of "min." The rest read it without it, with the accusative case as an adverbial of place (zarfiyyah). The explanation of the flowing of rivers from beneath the gardens and the explanation of "khulud" (eternal abiding) and "fawz" (triumph) have already been mentioned.

His saying: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites﴾. This is a return to the explanation of the states of the hypocrites, from the people of Madinah and those near it among the Bedouins. "Wa mimman hawlakum" is a fronted predicate, "min al-a'rab" is an explanation, and it is in the place of an accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). "Munafiqun" is the subject. It has been said: those who are around Madinah among the hypocrites are Juhaynah, Muzaynah, Ashja' and Ghifar. The clause ﴿And among the people of Madinah are those who persisted in hypocrisy﴾ is conjoined to the first clause as a clause conjoined to a clause. 

It has also been said: "wa min ahl al-Madinah" is conjoined to the predicate in the first clause. According to the first view, the subject is implied: that is, "and among the people of Madinah are a people who persisted in hypocrisy." According to the second, the implied meaning is: "And among those around you of the Bedouins and among the people of Madinah are hypocrites who persisted." Since the clause "maradu 'ala al-nifaq" (they persisted in hypocrisy) is a resumptive clause with no place in the sentence, the root of "marada" and "tamarrada" is smoothness, bareness and stripping. So it is as if they stripped themselves for hypocrisy. From this comes "ghusnun amrad" (a branch with no leaves), "faras amrad" (a horse without hair), "ghulam amrad" (a beardless youth), "ard marda'" (a land without vegetation), and "sarh mumarrad" (a stripped, smooth palace). The meaning is: they remained in hypocrisy, held firm to it, and did not turn away from it.

Ibn Zayd said: its meaning is that they persisted in it and clung to it. The clause ﴿You do not know them﴾ explains the first clause, which is "marada 'ala al-nifaq," i.e. they held firmly to it with a strong steadfastness, and became so skilled in it that their affair was hidden from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so how about the rest of the believers? The intended meaning is the Prophet's (ﷺ) lack of knowledge of their individual identities, not in general, for the hypocrite has signs that are not hidden from him (ﷺ). The clause ﴿We know them﴾ confirms what precedes it, due to what it contains of the indication of their expertise in hypocrisy and their firm rootedness in it in a way that is hidden from humans, and is not manifest to anyone except Allah, glorified is He, because of His knowledge of what is concealed, what the hearts hide, and what the inner secrets conceal. Then He, glorified is He, threatened them, saying: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾. It has been said: the intended meaning of "twice" is the punishment of this world by killing and captivity, and the punishment of the Hereafter. It has also been said: it is disgrace by the exposure of their hypocrisy and punishment in the Hereafter. It has been said: it is calamities in their wealth and children, and the punishment of the grave. Other views have been stated, which are lengthy to mention, with no evidence that any of them is specifically intended.

The apparent view is that this repeated punishment is in this world, by that which truly is called punishment, and that they are punished time after time, and then they are returned after that to the punishment of the Hereafter. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾. Whoever said that the punishment in the second time is the punishment of the Hereafter said: the meaning of His saying ﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾ is that after their punishment in the Fire, they will be returned, like the rest of the disbelievers, to its lowest level, or that they will be punished in the Fire with a punishment specific to them apart from the rest of the disbelievers, and then after that they will be returned to the punishment that encompasses them and the rest of the disbelievers.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned the state of a group of Muslims, namely those who mixed their religion, and said: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾. This is conjoined to His saying "hypocrites," meaning: and among those around you of the Bedouins and among the people of Madinah there is another people. It is permissible that "akharun" (others) be the subject, "i'tarafu bi dhunubihim" (they acknowledged their sins) its description, and "khalatu 'amalan salihan wa akhara sayyi'an" (they mixed a righteous deed and another evil one) its predicate. The meaning is: this group lagged behind from the expedition without any acceptable excuse for lagging, then they regretted that, and did not offer false excuses as the hypocrites did, but rather repented, acknowledged the sin, and hoped that Allah would accept their repentance.

The righteous deed refers to what came before of their Islam, their upholding of the laws of Islam, and their going out to fight in all the battlefields. The evil deed refers to their lagging behind from this expedition, and they followed this evil deed with a righteous deed, which is acknowledging it and repenting from it.

The origin of "i'tiraf" (acknowledgment) is affirmation of a matter. Mere affirmation is not repentance unless it is accompanied by remorse for the past and resolve to abandon it presently and in the future. What occurred from them indicates this, as will be explained, Allah willing.

The meaning of "khalt" (mixing) is that they mixed each of the two with the other, like your saying: "I mixed the water with the milk and the milk with the water." It is permissible that the "wa" (and) carries the meaning of "ba'" (with), like your saying: "I sold the sheep for a sheep and a dirham," meaning: for a dirham. His saying: ﴿Perhaps Allah will accept their repentance﴾ is evidence that along with the acknowledgment, what indicates repentance had already occurred from them, or that the preliminary step of repentance, which is acknowledgment, took the place of repentance. The particle of hope, "'asa," in the speech of Allah, glorified is He, indicates the certainty of occurrence, because raising hopes from Allah, glorified is He, is an obligation, given that He is the most Generous of the generous. ﴿Indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (p-596), meaning He forgives sins and bestows favor upon His servants.

His saying: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾. The scholars differed concerning this commanded charity. It has been said: it is the obligatory charity (sadaqat al-fard). It has also been said: it is specific to this group that acknowledged their sins, because after Allah accepted their repentance, they presented their wealth to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and so this verse was revealed. "Min" is partitive according to both interpretations. The verse is absolute and is clarified by the pure Sunnah. The word "sadaqah" (charity) is derived from "sidq" (truthfulness), since it is evidence of the truthfulness of the one who gives it in his faith.

His saying: ﴿It purifies them and causes them to grow with it﴾. The pronoun in both verbs refers to the Prophet (ﷺ): that is, you, O Muhammad, purify them and cause them to grow by what you take from them of the charity. It has also been said: the pronoun in "yutahhiruhum" refers to the charity, meaning this charity taken from them purifies them, and the pronoun in "yuzakkihim" refers to the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning: you, O Muhammad, cause them to grow with the charity taken. The first is preferable, because the second involves a difference in the pronouns of the two conjoined verbs. According to the first, the two verbs are in the accusative as a circumstantial state, and according to the second, the first verb is a description of "sadaqatan" (a charity) and the second is a circumstantial state of it (ﷺ).

The meaning of purification (tathhir) is removing what traces of sins remain upon them, and the meaning of growth (tazkiyah) is intensifying the purification.

Al-Zajjaj said: The better view is that the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning: indeed you, O Muhammad, purify them and cause them to grow with it, as a definite and new statement. It is permissible to read it in the jussive case as a response to the imperative. The meaning is: that you take from their wealth a charity which purifies them. 

Al-Hasan read "tutahhiruhum" in the jussive. On this reading, "wa tuzakkihim" is by implication of a subject: that is, "and you cause them to grow."

His saying: ﴿And pray for them﴾: that is, supplicate for them after your taking that charity from their wealth.

Al-Nahhas said: The people of the language have all agreed, as far as we know, that "salat" (prayer) in the speech of the Arabs means supplication. Then Allah, glorified is He, gave the reason for His command to His Messenger (ﷺ) to pray for those from whom he takes charity, saying: ﴿Indeed your prayer is a tranquility for them﴾.

Hafs, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "salataka" (your prayer) in the singular, and the rest read it in the plural. "Sakan" (tranquility) is that in which the soul finds rest and is reassured.

His saying: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants﴾. When Allah, glorified is He, accepted repentance from these people mentioned previously, Allah said: ﴿Do they not know﴾, that is, those who had not repented, or those who had repented before Allah accepted their repentance and accepted their charities, ﴿that it is Allah who accepts repentance﴾ because He is independent of the obedience of the obedient and does not care for the disobedience of the disobedient.

It has been read as "tu'lamu" (do you not know) with the second person, which is either addressed to the repentant ones, or to a group of believers. The meaning of ﴿and takes charities﴾ is: He accepts them from them. In attributing the taking to Him, glorified is He, after His command to His Messenger (ﷺ) to take them, there is great honor for this act of obedience and for those who perform it.

His saying: ﴿And that Allah is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful﴾ is conjoined to His saying: ﴿that Allah is the one who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, along with its inclusion of an emphasis of what the conjoined clause contains: that is, this is His, glorified is He, characteristic.

In the form of intensive emphasis in "al-Tawwab" (the Accepter of repentance) and "al-Rahim" (the Merciful), along with the placement of the separating pronoun and the emphasis, there is evident good news for His servants and encouragement for them.

His saying: ﴿And say: Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger and the believers﴾. In it is a warning and threat: that is, your deeds are not hidden from Allah, nor from His Messenger, nor from the believers. So hasten to deeds of goodness and make your deeds sincere for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. In it also is encouragement and enlivening: for whoever knows that his deed will not be hidden, whether good or bad, will be eager for deeds of goodness and will avoid deeds of evil. How excellent is the saying of Zuhayr:

The poem line is rendered as it stands:

"Whatever disposition a man may have, however well it is hidden from people, it will become known."

The meaning of "seeing" here is knowledge of the deeds that proceed from them. Then Allah, glorified is He, issued a severe warning, saying: ﴿And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed.﴾ That is, after death you will be returned to Allah, glorified is He, who knows what you conceal, what you disclose, what you hide and what you show. Placing "the unseen" before "the witnessed" indicates the vastness of His knowledge, glorified and exalted is He, that nothing is hidden from Him, and that every object of knowledge is equal to Him.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned what will happen after their return to Him, saying: ﴿then He will inform you﴾, that is, He will tell you ﴿of what you used to do﴾ in the world. He will then reward the good-doer for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil, and He bestows His grace upon whom He wills of His servants.

As for His saying ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah﴾: He, glorified is He, mentioned three categories among those who stayed behind. The first: the hypocrites who persisted in hypocrisy (marada, "became hardened in it"). The second: the penitent who acknowledged their sins. The third: those whose matter remained suspended in that state, and they are "those deferred to the command of Allah," from arjaytuhu and arja'tuhu, meaning "I postponed it."

Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Nafi' and Hafs read ﴿murjawna﴾ with a waw and without a hamza. The rest read it with a hamza after the jim, with a damma.

The meaning is that they are postponed in that state: no verdict is given for them regarding repentance or its absence, but they remain as Allah, glorified is He, will make clear regarding their situation. ﴿Either He will punish them﴾ if they remain in their present condition and do not repent, ﴿or He will accept their repentance﴾ if they repent with sincere repentance and devote themselves to it completely. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal), and the sense is: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah﴾ while they are either punished or forgiven. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of their circumstances, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in what He does to them, whether good or evil.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah report from Abu Musa that he was asked about His saying: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the emigrants and the helpers﴾, and he said: they are those who prayed towards both qiblahs (Jerusalem and the Ka'bah).

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu'aym report from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib the same.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu Nu'aym report from al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn Sirin the same as well.

Ibn Mardawayh reports from Ibn Abbas that he said: they are Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, Salman and Ammar ibn Yasir.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah report from al-Sha'bi that he said: they are those who attained the Pledge of Ridwan.

Ibn Abi Hatim reports from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿and those who followed them in goodness﴾, that he said: they are the Successors (tabi'un).

Ibn Abi Hatim reports from Ibn Zayd that he said: they are whoever remains of the people of Islam until the Hour is established.

Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Asakir report from Abu Sakhr Humayd ibn Ziyad, who said: I said to Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: "Tell me about the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," and I only meant the strife (that occurred among them). He said: Allah has indeed forgiven all the companions of the Prophet ﷺ and has made Paradise obligatory for them in His Book, both their good-doers and their wrong-doers. I said to him: "In which place did Allah make Paradise obligatory for them in His Book?" He said: "Do you not read His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the foremost, the first...﴾ to the end of the verse," and He made Paradise and His good pleasure obligatory for all the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and He stipulated a condition upon the Successors that He did not stipulate for them. I said: "And what condition did He stipulate upon them?" He said: "He stipulated upon them that they follow them in goodness," meaning: that they imitate them in their good deeds, and not imitate them in anything other than that.

Abu Sakhr said: "By Allah, it is as if I had never read it before, and I had not known its interpretation until Ibn Ka'b recited it to me."

Ibn Mardawayh reports through al-Awza'i, who said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, al-Qasim, Makhul, Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah and Hassan ibn Atiyyah told me that they heard a group of the companions of the Prophet ﷺ saying: "When this verse was revealed, ﴿And the foremost, the first...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and they are pleased with Him﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'This is for all my nation, and there is no displeasure after pleasure.'"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh report from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins﴾ up to the end of the verse, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up on a Friday to deliver a sermon, and said: 'Stand up, so-and-so, and leave, for you are a hypocrite. Leave, so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite.' He brought them out by their names and exposed them. Umar ibn al-Khattab had not attended that Friday prayer because of some need he had, so Umar met them as they were leaving the mosque, and he hid from them out of shame that he had not attended the Friday prayer. They assumed the people had dispersed, and they hid from Umar, thinking he had learned of their affair. Umar entered the mosque and found the people had not dispersed. A man said to him: 'Rejoice, O Umar, for Allah has today exposed the hypocrites.'" So that is the first punishment, and the second punishment is the punishment of the grave.

Ibn al-Mundhir reports from Ikrimah concerning His saying: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins﴾, that he said: they are Juhaynah, Muzaynah, Ash'a, Aslam and Ghifar.

Ibn Abi Hatim reports from Ibn Zayd concerning His saying: ﴿They became hardened in hypocrisy﴾, that he said: they persisted in it and did not repent as others repented.

Ibn al-Mundhir reports from Ibn Jurayj concerning the verse, that he said: they died upon it: Abdullah ibn Ubayy, Abu Amir the monk, and al-Jadd ibn Qays.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh report from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾, that he said: "with hunger and killing."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh report from Abu Malik, who said: "with hunger and the punishment of the grave."

Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi report from Qatadah, who said: "a punishment in the grave, and a punishment in the Fire."

Similar statements have been reported from a number of the early generations (salaf) regarding the identification of the two punishments, but the apparent meaning is what we have mentioned earlier.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il report from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And others who acknowledged their sins, having mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾, that he said: "They were ten men who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the Battle of Tabuk. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was about to return, seven of them tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque. The Prophet ﷺ used to pass by them when he returned. When he saw them he said: 'Who are these who have tied themselves up?' They said: 'This is Abu Lubabah and companions of his who stayed behind from you, O Messenger of Allah, until you release them and excuse them.' He said: 'And I swear by Allah I will not release them or excuse them until Allah is the One who releases them. They turned away from me and stayed behind from the expedition with the Muslims.' When this reached them, they said: 'And we will not release ourselves until Allah is the One who releases us.' So ﴿It may be that Allah will accept their repentance﴾ was revealed, and 'it may be' from Allah is binding. When it was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ sent for them, released them and excused them. They came with their wealth and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this is our wealth, so give it in charity on our behalf and ask forgiveness for us.' He said: 'I have not been commanded to take your wealth.' Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and invoke blessings upon them﴾, meaning: ask forgiveness for them. ﴿Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾, meaning: a mercy for them. So he took the charity from them and asked forgiveness for them. There were three men who had not tied themselves to the pillars, so they were deferred for a year, not knowing whether they would be punished or forgiven. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet﴾ [al-Tawbah: 117] to His saying: ﴿and to the three who were left behind﴾, to His saying: ﴿Then He turned to them that they might repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾ [al-Tawbah: 118], meaning: if they become upright."

Abu al-Shaykh reports from al-Dahhak the same, without difference.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il report from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿acknowledged their sins﴾, that he said: "It is Abu Lubabah, when he said to the Qurayzah what he said, and he gestured to his throat, meaning that Muhammad would slaughter you if you came down under his judgment." The story is mentioned in the books of biography (siyar).

Ibn Abi Hatim reports from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: ﴿they mixed a righteous deed﴾, that he said: "Their fighting alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." ﴿And another evil﴾: "Their staying behind from him."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh report from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿and invoke blessings upon them﴾, that he said: "Ask forgiveness for them for their sins which they had committed." ﴿Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾: "a mercy for them."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others report from Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, who said: "When charity was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would say: 'O Allah, bless the family of so-and-so.' My father brought him his charity, and he said: 'O Allah, bless the family of Abi Awfa.'"

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh report from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿Act, for Allah will see your deed, and so will His Messenger﴾, that he said: "This is a warning from Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Ahmad, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, and al-Diya in al-Mukhtarah report from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "If one of you were to work on a solid rock with no door or window, Allah would bring out his deed for the people, whatever it may be."

Ibn al-Mundhir reports from Ikrimah concerning His saying: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah﴾, that he said: "They are the three who were left behind."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh report from Mujahid concerning the verse, that he said: "They are Hilal ibn Umayyah, Murarah ibn al-Rabi' and Ka'b ibn Malik, from the Aws and the Khazraj."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh report from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: ﴿Either He will punish them﴾, that he said: "He will cause them to die in disobedience." ﴿Or He will accept their repentance﴾: "So He deferred their matter, then abrogated it (nasakha, the technical sense of naskh, abrogation of a ruling by a later revelation), saying: ﴿and [He turned] to the three who were left behind﴾ [al-Tawbah: 118]."

When Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the categories of the Bedouins, He mentioned the Emigrants (al-Muhajirun) and the Helpers (al-Ansar), and made clear that among them are those who were foremost to emigrate, and among them are those who follow them.

It is narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read "wa al-Ansaru" (and the Helpers) in the nominative case, as a conjunction with "wa al-sabiquna" (and the foremost). The rest of the reciters among the Companions and those after them read it in the genitive case.

Al-Akhfash said: The genitive in "al-Ansar" is the more preferred reading, because the foremost among them are included in the phrase "wa al-sabiquna," and the verse signifies the preference of the first foremost ones among the Emigrants and the Helpers. They are the ones who prayed towards both qiblas (the Jerusalem and the Ka'bah), according to the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and a group. Or they are those who witnessed the Pledge of al-Ridwan, which is the Pledge of al-Hudaybiyah, according to the view of al-Sha'bi. Or they are the people of Badr, according to the view of (p-595) Muhammad ibn Ka'b and Ata' ibn Yasar. There is no obstacle to applying the verse to all of these categories. Abu Mansur al-Baghdadi said: Our companions (scholars) are unanimously agreed that the most excellent of them are the Four Caliphs, then the six remaining (of the ten promised Paradise), then the people of Badr, then the companions of Uhud, then the people of the Pledge of al-Ridwan at al-Hudaybiyah.

His saying: ﴿And those who followed them in goodness﴾. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, read "alladhina ittaba'uhum" (those who followed them) without the waw, as a description of the Helpers according to his reading with the nominative "al-Ansar." Zayd ibn Thabit disputed this with him, so he asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who confirmed Zayd's view, and so Umar retracted from the aforementioned reading, as narrated by Abu Ubayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh. The meaning of "those who followed them in goodness" is: those who followed the first foremost ones among the Emigrants and the Helpers, namely those who came after them among the Companions and those who came after them until the Day of Resurrection. The intended meaning here is not the "Tabi'un" (Successors) in the technical sense, who are everyone who met the Companions but did not meet the Prophet (ﷺ). Rather, they are among those included under the verse. Thus "min" in his saying ﴿from the Emigrants﴾ is, on this view, for partitive (tab'id). It has also been said that it is for explanation (bayan), in which case the praise encompasses all the Companions, and the intended meaning of the Successors are those who came after them of the Ummah until the Day of Resurrection.

His saying: "in goodness" is a restriction on the Successors. That is: those who followed them while being characterized by goodness in deeds and words, emulating the first foremost ones.

His saying: ﴿Allah is pleased with them﴾ is the predicate of the subject and what is conjoined to it. The meaning of His pleasure, glorified is He, with them is that He accepted their acts of obedience, overlooked their faults, and was not angry with them. ﴿And they are pleased with Him﴾ for what He has given them of His bounty. Along with His pleasure with them, ﴿He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ in the Hereafter.

Ibn Kathir read "tajri tahtaha al-anharu" (beneath which rivers flow) with the addition of "min." The rest read it without it, with the accusative case as an adverbial of place (zarfiyyah). The explanation of the flowing of rivers from beneath the gardens and the explanation of "khulud" (eternal abiding) and "fawz" (triumph) have already been mentioned.

His saying: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites﴾. This is a return to the explanation of the states of the hypocrites, from the people of Madinah and those near it among the Bedouins. "Wa mimman hawlakum" is a fronted predicate, "min al-a'rab" is an explanation, and it is in the place of an accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). "Munafiqun" is the subject. It has been said: those who are around Madinah among the hypocrites are Juhaynah, Muzaynah, Ashja' and Ghifar. The clause ﴿And among the people of Madinah are those who persisted in hypocrisy﴾ is conjoined to the first clause as a clause conjoined to a clause. 

It has also been said: "wa min ahl al-Madinah" is conjoined to the predicate in the first clause. According to the first view, the subject is implied: that is, "and among the people of Madinah are a people who persisted in hypocrisy." According to the second, the implied meaning is: "And among those around you of the Bedouins and among the people of Madinah are hypocrites who persisted." Since the clause "maradu 'ala al-nifaq" (they persisted in hypocrisy) is a resumptive clause with no place in the sentence, the root of "marada" and "tamarrada" is smoothness, bareness and stripping. So it is as if they stripped themselves for hypocrisy. From this comes "ghusnun amrad" (a branch with no leaves), "faras amrad" (a horse without hair), "ghulam amrad" (a beardless youth), "ard marda'" (a land without vegetation), and "sarh mumarrad" (a stripped, smooth palace). The meaning is: they remained in hypocrisy, held firm to it, and did not turn away from it.

Ibn Zayd said: its meaning is that they persisted in it and clung to it. The clause ﴿You do not know them﴾ explains the first clause, which is "marada 'ala al-nifaq," i.e. they held firmly to it with a strong steadfastness, and became so skilled in it that their affair was hidden from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so how about the rest of the believers? The intended meaning is the Prophet's (ﷺ) lack of knowledge of their individual identities, not in general, for the hypocrite has signs that are not hidden from him (ﷺ). The clause ﴿We know them﴾ confirms what precedes it, due to what it contains of the indication of their expertise in hypocrisy and their firm rootedness in it in a way that is hidden from humans, and is not manifest to anyone except Allah, glorified is He, because of His knowledge of what is concealed, what the hearts hide, and what the inner secrets conceal. Then He, glorified is He, threatened them, saying: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾. It has been said: the intended meaning of "twice" is the punishment of this world by killing and captivity, and the punishment of the Hereafter. It has also been said: it is disgrace by the exposure of their hypocrisy and punishment in the Hereafter. It has been said: it is calamities in their wealth and children, and the punishment of the grave. Other views have been stated, which are lengthy to mention, with no evidence that any of them is specifically intended.

The apparent view is that this repeated punishment is in this world, by that which truly is called punishment, and that they are punished time after time, and then they are returned after that to the punishment of the Hereafter. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾. Whoever said that the punishment in the second time is the punishment of the Hereafter said: the meaning of His saying ﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾ is that after their punishment in the Fire, they will be returned, like the rest of the disbelievers, to its lowest level, or that they will be punished in the Fire with a punishment specific to them apart from the rest of the disbelievers, and then after that they will be returned to the punishment that encompasses them and the rest of the disbelievers.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned the state of a group of Muslims, namely those who mixed their religion, and said: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾. This is conjoined to His saying "hypocrites," meaning: and among those around you of the Bedouins and among the people of Madinah there is another people. It is permissible that "akharun" (others) be the subject, "i'tarafu bi dhunubihim" (they acknowledged their sins) its description, and "khalatu 'amalan salihan wa akhara sayyi'an" (they mixed a righteous deed and another evil one) its predicate. The meaning is: this group lagged behind from the expedition without any acceptable excuse for lagging, then they regretted that, and did not offer false excuses as the hypocrites did, but rather repented, acknowledged the sin, and hoped that Allah would accept their repentance.

The righteous deed refers to what came before of their Islam, their upholding of the laws of Islam, and their going out to fight in all the battlefields. The evil deed refers to their lagging behind from this expedition, and they followed this evil deed with a righteous deed, which is acknowledging it and repenting from it.

The origin of "i'tiraf" (acknowledgment) is affirmation of a matter. Mere affirmation is not repentance unless it is accompanied by remorse for the past and resolve to abandon it presently and in the future. What occurred from them indicates this, as will be explained, Allah willing.

The meaning of "khalt" (mixing) is that they mixed each of the two with the other, like your saying: "I mixed the water with the milk and the milk with the water." It is permissible that the "wa" (and) carries the meaning of "ba'" (with), like your saying: "I sold the sheep for a sheep and a dirham," meaning: for a dirham. His saying: ﴿Perhaps Allah will accept their repentance﴾ is evidence that along with the acknowledgment, what indicates repentance had already occurred from them, or that the preliminary step of repentance, which is acknowledgment, took the place of repentance. The particle of hope, "'asa," in the speech of Allah, glorified is He, indicates the certainty of occurrence, because raising hopes from Allah, glorified is He, is an obligation, given that He is the most Generous of the generous. ﴿Indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (p-596), meaning He forgives sins and bestows favor upon His servants.

His saying: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾. The scholars differed concerning this commanded charity. It has been said: it is the obligatory charity (sadaqat al-fard). It has also been said: it is specific to this group that acknowledged their sins, because after Allah accepted their repentance, they presented their wealth to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and so this verse was revealed. "Min" is partitive according to both interpretations. The verse is absolute and is clarified by the pure Sunnah. The word "sadaqah" (charity) is derived from "sidq" (truthfulness), since it is evidence of the truthfulness of the one who gives it in his faith.

His saying: ﴿It purifies them and causes them to grow with it﴾. The pronoun in both verbs refers to the Prophet (ﷺ): that is, you, O Muhammad, purify them and cause them to grow by what you take from them of the charity. It has also been said: the pronoun in "yutahhiruhum" refers to the charity, meaning this charity taken from them purifies them, and the pronoun in "yuzakkihim" refers to the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning: you, O Muhammad, cause them to grow with the charity taken. The first is preferable, because the second involves a difference in the pronouns of the two conjoined verbs. According to the first, the two verbs are in the accusative as a circumstantial state, and according to the second, the first verb is a description of "sadaqatan" (a charity) and the second is a circumstantial state of it (ﷺ).

The meaning of purification (tathhir) is removing what traces of sins remain upon them, and the meaning of growth (tazkiyah) is intensifying the purification.

Al-Zajjaj said: The better view is that the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning: indeed you, O Muhammad, purify them and cause them to grow with it, as a definite and new statement. It is permissible to read it in the jussive case as a response to the imperative. The meaning is: that you take from their wealth a charity which purifies them. 

Al-Hasan read "tutahhiruhum" in the jussive. On this reading, "wa tuzakkihim" is by implication of a subject: that is, "and you cause them to grow."

His saying: ﴿And pray for them﴾: that is, supplicate for them after your taking that charity from their wealth.

Al-Nahhas said: The people of the language have all agreed, as far as we know, that "salat" (prayer) in the speech of the Arabs means supplication. Then Allah, glorified is He, gave the reason for His command to His Messenger (ﷺ) to pray for those from whom he takes charity, saying: ﴿Indeed your prayer is a tranquility for them﴾.

Hafs, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "salataka" (your prayer) in the singular, and the rest read it in the plural. "Sakan" (tranquility) is that in which the soul finds rest and is reassured.

His saying: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants﴾. When Allah, glorified is He, accepted repentance from these people mentioned previously, Allah said: ﴿Do they not know﴾, that is, those who had not repented, or those who had repented before Allah accepted their repentance and accepted their charities, ﴿that it is Allah who accepts repentance﴾ because He is independent of the obedience of the obedient and does not care for the disobedience of the disobedient.

It has been read as "tu'lamu" (do you not know) with the second person, which is either addressed to the repentant ones, or to a group of believers. The meaning of ﴿and takes charities﴾ is: He accepts them from them. In attributing the taking to Him, glorified is He, after His command to His Messenger (ﷺ) to take them, there is great honor for this act of obedience and for those who perform it.

His saying: ﴿And that Allah is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful﴾ is conjoined to His saying: ﴿that Allah is the one who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, along with its inclusion of an emphasis of what the conjoined clause contains: that is, this is His, glorified is He, characteristic.

In the form of intensive emphasis in "al-Tawwab" (the Accepter of repentance) and "al-Rahim" (the Merciful), along with the placement of the separating pronoun and the emphasis, there is evident good news for His servants and encouragement for them.

His saying: ﴿And say: Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger and the believers﴾. In it is a warning and threat: that is, your deeds are not hidden from Allah, nor from His Messenger, nor from the believers. So hasten to deeds of goodness and make your deeds sincere for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. In it also is encouragement and enlivening: for whoever knows that his deed will not be hidden, whether good or bad, will be eager for deeds of goodness and will avoid deeds of evil. How excellent is the saying of Zuhayr:

The poem line is rendered as it stands:

"Whatever disposition a man may have, however well it is hidden from people, it will become known."

The meaning of "seeing" here is knowledge of the deeds that proceed from them. Then Allah, glorified is He, issued a severe warning, saying: ﴿And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed.﴾ That is, after death you will be returned to Allah, glorified is He, who knows what you conceal, what you disclose, what you hide and what you show. Placing "the unseen" before "the witnessed" indicates the vastness of His knowledge, glorified and exalted is He, that nothing is hidden from Him, and that every object of knowledge is equal to Him.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned what will happen after their return to Him, saying: ﴿then He will inform you﴾, that is, He will tell you ﴿of what you used to do﴾ in the world. He will then reward the good-doer for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil, and He bestows His grace upon whom He wills of His servants.

As for His saying ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah﴾: He, glorified is He, mentioned three categories among those who stayed behind. The first: the hypocrites who persisted in hypocrisy (marada, "became hardened in it"). The second: the penitent who acknowledged their sins. The third: those whose matter remained suspended in that state, and they are "those deferred to the command of Allah," from arjaytuhu and arja'tuhu, meaning "I postponed it."

Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Nafi' and Hafs read ﴿murjawna﴾ with a waw and without a hamza. The rest read it with a hamza after the jim, with a damma.

The meaning is that they are postponed in that state: no verdict is given for them regarding repentance or its absence, but they remain as Allah, glorified is He, will make clear regarding their situation. ﴿Either He will punish them﴾ if they remain in their present condition and do not repent, ﴿or He will accept their repentance﴾ if they repent with sincere repentance and devote themselves to it completely. The clause is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal), and the sense is: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah﴾ while they are either punished or forgiven. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of their circumstances, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in what He does to them, whether good or evil.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah report from Abu Musa that he was asked about His saying: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the emigrants and the helpers﴾, and he said: they are those who prayed towards both qiblahs (Jerusalem and the Ka'bah).

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu'aym report from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib the same.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu Nu'aym report from al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn Sirin the same as well.

Ibn Mardawayh reports from Ibn Abbas that he said: they are Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, Salman and Ammar ibn Yasir.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah report from al-Sha'bi that he said: they are those who attained the Pledge of Ridwan.

Ibn Abi Hatim reports from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿and those who followed them in goodness﴾, that he said: they are the Successors (tabi'un).

Ibn Abi Hatim reports from Ibn Zayd that he said: they are whoever remains of the people of Islam until the Hour is established.

Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Asakir report from Abu Sakhr Humayd ibn Ziyad, who said: I said to Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: "Tell me about the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," and I only meant the strife (that occurred among them). He said: Allah has indeed forgiven all the companions of the Prophet ﷺ and has made Paradise obligatory for them in His Book, both their good-doers and their wrong-doers. I said to him: "In which place did Allah make Paradise obligatory for them in His Book?" He said: "Do you not read His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the foremost, the first...﴾ to the end of the verse," and He made Paradise and His good pleasure obligatory for all the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and He stipulated a condition upon the Successors that He did not stipulate for them. I said: "And what condition did He stipulate upon them?" He said: "He stipulated upon them that they follow them in goodness," meaning: that they imitate them in their good deeds, and not imitate them in anything other than that.

Abu Sakhr said: "By Allah, it is as if I had never read it before, and I had not known its interpretation until Ibn Ka'b recited it to me."

Ibn Mardawayh reports through al-Awza'i, who said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, al-Qasim, Makhul, Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah and Hassan ibn Atiyyah told me that they heard a group of the companions of the Prophet ﷺ saying: "When this verse was revealed, ﴿And the foremost, the first...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and they are pleased with Him﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'This is for all my nation, and there is no displeasure after pleasure.'"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh report from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins﴾ up to the end of the verse, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up on a Friday to deliver a sermon, and said: 'Stand up, so-and-so, and leave, for you are a hypocrite. Leave, so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite.' He brought them out by their names and exposed them. Umar ibn al-Khattab had not attended that Friday prayer because of some need he had, so Umar met them as they were leaving the mosque, and he hid from them out of shame that he had not attended the Friday prayer. They assumed the people had dispersed, and they hid from Umar, thinking he had learned of their affair. Umar entered the mosque and found the people had not dispersed. A man said to him: 'Rejoice, O Umar, for Allah has today exposed the hypocrites.'" So that is the first punishment, and the second punishment is the punishment of the grave.

Ibn al-Mundhir reports from Ikrimah concerning His saying: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins﴾, that he said: they are Juhaynah, Muzaynah, Ash'a, Aslam and Ghifar.

Ibn Abi Hatim reports from Ibn Zayd concerning His saying: ﴿They became hardened in hypocrisy﴾, that he said: they persisted in it and did not repent as others repented.

Ibn al-Mundhir reports from Ibn Jurayj concerning the verse, that he said: they died upon it: Abdullah ibn Ubayy, Abu Amir the monk, and al-Jadd ibn Qays.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh report from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾, that he said: "with hunger and killing."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh report from Abu Malik, who said: "with hunger and the punishment of the grave."

Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and al-Bayhaqi report from Qatadah, who said: "a punishment in the grave, and a punishment in the Fire."

Similar statements have been reported from a number of the early generations (salaf) regarding the identification of the two punishments, but the apparent meaning is what we have mentioned earlier.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il report from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And others who acknowledged their sins, having mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾, that he said: "They were ten men who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the Battle of Tabuk. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was about to return, seven of them tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque. The Prophet ﷺ used to pass by them when he returned. When he saw them he said: 'Who are these who have tied themselves up?' They said: 'This is Abu Lubabah and companions of his who stayed behind from you, O Messenger of Allah, until you release them and excuse them.' He said: 'And I swear by Allah I will not release them or excuse them until Allah is the One who releases them. They turned away from me and stayed behind from the expedition with the Muslims.' When this reached them, they said: 'And we will not release ourselves until Allah is the One who releases us.' So ﴿It may be that Allah will accept their repentance﴾ was revealed, and 'it may be' from Allah is binding. When it was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ sent for them, released them and excused them. They came with their wealth and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this is our wealth, so give it in charity on our behalf and ask forgiveness for us.' He said: 'I have not been commanded to take your wealth.' Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and invoke blessings upon them﴾, meaning: ask forgiveness for them. ﴿Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾, meaning: a mercy for them. So he took the charity from them and asked forgiveness for them. There were three men who had not tied themselves to the pillars, so they were deferred for a year, not knowing whether they would be punished or forgiven. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet﴾ [al-Tawbah: 117] to His saying: ﴿and to the three who were left behind﴾, to His saying: ﴿Then He turned to them that they might repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾ [al-Tawbah: 118], meaning: if they become upright."

Abu al-Shaykh reports from al-Dahhak the same, without difference.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il report from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿acknowledged their sins﴾, that he said: "It is Abu Lubabah, when he said to the Qurayzah what he said, and he gestured to his throat, meaning that Muhammad would slaughter you if you came down under his judgment." The story is mentioned in the books of biography (siyar).

Ibn Abi Hatim reports from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: ﴿they mixed a righteous deed﴾, that he said: "Their fighting alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." ﴿And another evil﴾: "Their staying behind from him."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh report from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿and invoke blessings upon them﴾, that he said: "Ask forgiveness for them for their sins which they had committed." ﴿Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾: "a mercy for them."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others report from Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, who said: "When charity was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would say: 'O Allah, bless the family of so-and-so.' My father brought him his charity, and he said: 'O Allah, bless the family of Abi Awfa.'"

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh report from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿Act, for Allah will see your deed, and so will His Messenger﴾, that he said: "This is a warning from Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Ahmad, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, and al-Diya in al-Mukhtarah report from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "If one of you were to work on a solid rock with no door or window, Allah would bring out his deed for the people, whatever it may be."

Ibn al-Mundhir reports from Ikrimah concerning His saying: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah﴾, that he said: "They are the three who were left behind."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh report from Mujahid concerning the verse, that he said: "They are Hilal ibn Umayyah, Murarah ibn al-Rabi' and Ka'b ibn Malik, from the Aws and the Khazraj."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh report from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: ﴿Either He will punish them﴾, that he said: "He will cause them to die in disobedience." ﴿Or He will accept their repentance﴾: "So He deferred their matter, then abrogated it (nasakha, the technical sense of naskh, abrogation of a ruling by a later revelation), saying: ﴿and [He turned] to the three who were left behind﴾ [al-Tawbah: 118]."

When Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the categories of the Bedouins, He mentioned the Emigrants (al-Muhajirun) and the Helpers (al-Ansar), and made clear that among them are those who were foremost to emigrate, and among them are those who follow them.

It is narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read "wa al-Ansaru" (and the Helpers) in the nominative case, as a conjunction with "wa al-sabiquna" (and the foremost). The rest of the reciters among the Companions and those after them read it in the genitive case.

Al-Akhfash said: The genitive in "al-Ansar" is the more preferred reading, because the foremost among them are included in the phrase "wa al-sabiquna," and the verse signifies the preference of the first foremost ones among the Emigrants and the Helpers. They are the ones who prayed towards both qiblas (the Jerusalem and the Ka'bah), according to the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and a group. Or they are those who witnessed the Pledge of al-Ridwan, which is the Pledge of al-Hudaybiyah, according to the view of al-Sha'bi. Or they are the people of Badr, according to the view of (p-595) Muhammad ibn Ka'b and Ata' ibn Yasar. There is no obstacle to applying the verse to all of these categories. Abu Mansur al-Baghdadi said: Our companions (scholars) are unanimously agreed that the most excellent of them are the Four Caliphs, then the six remaining (of the ten promised Paradise), then the people of Badr, then the companions of Uhud, then the people of the Pledge of al-Ridwan at al-Hudaybiyah.

His saying: ﴿And those who followed them in goodness﴾. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, read "alladhina ittaba'uhum" (those who followed them) without the waw, as a description of the Helpers according to his reading with the nominative "al-Ansar." Zayd ibn Thabit disputed this with him, so he asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who confirmed Zayd's view, and so Umar retracted from the aforementioned reading, as narrated by Abu Ubayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh. The meaning of "those who followed them in goodness" is: those who followed the first foremost ones among the Emigrants and the Helpers, namely those who came after them among the Companions and those who came after them until the Day of Resurrection. The intended meaning here is not the "Tabi'un" (Successors) in the technical sense, who are everyone who met the Companions but did not meet the Prophet (ﷺ). Rather, they are among those included under the verse. Thus "min" in his saying ﴿from the Emigrants﴾ is, on this view, for partitive (tab'id). It has also been said that it is for explanation (bayan), in which case the praise encompasses all the Companions, and the intended meaning of the Successors are those who came after them of the Ummah until the Day of Resurrection.

His saying: "in goodness" is a restriction on the Successors. That is: those who followed them while being characterized by goodness in deeds and words, emulating the first foremost ones.

His saying: ﴿Allah is pleased with them﴾ is the predicate of the subject and what is conjoined to it. The meaning of His pleasure, glorified is He, with them is that He accepted their acts of obedience, overlooked their faults, and was not angry with them. ﴿And they are pleased with Him﴾ for what He has given them of His bounty. Along with His pleasure with them, ﴿He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ in the Hereafter.

Ibn Kathir read "tajri tahtaha al-anharu" (beneath which rivers flow) with the addition of "min." The rest read it without it, with the accusative case as an adverbial of place (zarfiyyah). The explanation of the flowing of rivers from beneath the gardens and the explanation of "khulud" (eternal abiding) and "fawz" (triumph) have already been mentioned.

His saying: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites﴾. This is a return to the explanation of the states of the hypocrites, from the people of Madinah and those near it among the Bedouins. "Wa mimman hawlakum" is a fronted predicate, "min al-a'rab" is an explanation, and it is in the place of an accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). "Munafiqun" is the subject. It has been said: those who are around Madinah among the hypocrites are Juhaynah, Muzaynah, Ashja' and Ghifar. The clause ﴿And among the people of Madinah are those who persisted in hypocrisy﴾ is conjoined to the first clause as a clause conjoined to a clause. 

It has also been said: "wa min ahl al-Madinah" is conjoined to the predicate in the first clause. According to the first view, the subject is implied: that is, "and among the people of Madinah are a people who persisted in hypocrisy." According to the second, the implied meaning is: "And among those around you of the Bedouins and among the people of Madinah are hypocrites who persisted." Since the clause "maradu 'ala al-nifaq" (they persisted in hypocrisy) is a resumptive clause with no place in the sentence, the root of "marada" and "tamarrada" is smoothness, bareness and stripping. So it is as if they stripped themselves for hypocrisy. From this comes "ghusnun amrad" (a branch with no leaves), "faras amrad" (a horse without hair), "ghulam amrad" (a beardless youth), "ard marda'" (a land without vegetation), and "sarh mumarrad" (a stripped, smooth palace). The meaning is: they remained in hypocrisy, held firm to it, and did not turn away from it.

Ibn Zayd said: its meaning is that they persisted in it and clung to it. The clause ﴿You do not know them﴾ explains the first clause, which is "marada 'ala al-nifaq," i.e. they held firmly to it with a strong steadfastness, and became so skilled in it that their affair was hidden from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so how about the rest of the believers? The intended meaning is the Prophet's (ﷺ) lack of knowledge of their individual identities, not in general, for the hypocrite has signs that are not hidden from him (ﷺ). The clause ﴿We know them﴾ confirms what precedes it, due to what it contains of the indication of their expertise in hypocrisy and their firm rootedness in it in a way that is hidden from humans, and is not manifest to anyone except Allah, glorified is He, because of His knowledge of what is concealed, what the hearts hide, and what the inner secrets conceal. Then He, glorified is He, threatened them, saying: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾. It has been said: the intended meaning of "twice" is the punishment of this world by killing and captivity, and the punishment of the Hereafter. It has also been said: it is disgrace by the exposure of their hypocrisy and punishment in the Hereafter. It has been said: it is calamities in their wealth and children, and the punishment of the grave. Other views have been stated, which are lengthy to mention, with no evidence that any of them is specifically intended.

The apparent view is that this repeated punishment is in this world, by that which truly is called punishment, and that they are punished time after time, and then they are returned after that to the punishment of the Hereafter. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾. Whoever said that the punishment in the second time is the punishment of the Hereafter said: the meaning of His saying ﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾ is that after their punishment in the Fire, they will be returned, like the rest of the disbelievers, to its lowest level, or that they will be punished in the Fire with a punishment specific to them apart from the rest of the disbelievers, and then after that they will be returned to the punishment that encompasses them and the rest of the disbelievers.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned the state of a group of Muslims, namely those who mixed their religion, and said: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾. This is conjoined to His saying "hypocrites," meaning: and among those around you of the Bedouins and among the people of Madinah there is another people. It is permissible that "akharun" (others) be the subject, "i'tarafu bi dhunubihim" (they acknowledged their sins) its description, and "khalatu 'amalan salihan wa akhara sayyi'an" (they mixed a righteous deed and another evil one) its predicate. The meaning is: this group lagged behind from the expedition without any acceptable excuse for lagging, then they regretted that, and did not offer false excuses as the hypocrites did, but rather repented, acknowledged the sin, and hoped that Allah would accept their repentance.

The righteous deed refers to what came before of their Islam, their upholding of the laws of Islam, and their going out to fight in all the battlefields. The evil deed refers to their lagging behind from this expedition, and they followed this evil deed with a righteous deed, which is acknowledging it and repenting from it.

The origin of "i'tiraf" (acknowledgment) is affirmation of a matter. Mere affirmation is not repentance unless it is accompanied by remorse for the past and resolve to abandon it presently and in the future. What occurred from them indicates this, as will be explained, Allah willing.

The meaning of "khalt" (mixing) is that they mixed each of the two with the other, like your saying: "I mixed the water with the milk and the milk with the water." It is permissible that the "wa" (and) carries the meaning of "ba'" (with), like your saying: "I sold the sheep for a sheep and a dirham," meaning: for a dirham. His saying: ﴿Perhaps Allah will accept their repentance﴾ is evidence that along with the acknowledgment, what indicates repentance had already occurred from them, or that the preliminary step of repentance, which is acknowledgment, took the place of repentance. The particle of hope, "'asa," in the speech of Allah, glorified is He, indicates the certainty of occurrence, because raising hopes from Allah, glorified is He, is an obligation, given that He is the most Generous of the generous. ﴿Indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (p-596), meaning He forgives sins and bestows favor upon His servants.

His saying: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾. The scholars differed concerning this commanded charity. It has been said: it is the obligatory charity (sadaqat al-fard). It has also been said: it is specific to this group that acknowledged their sins, because after Allah accepted their repentance, they presented their wealth to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and so this verse was revealed. "Min" is partitive according to both interpretations. The verse is absolute and is clarified by the pure Sunnah. The word "sadaqah" (charity) is derived from "sidq" (truthfulness), since it is evidence of the truthfulness of the one who gives it in his faith.

His saying: ﴿It purifies them and causes them to grow with it﴾. The pronoun in both verbs refers to the Prophet (ﷺ): that is, you, O Muhammad, purify them and cause them to grow by what you take from them of the charity. It has also been said: the pronoun in "yutahhiruhum" refers to the charity, meaning this charity taken from them purifies them, and the pronoun in "yuzakkihim" refers to the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning: you, O Muhammad, cause them to grow with the charity taken. The first is preferable, because the second involves a difference in the pronouns of the two conjoined verbs. According to the first, the two verbs are in the accusative as a circumstantial state, and according to the second, the first verb is a description of "sadaqatan" (a charity) and the second is a circumstantial state of it (ﷺ).

The meaning of purification (tathhir) is removing what traces of sins remain upon them, and the meaning of growth (tazkiyah) is intensifying the purification.

Al-Zajjaj said: The better view is that the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning: indeed you, O Muhammad, purify them and cause them to grow with it, as a definite and new statement. It is permissible to read it in the jussive case as a response to the imperative. The meaning is: that you take from their wealth a charity which purifies them. 

Al-Hasan read "tutahhiruhum" in the jussive. On this reading, "wa tuzakkihim" is by implication of a subject: that is, "and you cause them to grow."

His saying: ﴿And pray for them﴾: that is, supplicate for them after your taking that charity from their wealth.
