Abu Amir al-Rahib said to them: "Build your mosque and gather whatever strength and weapons you can, for I am going to Qaysar, king of the Romans, and I will bring an army of Romans, and I will expel Muhammad and his companions." When they finished their mosque, they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "We have finished building our mosque, so it is incumbent upon you to pray in it and invoke blessing." Then Allah revealed: ﴿Do not stand in it ever.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him that he said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) built the mosque of Quba', men from the Ansar went out, among them Bajdah, the grandfather of Abdullah ibn Hunayf, and Wadi'ah ibn Hizam, and Mujammi' ibn Jariyah al-Ansari, and they built the mosque of hypocrisy. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Bajdah: 'Woe to you, O Bajdah! What did you intend by what I see?' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I intended nothing but good,' and he was lying. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) believed him and wished to excuse him. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief and causing division among the believers and lying in wait for the one who waged war against Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning a man called Abu Amir who had been waging war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He had set off to Heraclius, and they used to watch, so that when Abu Amir came, he would pray in it. He had left Madinah waging war against Allah and His Messenger."

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him, likewise, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, and Malik said to Asim: 'Wait for me until I bring you a fire from my family.' He entered upon his family and took some palm fronds of fire, then they came out running until they entered the mosque, while its people were in it. They burned it and demolished it, and its people came out and dispersed from it. Then Allah revealed this verse."

[p. 599]

Al-Shawkani's commentary on surah 9, verses 107–110 (part 2 of 2):

It is possible that this narration omits something between his (ﷺ) saying "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum" and the words "Malik said to Asim." This is clarified by what Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Abu Ruhm Kulthum ibn al-Husayn al-Ghifari, who was among the Companions who pledged allegiance under the tree, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived and halted at Dhu Awan, a place between him and Madinah, for an hour of the day. The people of the Mosque of Harm (Masjid al-Dirar) had come to him while he was preparing for Tabuk and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we have built a mosque for the sick, the needy, the nights of cold and the nights of rain, and we wish that you would come to us and pray in it for us.' He said: 'I am on the verge of a journey. If we return, God willing, we will come to you and pray for you in it.' When he halted at Dhu Awan, news of the mosque reached him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, brother of the Banu Salim ibn Awf, and Ma'n ibn Adi, and his brother Asim ibn Adi, one of the Banu al-Ajlan, and said: 'Go to this mosque whose people are wrongdoers, demolish it and burn it.' They set out quickly until they reached the Banu Salim ibn Awf, who were the kin of Malik ibn al-Dukhshum. Malik said to Ma'n: 'Wait for me until I come out to you.' He entered his family's house, took a palm frond, lit fire to it, then they both came out running, while its people were inside it, and they burned it and demolished it, and its people dispersed from it. And there was revealed concerning them what was revealed of the Qur'an: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief﴾," and so on to the end of the story.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted that those who built the Mosque of Harm were twelve men, and they mentioned their names.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il transmitted from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "Two men disputed: a man from the Banu Khudrah, and in another wording: I and a man from the Banu Amr ibn Awf disputed concerning the mosque that was founded upon piety (taqwa). The Khudri said: 'It is the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' The Umari said: 'It is the Mosque of Quba'.' They both came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and asked him about it. He said: 'It is this mosque,' meaning the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah, and he said: 'In it there is much good,' meaning the Mosque of Quba'."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar in Akhbar al-Madinah, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim in al-Kuna, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi something similar.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Khatib, and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtara transmitted from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the mosque that was founded upon piety, and he said: 'It is this mosque of mine.'"

Al-Tabarani and al-Diya' al-Maqdisi in al-Mukhtara transmitted from Zayd ibn Thabit, as a marfu' report, something like it.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Tabarani transmitted through the chain of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "The mosque that was founded upon piety from the first day is the Mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Urwah said: "The Mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ) is better than it; it was only revealed concerning the Mosque of Quba'."

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Umar, who said: "The mosque that was founded upon piety is the Mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

The two mentioned (Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Mardawayh) transmitted from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri something similar.

It has been related from a group other than these the same as their statement.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il transmitted from Ibn Abbas that it is the Mosque of Quba'.

Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from al-Dahhak something similar.

It is not hidden from you that the Prophet (ﷺ) specified this mosque that was founded upon piety and affirmed with certainty that it is his mosque (ﷺ), as we have mentioned from the authentic hadiths. Therefore, the statement of an individual Companion, or a group of them, or others, does not stand against that, nor is it valid to cite it in opposition to what has been authentically established from the Prophet (ﷺ). There is also no benefit in citing what has come concerning the merit of praying in the Mosque of Quba', for that does not necessitate that it is the mosque founded upon piety. Moreover, what has come concerning the virtues of the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is, beyond any doubt or uncertainty, far greater than what has come concerning the merit of the Mosque of Quba'.

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "This verse was revealed concerning the people of Quba': ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾." He said: "They used to cleanse themselves with water, so this was revealed concerning them." In its chain is Yunus ibn al-Harith, who is weak.

Al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas, who said: "When this verse was revealed: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for Uwaym ibn Sa'idah and said: 'What is this purification by which God has praised you?' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, no man or woman among us comes out from the toilet without washing his private part,' or he said: 'his anus.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'That is it.'"

Ahmad, Ibn Khuzaymah, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Uwaym ibn Sa'idah al-Ansari that the Prophet (ﷺ) came to them at the Mosque of Quba' and said: "God has praised you well concerning purification in the story of your mosque. What is this purification with which you purify yourselves?" They said: "By God, O Messenger of Allah, we know nothing except that we had Jewish neighbours, who used to wash their posteriors after defecation, so we washed as they washed." Ahmad narrated it from Hasan ibn Muhammad.

Abu Uways narrated to us, Shurahbil narrated to us, from Uwaym ibn Sa'idah, and he mentioned it.

Ibn Khuzaymah also transmitted it in his Sahih.

Ibn Majah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Jarud in al-Muntaqa, al-Daraqutni, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir transmitted from Talhah ibn Nafi', who said: "Abu Ayyub, Jabir ibn Abd Allah, and Anas ibn Malik narrated to me that when this verse was revealed: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O assembly of the Ansar, God has praised you well concerning purification. What is this purification of yours?' They said: 'We perform ablution for prayer and bathe from major impurity.' He said: 'Is there anything with that besides it?' They said: 'No, except that when one of us goes out to relieve himself, he loves to cleanse himself with water.' He said: 'That is it, so adhere to it.'"

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Bukhari in his Tarikh, Ibn Jarir, al-Baghawi in his Mu'jam, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah transmitted from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam, from his father, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to the mosque that was founded upon piety, the Mosque of Quba', he said: 'God has praised you well concerning purification. Will you not tell me?' meaning His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves﴾. They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we find it written upon us in the Torah: cleansing with water, and we do it today.'"

The chain of Ahmad in this hadith is thus: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Malik, meaning Ibn Mighwal, narrated to me, I heard Sayyar Abu al-Hakim, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam.

It has been related from a group of the Successors (tabi'un) something like this concerning the mention of the occasion of revelation of the verse.

It is not hidden from you that some of these hadiths do not contain the identification of the Mosque of Quba' and its people; some are weak; and some have no explicit statement that the mosque founded upon piety is the Mosque of Quba'. In any case, those hadiths that explicitly state that the mosque founded upon piety is the Mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ) are not outweighed by these, in their authenticity and clarity.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿So it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell﴾, that he said: "Meaning its foundations in the fire of Hell."

Musaddad in his Musnad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: "I saw the smoke coming out of the Mosque of Harm at the place where it collapsed, in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il transmitted from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Their building which they built will not cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts﴾, that he said: "Meaning doubt." ﴿Unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾, meaning death.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from Habib ibn Abi Thabit concerning His saying: ﴿a source of doubt in their hearts﴾, that he said: "Rage in their hearts." ﴿Unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾, he said: "Until they die."

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Sufyan concerning His saying: ﴿Unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾, that he said: "Unless they repent."

The commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 9, verses 107–110 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah mentioned the categories of the hypocrites and explained their various ways, He linked to what preceded this group of them, namely those who took a mosque for harm (masjid dirar). The sense is: "And among them are those who took..." The relative pronoun alladhina is a subject (mubtada', the grammatical subject of a nominal sentence), and its predicate (khabar, the grammatical predicate) is the omitted "from among them" (minhum). The sentence is conjoined to what came before it. It is also permissible for the relative clause to be in the accusative position, as a form of censure (dhamm).

The Madinans and Ibn Amir read "alladhina ittakhadhu" without the conjunction waw. In that case it is an independent narrative, with the relative pronoun as subject and its predicate being "do not stand" (la taqum). This was stated by al-Kisa'i.

Al-Nahhas said: the predicate is "their building which they built will never cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts" (la yazalu bunyanuhumu alladhi banaw). It was also said that the predicate is omitted, and the sense is "they will be punished." The identity of those who built the mosque of harm will be explained later. The word dirar (harm) is in the accusative, either as a verbal noun (masdar) or as a causal accusative (ʿillah). The words "disbelief, causing division among the believers, and lying in wait" (wa kufran wa tafriqan bayna al-mu'minin wa irsadan) are conjoined to dirar.

Allah, glory be to Him, has informed us that the motives for their building this mosque were four:

The first: harming others, which is causing injury.

The second: disbelief in Allah and boasting over the people of Islam, because by building it they intended to strengthen the people of hypocrisy.

The third: dividing the believers, because they wanted that they would not attend the mosque of Quba', so that the congregation of the Muslims would diminish. In this there is a considerable amount of discord in unity and the destruction of harmony, which is not hidden.

The fourth: lying in wait (irsad) for the one who waged war against Allah and His Messenger. That is, preparing (i'dad) for the sake of the one who waged war against Allah and His Messenger.

Al-Zajjaj said: irsad means waiting (intizar).

Ibn Qutayba said: irsad means waiting combined with enmity.

Most of the scholars said: it means preparing (i'dad), and the meanings are close. It is said: "arsadtu li-kadha" when I prepared it while watching for it.

Abu Zayd said: it is said "rasadtuhu" and "arsadtuhu" for good, and "arsadtu lahu" for evil.

Ibn al-A'rabi said: one only says "arsadtu," and its meaning is "irtaqabtu" (I awaited).

By "the one who waged war against Allah and His Messenger" is meant the hypocrites, and among them Abu Amir al-Rahib. That is, they prepared it for these people, watched for their arrival, and waited for them, so that they would pray in it and thereby boast over the believers. His saying "min qabl" (beforehand) is linked to "ittakhadhu" (took), meaning they took a mosque before these people became hypocrites and built the mosque of harm. Or it is linked to "harab" (waged war), meaning: for the one who had waged war against Allah and His Messenger before the building of the mosque of harm.

His saying: ﴿And they will surely swear, "We intended nothing but good."﴾ means: we intended nothing but the good quality, which is kindness toward the Muslims. Allah refuted them with His saying: ﴿And Allah testifies that they are liars﴾ in what they swore to.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, forbade His Messenger (ﷺ) from praying in the mosque of harm, saying: ﴿Do not stand in it ever.﴾ That is, at any time. The prohibition on standing in it entails the prohibition on praying in it.

Prayer is sometimes expressed by "standing" (qiyam). One says: "So-and-so stands at night" (yaqumu al-layl), meaning he prays. From this is the sound hadith: "Whoever stands in Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven."

Then Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned the reason for the prohibition on standing in it, saying: ﴿Surely a mosque founded upon piety from the first day is more worthy that you stand in it.﴾ The lam in "la-masjidun" is the lam of oath, and it was also said it is the lam of initiation (ibtida'), and in it there is emphasis on the content of the sentence. The "foundation" (ta'sis) of a building is its establishment and raising. The meaning of its being founded upon piety is that it was founded upon the qualities by which one guards oneself against punishment.

The scholars differed about the mosque that was founded upon piety. One group said it is the mosque of Quba', as narrated from Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, and others. Others held that it is the mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ). The first view is more preponderant, for reasons that will come shortly, if Allah wills.

﴿From the first day﴾ is linked to "was founded" (ussisa): that is, it was founded upon piety from the first day of the days of its founding.

Some grammarians said: "min" here has the meaning of "mundhu" (since): that is, since the first day on which its building began. His saying ﴿is more worthy that you stand in it﴾ is the predicate of the subject.

The meaning is: if standing in any other place were permissible, this mosque would be more fitting for your standing in it, for prayer and the remembrance of Allah, because it was founded upon piety from the first day, and because ﴿in it are men who love to purify themselves﴾. This clause is a new sentence (isti'naf) explaining the greater right of his (ﷺ) standing in it. That is: just as this mosque is more fitting in terms of its location, it is also more fitting in terms of the condition of those in it. It is permissible for this clause to be in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: while in it are men who love to purify themselves. It is also permissible for it to be another attribute of "masjid."

The meaning of their love for purification is that they prefer it and are eager for it whenever its requirement arises. It was also said the meaning is: they love to purify themselves from sins through repentance and seeking forgiveness. The first is more preferable.

It was also said: they love to be purified by the purifying fever from sins, so they all got fever. This view is very weak.

The meaning of Allah's love for them is His good pleasure with them and His kindness toward them, as the lover does with the beloved.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, explained that there is a vast difference between the two groups, saying: ﴿Is one who founded his building upon the fear of Allah and His pleasure better, or one who founded his building on the brink of a crumbling bank that collapsed with him into the fire of Hell?﴾ The interrogative hamza here is for affirmative denial (inkar taqriri). The word bunyan is a verbal noun like 'umran, but here it is used to mean the thing built. The sentence is a new sentence. The meaning: whoever founded the building of his religion upon a strong and firm foundation, which is the fear of Allah and His good pleasure, is better than whoever founded his religion upon the opposite of that, which is falsehood and hypocrisy. The relative pronoun "man" is the subject, and its predicate is "khayr" (better). It was read as "asssa bunyanahu" with the verb in the active voice and "bunyanahu" in the accusative. Abu Ubayda chose this reading. It was also read in the passive voice. It was read "asasu bunyanihi" with "asas" in construct with "bunyanihi." It was read "ussu bunyanihi." The intended meaning is the bases of the building. Abu Hatim transmitted another reading, "a'sas bunyanihi," in the plural. From it is the verse:

"The kingdom has become firm in its foundations, by the noble men of the sons of al-Abbas."

The shafa is the edge, and the jurf is what is swept away by torrents, namely the banks that are carried away by water. The ijtiraf is the uprooting of a thing from its base. It was read with the "ra'" vowelled with a damma, from "jarafa," and also with it unvowelled.

The har is what has fallen. It is said "har al-bina'" when the building collapsed. Its origin is "ha'ir," as they said "shak al-silah" and "shA'ik kadha," as al-Zajjaj said.

Abu Hatim said its origin is "ha'wir."

In Shams al-Ulum it is said: the jurf is what the flood has undermined at its base, and whose top has overhung. If its top splits, then it is the har. End of quotation.

Allah, glory be to Him, made this an example of what they built their false religion upon, which quickly collapses and vanishes. Then He said: ﴿So it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell.﴾ The subject of "fa-inhara" (so it collapsed) is a pronoun referring to the jurf: that is, the bank collapsed with the building into the fire. It is also permissible for the pronoun in "bihi" (with him) to refer to "man," who is the builder.

The meaning is: falsehood collapsed with the builder, or the builder collapsed into the fire of Hell. The collapse, which belongs to the bank, is used as a "tarshih" (a supporting feature that reinforces a metaphor). Glory be to Allah, how eloquent this speech is, how strong its composition, how precise its meaning, and how clear its form.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned that their building this was the cause of increased doubt and continued hesitation and uncertainty. He said: ﴿Their building which they built will never cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts﴾ that is, a state of uncertainty (shakk) in their hearts and hypocrisy. From this is the saying of al-Nabigha:

"I swore, and I left you no doubt in yourself, and there is no refuge for a man beyond Allah."

It was said that the meaning of "rayb" is grief and regret, because they regretted its building. Al-Mubarrad said: that is, heat and rage.

These people who built the mosque of harm were hypocrites who were doubtful about their religion, but they increased in hypocrisy, in determination upon disbelief, and in hatred of Islam, through the demolition by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because of the severe rage and great anger that befell them through its demolition. Then Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned what indicates the continuation and persistence of this doubt, which is His saying: ﴿Except that their hearts be cut into pieces.﴾ That is, this doubt will not cease unless their hearts are cut into pieces and broken into parts, either by death or by the sword. The intended meaning is that this doubt will remain with them as long as they are alive. It is also permissible that the mention of cutting is a depiction of the state of the removal of doubt.

It was also said: the meaning is, "unless they repent with a repentance by which their hearts are cut in regret and sorrow for their negligence."

Ibn Amir, Hamza, Hafs, Ya'qub, and Abu Ja'far read the initial letter of the imperfect with a fatha (yataqatta'a), and the majority read it with a damma.

It is narrated from Ya'qub that he read "taqta'a" with the lightened form, and the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ): that is, "unless you cut, O Muhammad, their hearts."

The companions of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud read: "wa law taqatta'at qulubuhum" (even if their hearts were cut to pieces).

Al-Hasan, Ya'qub, and Abu Hatim read "ila an tuqta'a" (until they are cut), with the sense of a limit (ghaya), meaning: they will continue in this state until they die.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm﴾ he said: they were some people of the Ansar who built a mosque. Abu Amir al-Rahib said to them: "Build your mosque and gather whatever strength and weapons you can, for I am going to Qaysar, king of the Romans, and I will bring an army of Romans, and I will expel Muhammad and his companions." When they finished their mosque, they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "We have finished building our mosque, so it is incumbent upon you to pray in it and invoke blessing." Then Allah revealed: ﴿Do not stand in it ever.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him that he said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) built the mosque of Quba', men from the Ansar went out, among them Bajdah, the grandfather of Abdullah ibn Hunayf, and Wadi'ah ibn Hizam, and Mujammi' ibn Jariyah al-Ansari, and they built the mosque of hypocrisy. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Bajdah: 'Woe to you, O Bajdah! What did you intend by what I see?' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I intended nothing but good,' and he was lying. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) believed him and wished to excuse him. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief and causing division among the believers and lying in wait for the one who waged war against Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning a man called Abu Amir who had been waging war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He had set off to Heraclius, and they used to watch, so that when Abu Amir came, he would pray in it. He had left Madinah waging war against Allah and His Messenger."

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him, likewise, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, and Malik said to Asim: 'Wait for me until I bring you a fire from my family.' He entered upon his family and took some palm fronds of fire, then they came out running until they entered the mosque, while its people were in it. They burned it and demolished it, and its people came out and dispersed from it. Then Allah revealed this verse."

[p. 599]

Al-Shawkani's commentary on surah 9, verses 107–110 (part 2 of 2):

It is possible that this narration omits something between his (ﷺ) saying "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum" and the words "Malik said to Asim." This is clarified by what Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Abu Ruhm Kulthum ibn al-Husayn al-Ghifari, who was among the Companions who pledged allegiance under the tree, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived and halted at Dhu Awan, a place between him and Madinah, for an hour of the day. The people of the Mosque of Harm (Masjid al-Dirar) had come to him while he was preparing for Tabuk and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we have built a mosque for the sick, the needy, the nights of cold and the nights of rain, and we wish that you would come to us and pray in it for us.' He said: 'I am on the verge of a journey. If we return, God willing, we will come to you and pray for you in it.' When he halted at Dhu Awan, news of the mosque reached him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, brother of the Banu Salim ibn Awf, and Ma'n ibn Adi, and his brother Asim ibn Adi, one of the Banu al-Ajlan, and said: 'Go to this mosque whose people are wrongdoers, demolish it and burn it.' They set out quickly until they reached the Banu Salim ibn Awf, who were the kin of Malik ibn al-Dukhshum. Malik said to Ma'n: 'Wait for me until I come out to you.' He entered his family's house, took a palm frond, lit fire to it, then they both came out running, while its people were inside it, and they burned it and demolished it, and its people dispersed from it. And there was revealed concerning them what was revealed of the Qur'an: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief﴾," and so on to the end of the story.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted that those who built the Mosque of Harm were twelve men, and they mentioned their names.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il transmitted from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "Two men disputed: a man from the Banu Khudrah, and in another wording: I and a man from the Banu Amr ibn Awf disputed concerning the mosque that was founded upon piety (taqwa). The Khudri said: 'It is the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' The Umari said: 'It is the Mosque of Quba'.' They both came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and asked him about it. He said: 'It is this mosque,' meaning the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah, and he said: 'In it there is much good,' meaning the Mosque of Quba'."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar in Akhbar al-Madinah, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim in al-Kuna, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi something similar.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Khatib, and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtara transmitted from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the mosque that was founded upon piety, and he said: 'It is this mosque of mine.'"

Al-Tabarani and al-Diya' al-Maqdisi in al-Mukhtara transmitted from Zayd ibn Thabit, as a marfu' report, something like it.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Tabarani transmitted through the chain of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "The mosque that was founded upon piety from the first day is the Mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Urwah said: "The Mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ) is better than it; it was only revealed concerning the Mosque of Quba'."

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Umar, who said: "The mosque that was founded upon piety is the Mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

The two mentioned (Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Mardawayh) transmitted from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri something similar.

It has been related from a group other than these the same as their statement.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il transmitted from Ibn Abbas that it is the Mosque of Quba'.

Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from al-Dahhak something similar.

It is not hidden from you that the Prophet (ﷺ) specified this mosque that was founded upon piety and affirmed with certainty that it is his mosque (ﷺ), as we have mentioned from the authentic hadiths. Therefore, the statement of an individual Companion, or a group of them, or others, does not stand against that, nor is it valid to cite it in opposition to what has been authentically established from the Prophet (ﷺ). There is also no benefit in citing what has come concerning the merit of praying in the Mosque of Quba', for that does not necessitate that it is the mosque founded upon piety. Moreover, what has come concerning the virtues of the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is, beyond any doubt or uncertainty, far greater than what has come concerning the merit of the Mosque of Quba'.

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "This verse was revealed concerning the people of Quba': ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾." He said: "They used to cleanse themselves with water, so this was revealed concerning them." In its chain is Yunus ibn al-Harith, who is weak.

Al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas, who said: "When this verse was revealed: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for Uwaym ibn Sa'idah and said: 'What is this purification by which God has praised you?' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, no man or woman among us comes out from the toilet without washing his private part,' or he said: 'his anus.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'That is it.'"

Ahmad, Ibn Khuzaymah, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Uwaym ibn Sa'idah al-Ansari that the Prophet (ﷺ) came to them at the Mosque of Quba' and said: "God has praised you well concerning purification in the story of your mosque. What is this purification with which you purify yourselves?" They said: "By God, O Messenger of Allah, we know nothing except that we had Jewish neighbours, who used to wash their posteriors after defecation, so we washed as they washed." Ahmad narrated it from Hasan ibn Muhammad.

Abu Uways narrated to us, Shurahbil narrated to us, from Uwaym ibn Sa'idah, and he mentioned it.

Ibn Khuzaymah also transmitted it in his Sahih.

Ibn Majah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Jarud in al-Muntaqa, al-Daraqutni, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir transmitted from Talhah ibn Nafi', who said: "Abu Ayyub, Jabir ibn Abd Allah, and Anas ibn Malik narrated to me that when this verse was revealed: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O assembly of the Ansar, God has praised you well concerning purification. What is this purification of yours?' They said: 'We perform ablution for prayer and bathe from major impurity.' He said: 'Is there anything with that besides it?' They said: 'No, except that when one of us goes out to relieve himself, he loves to cleanse himself with water.' He said: 'That is it, so adhere to it.'"

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Bukhari in his Tarikh, Ibn Jarir, al-Baghawi in his Mu'jam, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah transmitted from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam, from his father, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to the mosque that was founded upon piety, the Mosque of Quba', he said: 'God has praised you well concerning purification. Will you not tell me?' meaning His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves﴾. They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we find it written upon us in the Torah: cleansing with water, and we do it today.'"

The chain of Ahmad in this hadith is thus: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Malik, meaning Ibn Mighwal, narrated to me, I heard Sayyar Abu al-Hakim, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam.

It has been related from a group of the Successors (tabi'un) something like this concerning the mention of the occasion of revelation of the verse.

It is not hidden from you that some of these hadiths do not contain the identification of the Mosque of Quba' and its people; some are weak; and some have no explicit statement that the mosque founded upon piety is the Mosque of Quba'. In any case, those hadiths that explicitly state that the mosque founded upon piety is the Mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ) are not outweighed by these, in their authenticity and clarity.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿So it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell﴾, that he said: "Meaning its foundations in the fire of Hell."

Musaddad in his Musnad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: "I saw the smoke coming out of the Mosque of Harm at the place where it collapsed, in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il transmitted from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Their building which they built will not cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts﴾, that he said: "Meaning doubt." ﴿Unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾, meaning death.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from Habib ibn Abi Thabit concerning His saying: ﴿a source of doubt in their hearts﴾, that he said: "Rage in their hearts." ﴿Unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾, he said: "Until they die."

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Sufyan concerning His saying: ﴿Unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾, that he said: "Unless they repent."

The commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 9, verses 107–110 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah mentioned the categories of the hypocrites and explained their various ways, He linked to what preceded this group of them, namely those who took a mosque for harm (masjid dirar). The sense is: "And among them are those who took..." The relative pronoun alladhina is a subject (mubtada', the grammatical subject of a nominal sentence), and its predicate (khabar, the grammatical predicate) is the omitted "from among them" (minhum). The sentence is conjoined to what came before it. It is also permissible for the relative clause to be in the accusative position, as a form of censure (dhamm).

The Madinans and Ibn Amir read "alladhina ittakhadhu" without the conjunction waw. In that case it is an independent narrative, with the relative pronoun as subject and its predicate being "do not stand" (la taqum). This was stated by al-Kisa'i.

Al-Nahhas said: the predicate is "their building which they built will never cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts" (la yazalu bunyanuhumu alladhi banaw). It was also said that the predicate is omitted, and the sense is "they will be punished." The identity of those who built the mosque of harm will be explained later. The word dirar (harm) is in the accusative, either as a verbal noun (masdar) or as a causal accusative (ʿillah). The words "disbelief, causing division among the believers, and lying in wait" (wa kufran wa tafriqan bayna al-mu'minin wa irsadan) are conjoined to dirar.

Allah, glory be to Him, has informed us that the motives for their building this mosque were four:

The first: harming others, which is causing injury.

The second: disbelief in Allah and boasting over the people of Islam, because by building it they intended to strengthen the people of hypocrisy.

The third: dividing the believers, because they wanted that they would not attend the mosque of Quba', so that the congregation of the Muslims would diminish. In this there is a considerable amount of discord in unity and the destruction of harmony, which is not hidden.

The fourth: lying in wait (irsad) for the one who waged war against Allah and His Messenger. That is, preparing (i'dad) for the sake of the one who waged war against Allah and His Messenger.

Al-Zajjaj said: irsad means waiting (intizar).

Ibn Qutayba said: irsad means waiting combined with enmity.

Most of the scholars said: it means preparing (i'dad), and the meanings are close. It is said: "arsadtu li-kadha" when I prepared it while watching for it.

Abu Zayd said: it is said "rasadtuhu" and "arsadtuhu" for good, and "arsadtu lahu" for evil.

Ibn al-A'rabi said: one only says "arsadtu," and its meaning is "irtaqabtu" (I awaited).

By "the one who waged war against Allah and His Messenger" is meant the hypocrites, and among them Abu Amir al-Rahib. That is, they prepared it for these people, watched for their arrival, and waited for them, so that they would pray in it and thereby boast over the believers. His saying "min qabl" (beforehand) is linked to "ittakhadhu" (took), meaning they took a mosque before these people became hypocrites and built the mosque of harm. Or it is linked to "harab" (waged war), meaning: for the one who had waged war against Allah and His Messenger before the building of the mosque of harm.

His saying: ﴿And they will surely swear, "We intended nothing but good."﴾ means: we intended nothing but the good quality, which is kindness toward the Muslims. Allah refuted them with His saying: ﴿And Allah testifies that they are liars﴾ in what they swore to.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, forbade His Messenger (ﷺ) from praying in the mosque of harm, saying: ﴿Do not stand in it ever.﴾ That is, at any time. The prohibition on standing in it entails the prohibition on praying in it.

Prayer is sometimes expressed by "standing" (qiyam). One says: "So-and-so stands at night" (yaqumu al-layl), meaning he prays. From this is the sound hadith: "Whoever stands in Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven."

Then Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned the reason for the prohibition on standing in it, saying: ﴿Surely a mosque founded upon piety from the first day is more worthy that you stand in it.﴾ The lam in "la-masjidun" is the lam of oath, and it was also said it is the lam of initiation (ibtida'), and in it there is emphasis on the content of the sentence. The "foundation" (ta'sis) of a building is its establishment and raising. The meaning of its being founded upon piety is that it was founded upon the qualities by which one guards oneself against punishment.

The scholars differed about the mosque that was founded upon piety. One group said it is the mosque of Quba', as narrated from Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, and others. Others held that it is the mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ). The first view is more preponderant, for reasons that will come shortly, if Allah wills.

﴿From the first day﴾ is linked to "was founded" (ussisa): that is, it was founded upon piety from the first day of the days of its founding.

Some grammarians said: "min" here has the meaning of "mundhu" (since): that is, since the first day on which its building began. His saying ﴿is more worthy that you stand in it﴾ is the predicate of the subject.

The meaning is: if standing in any other place were permissible, this mosque would be more fitting for your standing in it, for prayer and the remembrance of Allah, because it was founded upon piety from the first day, and because ﴿in it are men who love to purify themselves﴾. This clause is a new sentence (isti'naf) explaining the greater right of his (ﷺ) standing in it. That is: just as this mosque is more fitting in terms of its location, it is also more fitting in terms of the condition of those in it. It is permissible for this clause to be in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: while in it are men who love to purify themselves. It is also permissible for it to be another attribute of "masjid."

The meaning of their love for purification is that they prefer it and are eager for it whenever its requirement arises. It was also said the meaning is: they love to purify themselves from sins through repentance and seeking forgiveness. The first is more preferable.

It was also said: they love to be purified by the purifying fever from sins, so they all got fever. This view is very weak.

The meaning of Allah's love for them is His good pleasure with them and His kindness toward them, as the lover does with the beloved.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, explained that there is a vast difference between the two groups, saying: ﴿Is one who founded his building upon the fear of Allah and His pleasure better, or one who founded his building on the brink of a crumbling bank that collapsed with him into the fire of Hell?﴾ The interrogative hamza here is for affirmative denial (inkar taqriri). The word bunyan is a verbal noun like 'umran, but here it is used to mean the thing built. The sentence is a new sentence. The meaning: whoever founded the building of his religion upon a strong and firm foundation, which is the fear of Allah and His good pleasure, is better than whoever founded his religion upon the opposite of that, which is falsehood and hypocrisy. The relative pronoun "man" is the subject, and its predicate is "khayr" (better). It was read as "asssa bunyanahu" with the verb in the active voice and "bunyanahu" in the accusative. Abu Ubayda chose this reading. It was also read in the passive voice. It was read "asasu bunyanihi" with "asas" in construct with "bunyanihi." It was read "ussu bunyanihi." The intended meaning is the bases of the building. Abu Hatim transmitted another reading, "a'sas bunyanihi," in the plural. From it is the verse:

"The kingdom has become firm in its foundations, by the noble men of the sons of al-Abbas."

The shafa is the edge, and the jurf is what is swept away by torrents, namely the banks that are carried away by water. The ijtiraf is the uprooting of a thing from its base. It was read with the "ra'" vowelled with a damma, from "jarafa," and also with it unvowelled.

The har is what has fallen. It is said "har al-bina'" when the building collapsed. Its origin is "ha'ir," as they said "shak al-silah" and "shA'ik kadha," as al-Zajjaj said.

Abu Hatim said its origin is "ha'wir."

In Shams al-Ulum it is said: the jurf is what the flood has undermined at its base, and whose top has overhung. If its top splits, then it is the har. End of quotation.

Allah, glory be to Him, made this an example of what they built their false religion upon, which quickly collapses and vanishes. Then He said: ﴿So it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell.﴾ The subject of "fa-inhara" (so it collapsed) is a pronoun referring to the jurf: that is, the bank collapsed with the building into the fire. It is also permissible for the pronoun in "bihi" (with him) to refer to "man," who is the builder.

The meaning is: falsehood collapsed with the builder, or the builder collapsed into the fire of Hell. The collapse, which belongs to the bank, is used as a "tarshih" (a supporting feature that reinforces a metaphor). Glory be to Allah, how eloquent this speech is, how strong its composition, how precise its meaning, and how clear its form.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned that their building this was the cause of increased doubt and continued hesitation and uncertainty. He said: ﴿Their building which they built will never cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts﴾ that is, a state of uncertainty (shakk) in their hearts and hypocrisy. From this is the saying of al-Nabigha:

"I swore, and I left you no doubt in yourself, and there is no refuge for a man beyond Allah."

It was said that the meaning of "rayb" is grief and regret, because they regretted its building. Al-Mubarrad said: that is, heat and rage.

These people who built the mosque of harm were hypocrites who were doubtful about their religion, but they increased in hypocrisy, in determination upon disbelief, and in hatred of Islam, through the demolition by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because of the severe rage and great anger that befell them through its demolition. Then Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned what indicates the continuation and persistence of this doubt, which is His saying: ﴿Except that their hearts be cut into pieces.﴾ That is, this doubt will not cease unless their hearts are cut into pieces and broken into parts, either by death or by the sword. The intended meaning is that this doubt will remain with them as long as they are alive. It is also permissible that the mention of cutting is a depiction of the state of the removal of doubt.

It was also said: the meaning is, "unless they repent with a repentance by which their hearts are cut in regret and sorrow for their negligence."

Ibn Amir, Hamza, Hafs, Ya'qub, and Abu Ja'far read the initial letter of the imperfect with a fatha (yataqatta'a), and the majority read it with a damma.

It is narrated from Ya'qub that he read "taqta'a" with the lightened form, and the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ): that is, "unless you cut, O Muhammad, their hearts."

The companions of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud read: "wa law taqatta'at qulubuhum" (even if their hearts were cut to pieces).

Al-Hasan, Ya'qub, and Abu Hatim read "ila an tuqta'a" (until they are cut), with the sense of a limit (ghaya), meaning: they will continue in this state until they die.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm﴾ he said: they were some people of the Ansar who built a mosque. Abu Amir al-Rahib said to them: "Build your mosque and gather whatever strength and weapons you can, for I am going to Qaysar, king of the Romans, and I will bring an army of Romans, and I will expel Muhammad and his companions." When they finished their mosque, they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "We have finished building our mosque, so it is incumbent upon you to pray in it and invoke blessing." Then Allah revealed: ﴿Do not stand in it ever.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him that he said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) built the mosque of Quba', men from the Ansar went out, among them Bajdah, the grandfather of Abdullah ibn Hunayf, and Wadi'ah ibn Hizam, and Mujammi' ibn Jariyah al-Ansari, and they built the mosque of hypocrisy. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Bajdah: 'Woe to you, O Bajdah! What did you intend by what I see?' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I intended nothing but good,' and he was lying. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) believed him and wished to excuse him. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief and causing division among the believers and lying in wait for the one who waged war against Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning a man called Abu Amir who had been waging war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He had set off to Heraclius, and they used to watch, so that when Abu Amir came, he would pray in it. He had left Madinah waging war against Allah and His Messenger."

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him, likewise, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, and Malik said to Asim: 'Wait for me until I bring you a fire from my family.' He entered upon his family and took some palm fronds of fire, then they came out running until they entered the mosque, while its people were in it. They burned it and demolished it, and its people came out and dispersed from it. Then Allah revealed this verse."

[p. 599]

Al-Shawkani's commentary on surah 9, verses 107–110 (part 2 of 2):

It is possible that this narration omits something between his (ﷺ) saying "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum" and the words "Malik said to Asim." This is clarified by what Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Abu Ruhm Kulthum ibn al-Husayn al-Ghifari, who was among the Companions who pledged allegiance under the tree, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived and halted at Dhu Awan, a place between him and Madinah, for an hour of the day. The people of the Mosque of Harm (Masjid al-Dirar) had come to him while he was preparing for Tabuk and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we have built a mosque for the sick, the needy, the nights of cold and the nights of rain, and we wish that you would come to us and pray in it for us.' He said: 'I am on the verge of a journey. If we return, God willing, we will come to you and pray for you in it.' When he halted at Dhu Awan, news of the mosque reached him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, brother of the Banu Salim ibn Awf, and Ma'n ibn Adi, and his brother Asim ibn Adi, one of the Banu al-Ajlan, and said: 'Go to this mosque whose people are wrongdoers, demolish it and burn it.' They set out quickly until they reached the Banu Salim ibn Awf, who were the kin of Malik ibn al-Dukhshum. Malik said to Ma'n: 'Wait for me until I come out to you.' He entered his family's house, took a palm frond, lit fire to it, then they both came out running, while its people were inside it, and they burned it and demolished it, and its people dispersed from it. And there was revealed concerning them what was revealed of the Qur'an: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief﴾," and so on to the end of the story.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted that those who built the Mosque of Harm were twelve men, and they mentioned their names.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il transmitted from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "Two men disputed: a man from the Banu Khudrah, and in another wording: I and a man from the Banu Amr ibn Awf disputed concerning the mosque that was founded upon piety (taqwa). The Khudri said: 'It is the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' The Umari said: 'It is the Mosque of Quba'.' They both came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and asked him about it. He said: 'It is this mosque,' meaning the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah, and he said: 'In it there is much good,' meaning the Mosque of Quba'."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar in Akhbar al-Madinah, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim in al-Kuna, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi something similar.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Khatib, and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtara transmitted from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the mosque that was founded upon piety, and he said: 'It is this mosque of mine.'"

Al-Tabarani and al-Diya' al-Maqdisi in al-Mukhtara transmitted from Zayd ibn Thabit, as a marfu' report, something like it.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Tabarani transmitted through the chain of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "The mosque that was founded upon piety from the first day is the Mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Urwah said: "The Mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ) is better than it; it was only revealed concerning the Mosque of Quba'."

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Umar, who said: "The mosque that was founded upon piety is the Mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

The two mentioned (Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Mardawayh) transmitted from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri something similar.

It has been related from a group other than these the same as their statement.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il transmitted from Ibn Abbas that it is the Mosque of Quba'.

Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from al-Dahhak something similar.

It is not hidden from you that the Prophet (ﷺ) specified this mosque that was founded upon piety and affirmed with certainty that it is his mosque (ﷺ), as we have mentioned from the authentic hadiths. Therefore, the statement of an individual Companion, or a group of them, or others, does not stand against that, nor is it valid to cite it in opposition to what has been authentically established from the Prophet (ﷺ). There is also no benefit in citing what has come concerning the merit of praying in the Mosque of Quba', for that does not necessitate that it is the mosque founded upon piety. Moreover, what has come concerning the virtues of the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is, beyond any doubt or uncertainty, far greater than what has come concerning the merit of the Mosque of Quba'.

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "This verse was revealed concerning the people of Quba': ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾." He said: "They used to cleanse themselves with water, so this was revealed concerning them." In its chain is Yunus ibn al-Harith, who is weak.

Al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas, who said: "When this verse was revealed: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for Uwaym ibn Sa'idah and said: 'What is this purification by which God has praised you?' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, no man or woman among us comes out from the toilet without washing his private part,' or he said: 'his anus.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'That is it.'"

Ahmad, Ibn Khuzaymah, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Uwaym ibn Sa'idah al-Ansari that the Prophet (ﷺ) came to them at the Mosque of Quba' and said: "God has praised you well concerning purification in the story of your mosque. What is this purification with which you purify yourselves?" They said: "By God, O Messenger of Allah, we know nothing except that we had Jewish neighbours, who used to wash their posteriors after defecation, so we washed as they washed." Ahmad narrated it from Hasan ibn Muhammad.

Abu Uways narrated to us, Shurahbil narrated to us, from Uwaym ibn Sa'idah, and he mentioned it.

Ibn Khuzaymah also transmitted it in his Sahih.

Ibn Majah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Jarud in al-Muntaqa, al-Daraqutni, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir transmitted from Talhah ibn Nafi', who said: "Abu Ayyub, Jabir ibn Abd Allah, and Anas ibn Malik narrated to me that when this verse was revealed: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O assembly of the Ansar, God has praised you well concerning purification. What is this purification of yours?' They said: 'We perform ablution for prayer and bathe from major impurity.' He said: 'Is there anything with that besides it?' They said: 'No, except that when one of us goes out to relieve himself, he loves to cleanse himself with water.' He said: 'That is it, so adhere to it.'"

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Bukhari in his Tarikh, Ibn Jarir, al-Baghawi in his Mu'jam, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Ma'rifah transmitted from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam, from his father, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to the mosque that was founded upon piety, the Mosque of Quba', he said: 'God has praised you well concerning purification. Will you not tell me?' meaning His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves﴾. They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we find it written upon us in the Torah: cleansing with water, and we do it today.'"

The chain of Ahmad in this hadith is thus: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Malik, meaning Ibn Mighwal, narrated to me, I heard Sayyar Abu al-Hakim, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam.

It has been related from a group of the Successors (tabi'un) something like this concerning the mention of the occasion of revelation of the verse.

It is not hidden from you that some of these hadiths do not contain the identification of the Mosque of Quba' and its people; some are weak; and some have no explicit statement that the mosque founded upon piety is the Mosque of Quba'. In any case, those hadiths that explicitly state that the mosque founded upon piety is the Mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ) are not outweighed by these, in their authenticity and clarity.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿So it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell﴾, that he said: "Meaning its foundations in the fire of Hell."

Musaddad in his Musnad, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: "I saw the smoke coming out of the Mosque of Harm at the place where it collapsed, in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il transmitted from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Their building which they built will not cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts﴾, that he said: "Meaning doubt." ﴿Unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾, meaning death.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from Habib ibn Abi Thabit concerning His saying: ﴿a source of doubt in their hearts﴾, that he said: "Rage in their hearts." ﴿Unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾, he said: "Until they die."

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Sufyan concerning His saying: ﴿Unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾, that he said: "Unless they repent."

The commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 9, verses 107–110 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah mentioned the categories of the hypocrites and explained their various ways, He linked to what preceded this group of them, namely those who took a mosque for harm (masjid dirar). The sense is: "And among them are those who took..." The relative pronoun alladhina is a subject (mubtada', the grammatical subject of a nominal sentence), and its predicate (khabar, the grammatical predicate) is the omitted "from among them" (minhum). The sentence is conjoined to what came before it. It is also permissible for the relative clause to be in the accusative position, as a form of censure (dhamm).

The Madinans and Ibn Amir read "alladhina ittakhadhu" without the conjunction waw. In that case it is an independent narrative, with the relative pronoun as subject and its predicate being "do not stand" (la taqum). This was stated by al-Kisa'i.

Al-Nahhas said: the predicate is "their building which they built will never cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts" (la yazalu bunyanuhumu alladhi banaw). It was also said that the predicate is omitted, and the sense is "they will be punished." The identity of those who built the mosque of harm will be explained later. The word dirar (harm) is in the accusative, either as a verbal noun (masdar) or as a causal accusative (ʿillah). The words "disbelief, causing division among the believers, and lying in wait" (wa kufran wa tafriqan bayna al-mu'minin wa irsadan) are conjoined to dirar.

Allah, glory be to Him, has informed us that the motives for their building this mosque were four:

The first: harming others, which is causing injury.

The second: disbelief in Allah and boasting over the people of Islam, because by building it they intended to strengthen the people of hypocrisy.

The third: dividing the believers, because they wanted that they would not attend the mosque of Quba', so that the congregation of the Muslims would diminish. In this there is a considerable amount of discord in unity and the destruction of harmony, which is not hidden.

The fourth: lying in wait (irsad) for the one who waged war against Allah and His Messenger. That is, preparing (i'dad) for the sake of the one who waged war against Allah and His Messenger.

Al-Zajjaj said: irsad means waiting (intizar).

Ibn Qutayba said: irsad means waiting combined with enmity.

Most of the scholars said: it means preparing (i'dad), and the meanings are close. It is said: "arsadtu li-kadha" when I prepared it while watching for it.

Abu Zayd said: it is said "rasadtuhu" and "arsadtuhu" for good, and "arsadtu lahu" for evil.

Ibn al-A'rabi said: one only says "arsadtu," and its meaning is "irtaqabtu" (I awaited).

By "the one who waged war against Allah and His Messenger" is meant the hypocrites, and among them Abu Amir al-Rahib. That is, they prepared it for these people, watched for their arrival, and waited for them, so that they would pray in it and thereby boast over the believers. His saying "min qabl" (beforehand) is linked to "ittakhadhu" (took), meaning they took a mosque before these people became hypocrites and built the mosque of harm. Or it is linked to "harab" (waged war), meaning: for the one who had waged war against Allah and His Messenger before the building of the mosque of harm.

His saying: ﴿And they will surely swear, "We intended nothing but good."﴾ means: we intended nothing but the good quality, which is kindness toward the Muslims. Allah refuted them with His saying: ﴿And Allah testifies that they are liars﴾ in what they swore to.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, forbade His Messenger (ﷺ) from praying in the mosque of harm, saying: ﴿Do not stand in it ever.﴾ That is, at any time. The prohibition on standing in it entails the prohibition on praying in it.

Prayer is sometimes expressed by "standing" (qiyam). One says: "So-and-so stands at night" (yaqumu al-layl), meaning he prays. From this is the sound hadith: "Whoever stands in Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven."

Then Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned the reason for the prohibition on standing in it, saying: ﴿Surely a mosque founded upon piety from the first day is more worthy that you stand in it.﴾ The lam in "la-masjidun" is the lam of oath, and it was also said it is the lam of initiation (ibtida'), and in it there is emphasis on the content of the sentence. The "foundation" (ta'sis) of a building is its establishment and raising. The meaning of its being founded upon piety is that it was founded upon the qualities by which one guards oneself against punishment.

The scholars differed about the mosque that was founded upon piety. One group said it is the mosque of Quba', as narrated from Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, and others. Others held that it is the mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ). The first view is more preponderant, for reasons that will come shortly, if Allah wills.

﴿From the first day﴾ is linked to "was founded" (ussisa): that is, it was founded upon piety from the first day of the days of its founding.

Some grammarians said: "min" here has the meaning of "mundhu" (since): that is, since the first day on which its building began. His saying ﴿is more worthy that you stand in it﴾ is the predicate of the subject.

The meaning is: if standing in any other place were permissible, this mosque would be more fitting for your standing in it, for prayer and the remembrance of Allah, because it was founded upon piety from the first day, and because ﴿in it are men who love to purify themselves﴾. This clause is a new sentence (isti'naf) explaining the greater right of his (ﷺ) standing in it. That is: just as this mosque is more fitting in terms of its location, it is also more fitting in terms of the condition of those in it. It is permissible for this clause to be in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: while in it are men who love to purify themselves. It is also permissible for it to be another attribute of "masjid."

The meaning of their love for purification is that they prefer it and are eager for it whenever its requirement arises. It was also said the meaning is: they love to purify themselves from sins through repentance and seeking forgiveness. The first is more preferable.

It was also said: they love to be purified by the purifying fever from sins, so they all got fever. This view is very weak.

The meaning of Allah's love for them is His good pleasure with them and His kindness toward them, as the lover does with the beloved.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, explained that there is a vast difference between the two groups, saying: ﴿Is one who founded his building upon the fear of Allah and His pleasure better, or one who founded his building on the brink of a crumbling bank that collapsed with him into the fire of Hell?﴾ The interrogative hamza here is for affirmative denial (inkar taqriri). The word bunyan is a verbal noun like 'umran, but here it is used to mean the thing built. The sentence is a new sentence. The meaning: whoever founded the building of his religion upon a strong and firm foundation, which is the fear of Allah and His good pleasure, is better than whoever founded his religion upon the opposite of that, which is falsehood and hypocrisy. The relative pronoun "man" is the subject, and its predicate is "khayr" (better). It was read as "asssa bunyanahu" with the verb in the active voice and "bunyanahu" in the accusative. Abu Ubayda chose this reading. It was also read in the passive voice. It was read "asasu bunyanihi" with "asas" in construct with "bunyanihi." It was read "ussu bunyanihi." The intended meaning is the bases of the building. Abu Hatim transmitted another reading, "a'sas bunyanihi," in the plural. From it is the verse:

"The kingdom has become firm in its foundations, by the noble men of the sons of al-Abbas."

The shafa is the edge, and the jurf is what is swept away by torrents, namely the banks that are carried away by water. The ijtiraf is the uprooting of a thing from its base. It was read with the "ra'" vowelled with a damma, from "jarafa," and also with it unvowelled.

The har is what has fallen. It is said "har al-bina'" when the building collapsed. Its origin is "ha'ir," as they said "shak al-silah" and "shA'ik kadha," as al-Zajjaj said.

Abu Hatim said its origin is "ha'wir."

In Shams al-Ulum it is said: the jurf is what the flood has undermined at its base, and whose top has overhung. If its top splits, then it is the har. End of quotation.

Allah, glory be to Him, made this an example of what they built their false religion upon, which quickly collapses and vanishes. Then He said: ﴿So it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell.﴾ The subject of "fa-inhara" (so it collapsed) is a pronoun referring to the jurf: that is, the bank collapsed with the building into the fire. It is also permissible for the pronoun in "bihi" (with him) to refer to "man," who is the builder.

The meaning is: falsehood collapsed with the builder, or the builder collapsed into the fire of Hell. The collapse, which belongs to the bank, is used as a "tarshih" (a supporting feature that reinforces a metaphor). Glory be to Allah, how eloquent this speech is, how strong its composition, how precise its meaning, and how clear its form.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned that their building this was the cause of increased doubt and continued hesitation and uncertainty. He said: ﴿Their building which they built will never cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts﴾ that is, a state of uncertainty (shakk) in their hearts and hypocrisy. From this is the saying of al-Nabigha:

"I swore, and I left you no doubt in yourself, and there is no refuge for a man beyond Allah."

It was said that the meaning of "rayb" is grief and regret, because they regretted its building. Al-Mubarrad said: that is, heat and rage.

These people who built the mosque of harm were hypocrites who were doubtful about their religion, but they increased in hypocrisy, in determination upon disbelief, and in hatred of Islam, through the demolition by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because of the severe rage and great anger that befell them through its demolition. Then Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned what indicates the continuation and persistence of this doubt, which is His saying: ﴿Except that their hearts be cut into pieces.﴾ That is, this doubt will not cease unless their hearts are cut into pieces and broken into parts, either by death or by the sword. The intended meaning is that this doubt will remain with them as long as they are alive. It is also permissible that the mention of cutting is a depiction of the state of the removal of doubt.

It was also said: the meaning is, "unless they repent with a repentance by which their hearts are cut in regret and sorrow for their negligence."

Ibn Amir, Hamza, Hafs, Ya'qub, and Abu Ja'far read the initial letter of the imperfect with a fatha (yataqatta'a), and the majority read it with a damma.

It is narrated from Ya'qub that he read "taqta'a" with the lightened form, and the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ): that is, "unless you cut, O Muhammad, their hearts."

The companions of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud read: "wa law taqatta'at qulubuhum" (even if their hearts were cut to pieces).

Al-Hasan, Ya'qub, and Abu Hatim read "ila an tuqta'a" (until they are cut), with the sense of a limit (ghaya), meaning: they will continue in this state until they die.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm﴾ he said: they were some people of the Ansar who built a mosque. Abu Amir al-Rahib said to them: "Build your mosque and gather whatever strength and weapons you can, for I am going to Qaysar, king of the Romans, and I will bring an army of Romans, and I will expel Muhammad and his companions." When they finished their mosque, they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "We have finished building our mosque, so it is incumbent upon you to pray in it and invoke blessing." Then Allah revealed: ﴿Do not stand in it ever.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from him that he said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) built the mosque of Quba', men from the Ansar went out, among them Bajdah, the grandfather of Abdullah ibn Hunayf, and Wadi'ah ibn Hizam, and Mujammi' ibn Jariyah al-Ansari, and they built the mosque of hypocrisy. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Bajdah: 'Woe to you, O Bajdah! What did you intend by what I see?' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I intended nothing but good,' and he was lying. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) believed him and wished to excuse him. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief and causing division among the believers and lying in wait for the one who waged war against Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning a man called Abu Amir who had been waging war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He had set off to Heraclius, and they used to watch, so that when Abu Amir came, he would pray in it. He had left Madinah waging war against Allah and His Messenger."

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from him, likewise, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, and Malik said to Asim: 'Wait for me until I bring you a fire from my family.' He entered upon his family and took some palm fronds of fire, then they came out running until they entered the mosque, while its people were in it. They burned it and demolished it, and its people came out and dispersed from it. Then Allah revealed this verse."

[p. 599]

Al-Shawkani's commentary on surah 9, verses 107–110 (part 2 of 2):

It is possible that this narration omits something between his (ﷺ) saying "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum" and the words "Malik said to Asim." This is clarified by what Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Abu Ruhm Kulthum ibn al-Husayn al-Ghifari, who was among the Companions who pledged allegiance under the tree, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived and halted at Dhu Awan, a place between him and Madinah, for an hour of the day. The people of the Mosque of Harm (Masjid al-Dirar) had come to him while he was preparing for Tabuk and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we have built a mosque for the sick, the needy, the nights of cold and the nights of rain, and we wish that you would come to us and pray in it for us.' He said: 'I am on the verge of a journey. If we return, God willing, we will come to you and pray for you in it.' When he halted at Dhu Awan, news of the mosque reached him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, brother of the Banu Salim ibn Awf, and Ma'n ibn Adi, and his brother Asim ibn Adi, one of the Banu al-Ajlan, and said: 'Go to this mosque whose people are wrongdoers, demolish it and burn it.' They set out quickly until they reached the Banu Salim ibn Awf, who were the kin of Malik ibn al-Dukhshum. Malik said to Ma'n: 'Wait for me until I come out to you.' He entered his family's house, took a palm frond, lit fire to it, then they both came out running, while its people were inside it, and they burned it and demolished it, and its people dispersed from it. And there was revealed concerning them what was revealed of the Qur'an: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief﴾," and so on to the end of the story.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted that those who built the Mosque of Harm were twelve men, and they mentioned their names.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il transmitted from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "Two men disputed: a man from the Banu Khudrah, and in another wording: I and a man from the Banu Amr ibn Awf disputed concerning the mosque that was founded upon piety (taqwa). The Khudri said: 'It is the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' The Umari said: 'It is the Mosque of Quba'.' They both came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and asked him about it. He said: 'It is this mosque,' meaning the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah, and he said: 'In it there is much good,' meaning the Mosque of Quba'."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar in Akhbar al-Madinah, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim in al-Kuna, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi something similar.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Khatib, and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtara transmitted from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the mosque that was founded upon piety, and he said: 'It is this mosque of mine.'"

Al-Tabarani and al-Diya' al-Maqdisi in al-Mukhtara transmitted from Zayd ibn Thabit, as a marfu' report, something like it.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Tabarani transmitted through the chain of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "The mosque that was founded upon piety from the first day is the Mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Urwah said: "The Mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ) is better than it; it was only revealed concerning the Mosque of Quba'."

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Umar, who said: "The mosque that was founded upon piety is the Mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

The two mentioned (Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Mardawayh) transmitted from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri something similar.

It has been related from a group other than these the same as their statement.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il transmitted from Ibn Abbas that it is the Mosque of Quba'.

Abu al-Shaykh transmitted from al-Dahhak something similar.

It is not hidden from you that the Prophet (ﷺ) specified this mosque that was founded upon piety and affirmed with certainty that it is his mosque (ﷺ), as we have mentioned from the authentic hadiths. Therefore, the statement of an individual Companion, or a group of them, or others, does not stand against that, nor is it valid to cite it in opposition to what has been authentically established from the Prophet (ﷺ). There is also no benefit in citing what has come concerning the merit of praying in the Mosque of Quba', for that does not necessitate that it is the mosque founded upon piety. Moreover, what has come concerning the virtues of the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is, beyond any doubt or uncertainty, far greater than what has come concerning the merit of the Mosque of Quba'.

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "This verse was revealed concerning the people of Quba': ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾." He said: "They used to cleanse themselves with water, so this was revealed concerning them." In its chain is Yunus ibn al-Harith, who is weak.

Al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas, who said: "When this verse was revealed: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for Uwaym ibn Sa'idah and said: 'What is this purification by which God has praised you?' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, no man or woman among us comes out from the toilet without washing his private part,' or he said: 'his anus.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'That is it.'"

Ahmad, Ibn Khuzaymah, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Uwaym ibn Sa'idah al-Ansari that the Prophet (ﷺ) came to them at the Mosque of Quba' and said: "God has praised you well concerning purification in the story of your mosque. What is this purification with which you purify yourselves?" They said: "By God, O Messenger of Allah, we know nothing except that we had Jewish neighbours, who used to wash their posteriors after defecation, so we washed as they washed." Ahmad narrated it from Hasan ibn Muhammad.

Abu Uways narrated to us, Shurahbil narrated to us, from Uwaym ibn Sa'idah, and he mentioned it.

Ibn Khuzaymah also transmitted it in his Sahih.

Ibn Majah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Jarud in al-Muntaqa, al-Daraqutni, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir transmitted from Talhah ibn Nafi', who said: "Abu Ayyub, Jabir ibn Abd Allah, and Anas ibn Malik narrated to me that when this verse was revealed: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O assembly of the Ansar, God has praised you well concerning purification. What is this purification of yours?' They said: 'We perform ablution for prayer and bathe from major impurity.' He said: 'Is there anything with that besides it?' They said: 'No, except that when one of us goes out to relieve himself, he loves to cleanse himself with water.' He said: 'That is it, so adhere to it.'"
