The ﴿hour of hardship﴾ is the expedition of Tabuk, for they were in severe hardship. So what is meant by "the hour" is all the times of that campaign, and not one specific hour. ﴿Hardship﴾ means difficulty of the matter.

His saying: ﴿After the hearts of a group of them had nearly swerved﴾. In kāda there is a dummy pronoun (ḍamīr al-sha'n), and "qulūb" (hearts) is in the nominative, being the subject of "tazīgh" (swerve), according to Sibawayh. It is also said that it is in the nominative by "kāda", and the sense would be: "after the hearts of a group of them had nearly swerved."

Al-A'mash, Hamzah and Hafs read "yazīgh" with the yā' (third person masculine form).

Abu Hatim said: Whoever reads with the yā' cannot take "al-qulūb" as the subject of kāda.

Al-Nahhas said: What he (Abu Hatim) disallowed is permitted according to others, on the basis of the masculine form for a plural. The meaning of "tazīgh" is that they would be destroyed through exertion, hardship and severity. It is also said that its meaning is: they would incline away from the truth and abandon support and resistance. It is also said that its meaning is: they were resolved to remain behind from the campaign because of the great severity they were in.

In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, it is "min ba'di mā zāghat" (after they had swerved). According to this reading, those are the ones who remained behind. The repetition of the repentance toward them in His saying: ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness that they might repent﴾ is a clear emphasis and attention to its matter. This holds if the pronoun refers to those whose repentance was mentioned earlier. If the pronoun refers to the group, then there is no repetition.

His saying: ﴿And [He turned in forgiveness] to the three who were left behind﴾: that is, He turned in forgiveness to the three who were left behind, meaning deferred, and their repentance was not accepted immediately as the repentance of those remaining behind mentioned earlier had been accepted.

Ibn Jarir said: The meaning of "khullifū" is "left," as one says: "I left so-and-so," meaning I separated from him.

ʿIkrimah ibn Khalid read "khulifū" with the short vowel, meaning: they remained after the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the believers had set out for the campaign.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad read "khālafū" (they opposed). These three were Ka'b ibn Malik, Murarah ibn al-Rabi' or Ibn Rabi'ah al-'Amiri, and Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqifi, all of them from the Helpers. The Prophet (ﷺ) did not accept their repentance until the Qur'an was revealed that God had turned in forgiveness to them. It is also said that the meaning of "khullifū" is: they became corrupt, derived from "khulūf al-fam" (bad breath of the mouth).

His saying: ﴿Until, when the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness﴾: its meaning is that they were deferred from acceptance of repentance until this limit, which is the time when the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness. "Mā" here is a verbal-noun particle (maṣdariyyah): that is, "with its vastness." This was because people turned away from them and did not speak with them, from everyone, for the Prophet (ﷺ) had forbidden people from speaking with them. "Al-rahb" means wide, as one says: "manzil rahb" and "raḥīb" and "rihāb" (a spacious dwelling).

In this verse there is evidence for the permissibility of shunning people of sins as a discipline for them, so that they may desist from sins.

The meaning of "the constriction of their souls upon them" is that their hearts became constricted by the loneliness that befell them and the estrangement that resulted for them. In His saying: ﴿And they knew that there is no refuge from God except in Him﴾, the word "ẓann" (thought/assumption) is used to mean knowledge: that is, they knew that there was no refuge at all to which they could flee except God, glorified is He, through repentance and seeking forgiveness.

His saying: ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness that they might repent﴾: that is, He returned to them with acceptance and mercy, and sent down in the Qur'an the repentance upon them, so that they might be upright, or He enabled them to repent for whatever in the future time they might commit of error, so that they would repent of it, return to God regarding it, and feel remorse for what had occurred from them. ﴿Indeed, God is the Accepting of repentance﴾, that is, the Greatly Accepting of the repentance of those who repent, ﴿the Merciful﴾, that is, the Greatly Merciful to whoever of His servants seeks it.

His saying: ﴿And be with the truthful﴾. This command to be with the truthful, after the story of the three, contains an indication that these three attained through truthfulness what they attained of God's repentance. The apparent meaning of the verse is a command to the servants in general.

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And God would not send astray a people after He has guided them﴾, that he said: It was revealed when they took ransom from the polytheists on the day of the captives.

He said: It was not permitted for you to take it until you were given permission. But God would not punish a people for a sin they had committed ﴿until He makes clear to them what they should avoid﴾. He said: until He forbids them before that.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Mujahid regarding the verse that he said: It is God's clarification to the believers concerning seeking forgiveness for the polytheists specifically, and in His clarification of His obedience and disobedience generally, whether they did or abstained.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym, al-Bayhaqi and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah reported from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab: "Tell us about the matter of the hour of hardship." He said: "We set out with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to Tabuk in intense heat. We stopped at a station, and we were struck there by thirst until we thought our necks would be cut off. So much so that a man would slaughter his camel, squeeze its dung and drink it, and put what remained on his liver. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: 'O Messenger of God, indeed God has accustomed you to good in supplication, so supplicate for us.' He raised his hands and did not lower them until the sky spoke, then it poured heavily and then it flowed. They filled what they had with them, then we went to look and we did not find that it had passed beyond the army."

It is agreed among the narrators that the hour of hardship is the expedition of Tabuk.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mandah, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn ʿAsakir reported from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah regarding His saying: ﴿And [He turned in forgiveness] to the three who were left behind﴾ that he said: They were Ka'b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayyah and Murarah ibn al-Rabi', and all of them were from the Helpers.

Ibn Mandah and Ibn ʿAsakir reported from Ibn ʿAbbas something similar.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others reported "from Ka'b ibn Malik who said: I never remained behind from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in any campaign he undertook, except the campaign of Tabuk. Except that I had remained behind in the campaign of Badr, and he did not reproach anyone who remained behind from it. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) went out seeking the caravan of Quraysh, until God brought them together with their enemy without prior appointment. And I witnessed with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) the night of ʿAqabah, when we agreed together upon Islam, and I would not love to have it in exchange for the battle of Badr, though Badr is more remembered among people and more famous." Then he mentioned the long story well known in the books of hadith and biography, which is known to the people of knowledge, so we will not lengthen by mentioning it.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿And [He turned in forgiveness] to the three who were left behind﴾, that he said: It means they were left behind from repentance; it was not accepted from them when God accepted the repentance of Abu Lubabah and his companions.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn ʿAsakir reported from ʿIkrimah something similar.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Nafi' regarding His saying: ﴿And be with the truthful﴾ that he said: It was revealed concerning the three who were left behind. It was said to them: "Be with Muhammad and his companions."

Ibn Jarir reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His saying: ﴿And be with the truthful﴾ that he said: "With Abu Bakr and ʿUmar."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn ʿAsakir reported from al-Dahhak regarding the verse that he said: "With Abu Bakr and ʿUmar and their companions."

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "With ʿAli ibn Abi Talib."

Ibn ʿAsakir reported from Abu Ja'far who said: "With the three who were left behind."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 9, verses 120–121:

His saying: ﴿It is not for the people of Medina﴾ and so on is an additional emphasis on the obligation of going out to war with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and on the prohibition of staying behind from him. That is: it is not proper and not fitting for the people of Medina ﴿and for those Bedouin around them﴾, such as Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Ashja', Aslam and Ghifar, ﴿to stay behind from the Messenger of Allah﴾ (ﷺ) on the expedition of Tabuk. Allah, glory be to Him, singled them out because they had been called to go forth and did not go forth, unlike the other Arabs, who had not been called to go forth. Yet these, because of their nearness and their being neighbours, were most deserving of giving support and following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿Nor should they prefer themselves over his self﴾: that is, it was not for them to prefer themselves over his self, so that they would be stingy with their own selves and guard them, while not being stingy with the self of the Messenger of Allah and guarding it as they were stingy with and guarded their own selves. It is said: "I turned away from such-and-such" (raghibtu 'an kadha), meaning I held myself above it. Rather, it is obligatory upon them to endure the hardships along with him and to fight before him against the people of opposition, and to give their own selves in place of his self. In this statement there is the meaning of a command to them, together with what its being phrased in this form conveys of rebuke, severe reproach, stirring them up, and disparagement of them.

The reference in His saying "that" (dhalika) is to what the context implies of the obligation to follow the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). That is: that obligation is upon them because they are rewarded for kinds of hardship and types of difficulties.

Al-Zama' (ẓama'): thirst. Al-Nasab: fatigue. Al-Makhmasah: severe hunger, in which the emptiness of the belly becomes apparent.

'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr read "ẓamā'un" with the long vowel (madd).

Others read it with the short vowel (qasr), and both are dialectal forms, like khaṭa'un and khaṭā'un.

The "lā" in these places is an emphatic supernumerary (zā'idah li-l-ta'kid).

The meaning of "in the way of Allah" is "in the obedience of Allah."

His saying: ﴿Nor do they tread a path that enrages the disbelievers﴾: that is, they do not trample any place of the disbelievers with their feet, or with the hooves of their horses, or with the soles of their mounts, so that thereby the disbelievers are enraged.

Al-Mawti' (mawṭi'): is a noun of place, and it may also be a verbal noun. ﴿Nor do they inflict on an enemy any infliction﴾: that is, they strike their enemy with killing, or capture, or defeat, or plunder. Its root is from niltu al-shay' anālu, meaning I attain it.

Al-Kisa'i said: it is from their saying "amrun manīlun minhu" (a matter attainable from him), and it is not from tanāwul (taking hold of); tanāwul is from nultuhu bi-l-'aṭiyyah (I gave him by way of a gift).

Others said: nultu anūlu from giving, and niltuhu anālahu means I reached it.

The pronoun in "bihi" refers to each of the matters mentioned. And "righteous deed" (ʿamal ṣāliḥ) means an accepted good deed: that is, unless Allah records for them a good deed that is accepted, by which He will reward them. The clause ﴿Indeed Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers﴾ is in the sense of a reason for what precedes, while it also encompasses every good-doer, and it applies to those mentioned here in a primary sense.

His saying: ﴿Nor do they spend any expense﴾ is coordinated with what precedes it: that is, no expenditure in war issues from them, even if it is something small and slight. ﴿Nor do they cross a valley﴾: it is originally every opening between mountains and hills that serves as an outlet for floodwater. The Arabs say wādin and awdiyah (plural) contrary to analogy. Al-Nahhas said: "As far as I know, there is no known pattern of fā'il with af'ilah."

﴿Except that it is recorded for them﴾: that is, that which they did of expenditure and travel in jihad is recorded for them, so that Allah may reward them for it ﴿with the best of what they used to do﴾: that is, the best reward for the deeds they used to do. It is also permissible that the pronoun in His saying "it is recorded for them" refers to "righteous deed" (ʿamal ṣāliḥ).

A group has held that this verse is abrogated by the verse mentioned after it, which is His saying: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾ [al-Tawbah: 122], for it indicates the permissibility of some staying behind while others maintain the jihad. This will come later.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, through the chain of 'Umar ibn Malik, from some of the Companions, who said: "When the verse ﴿It is not for the people of Medina﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'By Him who sent me with the truth, were it not for the weak among the people, no expedition would go forth without my being in it.'"

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Zayd, regarding His saying ﴿It is not for the people of Medina﴾, that he said: "This was when Islam was few; it was not permissible for anyone to stay behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then when Islam became numerous and spread, Allah said: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Awza'i, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Fazari, and 'Isa ibn Yunus al-Sab'i that they said regarding His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Nor do they inflict on an enemy any infliction﴾: "This verse is for the Muslims until the Hour arrives."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 9, verse 122–123:

The commentators differed concerning the meaning of ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾. A group held that it belongs to the remaining rulings of jihad, because when Allah, glorified is He, had emphasized the command to fight and the call to go out on raids, the Muslims, whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent out a detachment (sariyyah) against the disbelievers, would all go forth and leave Madinah empty. So Allah, glorified is He, informed them that it was not for them to do that, i.e., it was not correct or proper for them to go forth all together; rather, from every group of them a party should go forth, and the rest of that group should remain behind.

They said: the pronoun in His saying ﴿that they may gain understanding (liyatafaqqahu) in the religion﴾ refers to the group that remains behind.

The meaning is: a party from this group goes out to the raid, and those who remain of the group stand to seek knowledge, and they teach the warriors when they return to them from the raid, or they go in pursuit of it to the place where they find someone from whom they may learn, so that they may take from him the understanding (fiqh) of the religion and warn their people at the time of their return to them. Others held that this verse is not among the remaining rulings of jihad, but is an independent ruling concerning the legitimacy of going forth to seek knowledge and gain understanding of the religion, which Allah, glorified is He, linked to what indicates the obligation of going forth to jihad. Thus travel becomes two kinds: the first, travel for jihad; and the second, travel to seek knowledge. There is no doubt that the obligation of going forth to seek knowledge arises only when the seeker does not find anyone in his own locality from whom he can learn without travel.

Fiqh (understanding of the religion): it is knowledge of the legal rulings (al-ahkam al-shar'iyyah), and of what leads to knowledge of them, such as lexicography (lughah), grammar (nahw), morphology (sarf), rhetoric (bayan) and the principles of jurisprudence (usul).

The meaning of ﴿So why did not a party from every group of them go forth﴾ is: why did they not go forth. Ta'ifah, in the language, means a group.

Allah, glorified is He, has made the purpose of this the understanding of the religion and the warning of those who have not gained understanding. He combined the two good aims and the two sound objectives, namely learning knowledge and teaching it. Whoever seeks knowledge for a purpose other than these two is one who seeks a worldly aim, not a religious aim; so he is as I said:

"The seeker of the world through the knowledge of religion, how wretched he is, like one who went out to rub his sandal with his skullcap."

The meaning of ﴿so that they may beware﴾ (la'allahum yahdharun) is the hope that they will take precaution against neglecting what must be done, or against doing what must be left undone.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded the believers to strive in fighting those of the disbelievers who are near them, and to deal with them in harshness and severity in war. Jihad is obligatory against all the disbelievers, though beginning with those nearest to the fighters is more important and more urgent, then the nearer and the nearer. Then Allah informed them of what strengthens their resolve and steadies their feet, saying: ﴿And know that Allah is with the righteous﴾, i.e., with victory for them and support against their enemy; and whomever Allah is with, nothing can stand against him.

Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh recorded from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "These verses abrogated ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ [al-Tawbah: 41] and ﴿If you do not go forth, He will punish you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 39]. His saying ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾ means: let a party go forth and let a party remain with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Those who remain with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) are those who gain understanding in the religion and warn their brothers when they return to them from the raid, so that they may beware of what has been revealed after them of Allah's decree in His Book and His limits."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi also recorded from him something similar by another route, with a more complete context.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also recorded from him, concerning this verse, that he said: "This verse is not about jihad. Rather, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invoked against Mudar with years of drought, their lands became barren, so a tribe of them would come in its entirety until they emptied Madinah of its hardship, and they would accept Islam while they were liars. They constricted the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and afflicted them, so Allah revealed, informing His Messenger that they were not believers; He returned them to their clans and warned their people not to do as they had done. That is His saying: ﴿so that they may warn their people when they return to them, so that they may beware﴾." There are also reports on this matter from a number of the Successors (tabi'un).

Ibn Abi Hatim recorded from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you﴾, that he said: "The nearest, then the nearest."

Abu al-Shaykh recorded the like of it from al-Dahhak.

Ibn Mardawayh recorded from Ibn 'Umar that he was asked about the raid on the Daylam, and he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: ﴿Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you﴾ — they are the Romans."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh recorded from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿and let them find in you harshness﴾, that he said: "Severity."

"The seeker of the world through the knowledge of religion, how wretched he is, like one who went out to rub his sandal with his skullcap."

The meaning of ﴿so that they may beware﴾ (la'allahum yahdharun) is the hope that they will take precaution against neglecting what must be done, or against doing what must be left undone.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded the believers to strive in fighting those of the disbelievers who are near them, and to deal with them in harshness and severity in war. Jihad is obligatory against all the disbelievers, though beginning with those nearest to the fighters is more important and more urgent, then the nearer and the nearer. Then Allah informed them of what strengthens their resolve and steadies their feet, saying: ﴿And know that Allah is with the righteous﴾, i.e., with victory for them and support against their enemy; and whomever Allah is with, nothing can stand against him.

Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh recorded from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "These verses abrogated ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ [al-Tawbah: 41] and ﴿If you do not go forth, He will punish you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 39]. His saying ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾ means: let a party go forth and let a party remain with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Those who remain with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) are those who gain understanding in the religion and warn their brothers when they return to them from the raid, so that they may beware of what has been revealed after them of Allah's decree in His Book and His limits."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi also recorded from him something similar by another route, with a more complete context.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also recorded from him, concerning this verse, that he said: "This verse is not about jihad. Rather, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invoked against Mudar with years of drought, their lands became barren, so a tribe of them would come in its entirety until they emptied Madinah of its hardship, and they would accept Islam while they were liars. They constricted the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and afflicted them, so Allah revealed, informing His Messenger that they were not believers; He returned them to their clans and warned their people not to do as they had done. That is His saying: ﴿so that they may warn their people when they return to them, so that they may beware﴾." There are also reports on this matter from a number of the Successors (tabi'un).

Ibn Abi Hatim recorded from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you﴾, that he said: "The nearest, then the nearest."

Abu al-Shaykh recorded the like of it from al-Dahhak.

Ibn Mardawayh recorded from Ibn 'Umar that he was asked about the raid on the Daylam, and he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: ﴿Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you﴾ — they are the Romans."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh recorded from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿and let them find in you harshness﴾, that he said: "Severity."

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 9, verses 124–129 (part 1 of 2)**

His saying: ﴿And whenever a surah is sent down﴾, a report from Him, glorified is He, concerning the remaining disgraceful acts of the hypocrites. That is: whenever Allah sends down to His Messenger (ﷺ) a surah from His Mighty Book, some of the hypocrites say to their companions among them, "Which of you has had his faith increased by this surah that has been revealed?" They say this mockingly toward the believers. It is also possible that they said it to a group of Muslims, intending by it to turn them away from Islam and to make them averse to it. The word ﴿أيُّكم﴾ (ayyukum, "which of you") is in the nominative case as the subject of the sentence, and its predicate is ﴿زادَتْهُ﴾ (zadathu, "has increased him").

The explanation of the meaning of "surah" has already been given.

Then, after their statement, Allah, glorified is He, reports that the believers had their faith increased, in addition to their existing faith, and that they rejoice, along with this increase, at the descent of revelation and at what it contains of religious and worldly benefits.

﴿As for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, and they are the hypocrites, the revealed surah increases them in ﴿رِجْسًا﴾ (rijsan, "uncleanness") in addition to their uncleanness, that is, in wickedness added to the wickedness they already had: disbelief, corruption of belief, and displaying what is other than what they conceal. They persisted in this and remained upon it until they died as disbelieving hypocrites. The meaning of "disease" here is doubt and hypocrisy. It has also been said that the meaning is: it increases them in sin in addition to their sin.

His saying: ﴿Do they not see that they are tested every year once or twice?﴾

The majority of reciters (qira'ah, "recited reading") read ﴿يَرَوْنَ﴾ (yarawna, "they see") with the third-person ya' (the yā' prefix).

Hamzah and Ya'qub read it with the second-person ta' (تاء, "you"), addressing the believers.

al-A'mash read ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا﴾ (awa lam yarawa, "have they not seen").

Talhah ibn Musarrif read ﴿أوَلا تَرى﴾ (awa la tara, "do you not see"), addressing the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This is also the reading of Ibn Mas'ud.

The meaning of ﴿يُفْتَنُونَ﴾ (yuftanuna, "they are tested") is "they are examined." This is what Ibn Jarir and others said. Or Allah tests them with drought and hardship, as Mujahid said. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: with illnesses and pains. Qatadah and al-Hasan said: with raids and jihad alongside the Prophet (ﷺ), and they see what Allah promised of victory.

﴿Then they do not repent﴾ because of that, ﴿nor do they take heed﴾. The particle ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ (thumma, "then") is for the coordination of what follows it with ﴿يَرَوْنَ﴾. The interrogative hamzah in ﴿أوَلا يَرَوْنَ﴾ is for censure and rebuke, and the waw is a conjunction coordinating with an implied element: that is, "they do not look, and they do not see." This is an expression of wonder from Allah, glorified is He, to the believers, concerning the state of the hypocrites, their obstinacy in hypocrisy, and their neglect of reflection and lesson-taking.

Then Allah, glorified is He, mentioned what they used to do when a surah was sent down, after mentioning what they used to say. He said: ﴿And whenever a surah is sent down, some of them look at others﴾. That is: some of the hypocrites look at others, saying ﴿هَلْ يَراكم مِن أحَدٍ﴾ (hal yarakum min ahad, "Does anyone see you?"), meaning from among the believers, so that we may withdraw from the place where revelation descends, for we have no patience to listen to it, and so that we may speak what we want of slander, mockery and laughter.

It has also been said that the meaning is: when a surah is sent down in which Allah mentions the disgraceful acts and shame of the hypocrites, some of those who attend the gathering of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to others among them, "Does anyone see you?" Then they went away to their homes.

Ibn Jarir reported from some of the people of knowledge that he said: the word ﴿نَظَرَ﴾ (nazara, "looked") in this verse is used in place of "said." That is: some of them said to others, "Does anyone see you?"

His saying: ﴿Then they turned away﴾, that is, from that gathering, to (p. 608) their homes. Or they turned away from what leads to guidance and faith to what leads to disbelief and hypocrisy.

Then Allah, glorified is He, invoked against them, saying: ﴿Allah has turned their hearts away﴾, that is, He turned them away from goodness and from what would be right and guidance for them. He, glorified is He, is the Turner of hearts and the One who causes them to turn. It has also been said that the meaning is: He forsook them, so that they could not accept guidance. It has been said that it is a supplication that is not intended to bring about its content, like the saying of the people, "May Allah fight him" (qatalahu Allah).

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned the reason for which they turned away from the place of guidance, or the reason for which they deserved the supplication against them, by His words: ﴿Allah has turned their hearts away, because they are a people who do not understand﴾, that is, what they hear, because of their lack of contemplation and fairness.

Then Allah, glorified is He, concluded this surah with what alleviates, in the sight of the believers, some of the heavy obligations it contains. He said: ﴿There has certainly come to you, O company of Arabs, a Messenger from Allah, who has a great station, from among yourselves﴾, meaning from your own kind in being an Arab. The majority of exegetes held that this verse is addressed to the Arabs.

Al-Zajjaj said: it is addressed to the whole world.

The meaning is: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among﴾ your kind in humanity, ﴿who grieves over what distresses you﴾. The particle ﴿ما﴾ (ma, "what") is a verbal-masdar particle (mā maṣdariyyah). The meaning: his distress at your suffering is great, because he is of your kind, and sent for your guidance. The word ﴿العَنَتُ﴾ (al-'anat, "suffering") means hardship for them and difficulty upon them, whether through the punishment of this world, by the sword and the like, or through the punishment of the Hereafter, by the Fire, or both together. ﴿He is eager for you﴾, that is, he is greedy for you that you should not enter the Fire, or eager for your faith.

The first is preferable, and al-Farra' said so. ﴿Kind and merciful﴾: their meanings have already been explained. That is: this Messenger is kind and merciful toward the believers among you, O Arabs, or toward people.

Then He said, addressing His Messenger and consoling him, and guiding him to what he should say when he is disobeyed: ﴿But if they turn away﴾, that is, they turn away from you and do not act upon what you have brought, nor accept it. Then say, O Muhammad: ﴿Allah is sufficient for me﴾, that is, Allah, glorified is He, the One alone deserving worship, is sufficient for me. ﴿Upon Him I have relied﴾, that is, I have entrusted all my affairs to Him. ﴿He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾. He described it with greatness because it is the greatest of created things.

The majority read ﴿العَرْشِ﴾ (al-'arshi, "the Throne") in the genitive case, as an adjective for ﴿عَرْشٍ﴾ (in "the Throne"). Ibn Muhaysin read it in the nominative case as an adjective for ﴿رَبُّ﴾ (Rabb, "Lord"). This reading has also been narrated from Ibn Kathir.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith﴾, that he said: whenever a surah was revealed, they believed in it, and Allah increased them in faith and confirmation, and they rejoiced in it.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿uncleanness upon their uncleanness﴾, that he said: doubt upon their doubt.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Do they not see that they are tested﴾, that he said: they are killed.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Mujahid something similar, and he said: with drought and hunger.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from al-Hasan, who said: with the enemy.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Qatadah, who said: with raiding in the way of Allah.

Abu al-Shaykh reported from Bakkar ibn Malik, who said: they fall ill every year once or twice.

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Abu Sa'id, who said: they had one or two lies every year.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Hudhayfah, who said: we used to hear one or two lies every year, by which a large group of people went astray.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿some of them look at others﴾, that he said: they are the hypocrites.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Do not say "we turned away from the prayer," for indeed a people turned away and Allah turned their hearts; rather say "we completed the prayer."

Ibn Abi Shaybah reported something similar from Ibn 'Umar.

I say: The word "turning away" (al-insiraf) can be used for turning away from good as it can be used for turning away from evil. Its use here for the hypocrites' return from the gathering of goodness does not indicate that it is used only for such a thing. Otherwise it would follow that every word used in the Arabic language for multiple matters, when used in the Qur'an to report what the disbelievers did, could not be used to report what the people of goodness did, such as return, going, entering, leaving, standing and sitting. The implication is false by consensus (ijma', "scholarly agreement"), so the implied (the consequent) is likewise false. The reasoning of the implication is clear and does not need explanation.

Abd ibn Humayd, al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah in his Musnad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, and Ibn 'Asakir reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾, that he said: there is no tribe among the Arabs but that the Prophet (ﷺ) has been born into it, from its Mudar, its Rabi'ah, and its Yemen.

Ibn Sa'd reported from him regarding His saying "from among yourselves", that he said: you gave birth to him, O company of Arabs.

'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, regarding His saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾, that he said: nothing of the birth of the Age of Ignorance touched him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I came forth from a marriage and did not come forth from fornication." This report has a break in its chain (inqita', "disconnection"), but al-Hafiz al-Ramahurmuzi connected it in his book al-Fasil bayn al-Rawi wa al-Wa'i. He said: Abu Ahmad Yusuf ibn Harun ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: I bear witness concerning my father who narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I came forth from a marriage and did not come forth from fornication, from Adam until my father and my mother gave birth to me."

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾, and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the meaning of "from among yourselves"? He said: "Lineage, in-law relations and nobility. There is no fornication in me, nor in my fathers from Adam; all of us are from marriage."

al-Hakim reported from Ibn 'Abbas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾, meaning "from among the most honored of you in rank."

Ibn Sa'd reported from him something similar to the first hadith of 'Ali.

al-Tabarani reported from him as well something similar.

Ibn Sa'd and Ibn 'Asakir reported from 'A'ishah something similar.

There are hadiths with the same meaning on this subject, and what is in Sahih Muslim and others supports it, from the hadith of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah chose Isma'il from the children of Ibrahim, (p. 609) and chose from the children of Isma'il the Banu Kinanah, and chose from the Banu Kinanah the Quraysh, and chose from the Quraysh the Banu Hashim, and chose me from the Banu Hashim."

Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym and al-Bayhaqi reported from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah created the creation, He made me among the best of His creation. Then when He divided them into two groups, He made me among the best of the two groups. Then when He created the tribes, He made me among the best tribe. And when He created the souls, He made me among the best of their souls. Then when He created the houses, He made me among the best of their houses. So I am the best of them in house and the best of them in soul." There are hadiths on this subject.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Ibn Mani', Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il reported through the route of Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The last verse revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ), and in another wording: the last of the Qur'an to be revealed, was ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾ to the end of the verse. Something similar has been narrated from him through another route, recorded by Abd Allah ibn Ahmad in Zawa'id al-Musnad, Ibn al-Dharis in his Fada'il, Ibn Abi Dawud in al-Masahif, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il, al-Khatib in Talkhis al-Mutashabih, and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Medina, the tribe of Juhayna came to him and said: 'You have settled among us, so make a covenant with us: we will be safe from you and you will be safe from us.' He said: 'Why do you ask this?' They said: 'We seek safety.' So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿But if they turn away, say: Allah is sufficient for me﴾, that it means: the disbelievers turned away from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, who said: The Throne ('arsh) was so named only because of its elevation (irtifa'), and many hadiths have been related concerning the description of the Throne, its reality (mahiyyah) and its extent (qadr).

Here ends the first third of the tafsir called Fath al-Qadir, which combines the two disciplines of transmission (riwayah) and understanding (dirayah) in the science of tafsir, by the pen of its author Muhammad ibn Ali al-Shawkani, may Allah forgive them both.

The completion of this third was on the afternoon of Tuesday, perhaps the twentieth of the month of Muharram, in the year 1227 AH.

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon the master of the messengers, and upon his family and all his companions.

Its hearing (sama') was completed in the presence of its author, may Allah prolong his life, in the month of Jumada al-Ula of the year 1235 AH.

Yahya ibn Ali al-Shawkani, may Allah forgive them both. Amin.

The word ﴿أيُّكم﴾ (ayyukum, "which of you") is in the nominative case as the subject of the sentence, and its predicate is ﴿زادَتْهُ﴾ (zadathu, "has increased him").

The explanation of the meaning of "surah" has already been given.

Then, after their statement, Allah, glorified is He, reports that the believers had their faith increased, in addition to their existing faith, and that they rejoice, along with this increase, at the descent of revelation and at what it contains of religious and worldly benefits.

﴿As for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, and they are the hypocrites, the revealed surah increases them in ﴿رِجْسًا﴾ (rijsan, "uncleanness") in addition to their uncleanness, that is, in wickedness added to the wickedness they already had: disbelief, corruption of belief, and displaying what is other than what they conceal. They persisted in this and remained upon it until they died as disbelieving hypocrites. The meaning of "disease" here is doubt and hypocrisy. It has also been said that the meaning is: it increases them in sin in addition to their sin.

His saying: ﴿Do they not see that they are tested every year once or twice?﴾

Talhah ibn Musarrif read ﴿أوَلا تَرى﴾ (awa la tara, "do you not see"), addressing the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This is also the reading of Ibn Mas'ud.

Ibn Jarir reported from some of the people of knowledge that he said: the word ﴿نَظَرَ﴾ (nazara, "looked") in this verse is used in place of "said." That is: some of them said to others, "Does anyone see you?"

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿But if they turn away, say: Allah is sufficient for me﴾, that it means: the disbelievers turned away from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Here ends the first third of the tafsir called Fath al-Qadir, which combines the two disciplines of transmission (riwayah) and understanding (dirayah) in the science of tafsir, by the pen of its author Muhammad ibn Ali al-Shawkani, may Allah forgive them both.

The completion of this third was on the afternoon of Tuesday, perhaps the twentieth of the month of Muharram, in the year 1227 AH.

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon the master of the messengers, and upon his family and all his companions.

Its hearing (sama') was completed in the presence of its author, may Allah prolong his life, in the month of Jumada al-Ula of the year 1235 AH.

Yahya ibn Ali al-Shawkani, may Allah forgive them both. Amin.

The explanation of the meaning of "surah" has already been given.

Then, after their statement, Allah, glorified is He, reports that the believers had their faith increased, in addition to their existing faith, and that they rejoice, along with this increase, at the descent of revelation and at what it contains of religious and worldly benefits.

They persisted in this and remained upon it until they died as disbelieving hypocrites. The meaning of "disease" here is doubt and hypocrisy. It has also been said that the meaning is: it increases them in sin in addition to their sin.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿But if they turn away, say: Allah is sufficient for me﴾, that it means: the disbelievers turned away from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, who said: The Throne ('arsh) was so named only because of its elevation (irtifa'), and many hadiths have been related concerning the description of the Throne, its reality (mahiyyah) and its extent (qadr).

Here ends the first third of the tafsir called Fath al-Qadir, which combines the two disciplines of transmission (riwayah) and understanding (dirayah) in the science of tafsir, by the pen of its author Muhammad ibn Ali al-Shawkani, may Allah forgive them both.

The completion of this third was on the afternoon of Tuesday, perhaps the twentieth of the month of Muharram, in the year 1227 AH.

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon the master of the messengers, and upon his family and all his companions.

Its hearing (sama') was completed in the presence of its author, may Allah prolong his life, in the month of Jumada al-Ula of the year 1235 AH.

Yahya ibn Ali al-Shawkani, may Allah forgive them both. Amin.

**Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 9, verses 124–129 (part 1 of 2)**

His saying: ﴿And whenever a surah is sent down﴾, a report from Him, glorified is He, concerning the remaining disgraceful acts of the hypocrites. That is: whenever Allah sends down to His Messenger (ﷺ) a surah from His Mighty Book, some of the hypocrites say to their companions among them, "Which of you has had his faith increased by this surah that has been revealed?" They say this mockingly toward the believers. It is also possible that they said it to a group of Muslims, intending by it to turn them away from Islam and to make them averse to it. The word ﴿أيُّكم﴾ (ayyukum, "which of you") is in the nominative case as the subject of the sentence, and its predicate is ﴿زادَتْهُ﴾ (zadathu, "has increased him").

The explanation of the meaning of "surah" has already been given.

Then, after their statement, Allah, glorified is He, reports that the believers had their faith increased, in addition to their existing faith, and that they rejoice, along with this increase, at the descent of revelation and at what it contains of religious and worldly benefits.

﴿As for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, and they are the hypocrites, the revealed surah increases them in ﴿رِجْسًا﴾ (rijsan, "uncleanness") in addition to their uncleanness, that is, in wickedness added to the wickedness they already had: disbelief, corruption of belief, and displaying what is other than what they conceal. They persisted in this and remained upon it until they died as disbelieving hypocrites. The meaning of "disease" here is doubt and hypocrisy. It has also been said that the meaning is: it increases them in sin in addition to their sin.

His saying: ﴿Do they not see that they are tested every year once or twice?﴾

The majority of reciters (qira'ah, "recited reading") read ﴿يَرَوْنَ﴾ (yarawna, "they see") with the third-person ya' (the yā' prefix).

Hamzah and Ya'qub read it with the second-person ta' (تاء, "you"), addressing the believers.

al-A'mash read ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا﴾ (awa lam yarawa, "have they not seen").

Talhah ibn Musarrif read ﴿أوَلا تَرى﴾ (awa la tara, "do you not see"), addressing the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This is also the reading of Ibn Mas'ud.

The meaning of ﴿يُفْتَنُونَ﴾ (yuftanuna, "they are tested") is "they are examined." This is what Ibn Jarir and others said. Or Allah tests them with drought and hardship, as Mujahid said. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: with illnesses and pains. Qatadah and al-Hasan said: with raids and jihad alongside the Prophet (ﷺ), and they see what Allah promised of victory.

﴿Then they do not repent﴾ because of that, ﴿nor do they take heed﴾. The particle ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ (thumma, "then") is for the coordination of what follows it with ﴿يَرَوْنَ﴾. The interrogative hamzah in ﴿أوَلا يَرَوْنَ﴾ is for censure and rebuke, and the waw is a conjunction coordinating with an implied element: that is, "they do not look, and they do not see." This is an expression of wonder from Allah, glorified is He, to the believers, concerning the state of the hypocrites, their obstinacy in hypocrisy, and their neglect of reflection and lesson-taking.

Then Allah, glorified is He, mentioned what they used to do when a surah was sent down, after mentioning what they used to say. He said: ﴿And whenever a surah is sent down, some of them look at others﴾. That is: some of the hypocrites look at others, saying ﴿هَلْ يَراكم مِن أحَدٍ﴾ (hal yarakum min ahad, "Does anyone see you?"), meaning from among the believers, so that we may withdraw from the place where revelation descends, for we have no patience to listen to it, and so that we may speak what we want of slander, mockery and laughter.

It has also been said that the meaning is: when a surah is sent down in which Allah mentions the disgraceful acts and shame of the hypocrites, some of those who attend the gathering of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to others among them, "Does anyone see you?" Then they went away to their homes.

Ibn Jarir reported from some of the people of knowledge that he said: the word ﴿نَظَرَ﴾ (nazara, "looked") in this verse is used in place of "said." That is: some of them said to others, "Does anyone see you?"

His saying: ﴿Then they turned away﴾, that is, from that gathering, to (p. 608) their homes. Or they turned away from what leads to guidance and faith to what leads to disbelief and hypocrisy.

Then Allah, glorified is He, invoked against them, saying: ﴿Allah has turned their hearts away﴾, that is, He turned them away from goodness and from what would be right and guidance for them. He, glorified is He, is the Turner of hearts and the One who causes them to turn. It has also been said that the meaning is: He forsook them, so that they could not accept guidance. It has been said that it is a supplication that is not intended to bring about its content, like the saying of the people, "May Allah fight him" (qatalahu Allah).

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned the reason for which they turned away from the place of guidance, or the reason for which they deserved the supplication against them, by His words: ﴿Allah has turned their hearts away, because they are a people who do not understand﴾, that is, what they hear, because of their lack of contemplation and fairness.

Then Allah, glorified is He, concluded this surah with what alleviates, in the sight of the believers, some of the heavy obligations it contains. He said: ﴿There has certainly come to you, O company of Arabs, a Messenger from Allah, who has a great station, from among yourselves﴾, meaning from your own kind in being an Arab. The majority of exegetes held that this verse is addressed to the Arabs.

Al-Zajjaj said: it is addressed to the whole world.

The meaning is: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among﴾ your kind in humanity, ﴿who grieves over what distresses you﴾. The particle ﴿ما﴾ (ma, "what") is a verbal-masdar particle (mā maṣdariyyah). The meaning: his distress at your suffering is great, because he is of your kind, and sent for your guidance. The word ﴿العَنَتُ﴾ (al-'anat, "suffering") means hardship for them and difficulty upon them, whether through the punishment of this world, by the sword and the like, or through the punishment of the Hereafter, by the Fire, or both together. ﴿He is eager for you﴾, that is, he is greedy for you that you should not enter the Fire, or eager for your faith.

The first is preferable, and al-Farra' said so. ﴿Kind and merciful﴾: their meanings have already been explained. That is: this Messenger is kind and merciful toward the believers among you, O Arabs, or toward people.

Then He said, addressing His Messenger and consoling him, and guiding him to what he should say when he is disobeyed: ﴿But if they turn away﴾, that is, they turn away from you and do not act upon what you have brought, nor accept it. Then say, O Muhammad: ﴿Allah is sufficient for me﴾, that is, Allah, glorified is He, the One alone deserving worship, is sufficient for me. ﴿Upon Him I have relied﴾, that is, I have entrusted all my affairs to Him. ﴿He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾. He described it with greatness because it is the greatest of created things.

The majority read ﴿العَرْشِ﴾ (al-'arshi, "the Throne") in the genitive case, as an adjective for ﴿عَرْشٍ﴾ (in "the Throne"). Ibn Muhaysin read it in the nominative case as an adjective for ﴿رَبُّ﴾ (Rabb, "Lord"). This reading has also been narrated from Ibn Kathir.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith﴾, that he said: whenever a surah was revealed, they believed in it, and Allah increased them in faith and confirmation, and they rejoiced in it.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿uncleanness upon their uncleanness﴾, that he said: doubt upon their doubt.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Do they not see that they are tested﴾, that he said: they are killed.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Mujahid something similar, and he said: with drought and hunger.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from al-Hasan, who said: with the enemy.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Qatadah, who said: with raiding in the way of Allah.

Abu al-Shaykh reported from Bakkar ibn Malik, who said: they fall ill every year once or twice.

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Abu Sa'id, who said: they had one or two lies every year.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Hudhayfah, who said: we used to hear one or two lies every year, by which a large group of people went astray.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿some of them look at others﴾, that he said: they are the hypocrites.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Do not say "we turned away from the prayer," for indeed a people turned away and Allah turned their hearts; rather say "we completed the prayer."

Ibn Abi Shaybah reported something similar from Ibn 'Umar.

I say: The word "turning away" (al-insiraf) can be used for turning away from good as it can be used for turning away from evil. Its use here for the hypocrites' return from the gathering of goodness does not indicate that it is used only for such a thing. Otherwise it would follow that every word used in the Arabic language for multiple matters, when used in the Qur'an to report what the disbelievers did, could not be used to report what the people of goodness did, such as return, going, entering, leaving, standing and sitting. The implication is false by consensus (ijma', "scholarly agreement"), so the implied (the consequent) is likewise false. The reasoning of the implication is clear and does not need explanation.

Abd ibn Humayd, al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah in his Musnad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, and Ibn 'Asakir reported from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾, that he said: there is no tribe among the Arabs but that the Prophet (ﷺ) has been born into it, from its Mudar, its Rabi'ah, and its Yemen.

Ibn Sa'd reported from him regarding His saying "from among yourselves", that he said: you gave birth to him, O company of Arabs.

'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, regarding His saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾, that he said: nothing of the birth of the Age of Ignorance touched him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I came forth from a marriage and did not come forth from fornication." This report has a break in its chain (inqita', "disconnection"), but al-Hafiz al-Ramahurmuzi connected it in his book al-Fasil bayn al-Rawi wa al-Wa'i. He said: Abu Ahmad Yusuf ibn Harun ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: I bear witness concerning my father who narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I came forth from a marriage and did not come forth from fornication, from Adam until my father and my mother gave birth to me."

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾, and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the meaning of "from among yourselves"? He said: "Lineage, in-law relations and nobility. There is no fornication in me, nor in my fathers from Adam; all of us are from marriage."

al-Hakim reported from Ibn 'Abbas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾, meaning "from among the most honored of you in rank."

Ibn Sa'd reported from him something similar to the first hadith of 'Ali.

al-Tabarani reported from him as well something similar.

Ibn Sa'd and Ibn 'Asakir reported from 'A'ishah something similar.

There are hadiths with the same meaning on this subject, and what is in Sahih Muslim and others supports it, from the hadith of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah chose Isma'il from the children of Ibrahim, (p. 609) and chose from the children of Isma'il the Banu Kinanah, and chose from the Banu Kinanah the Quraysh, and chose from the Quraysh the Banu Hashim, and chose me from the Banu Hashim."

Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym and al-Bayhaqi reported from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah created the creation, He made me among the best of His creation. Then when He divided them into two groups, He made me among the best of the two groups. Then when He created the tribes, He made me among the best tribe. And when He created the souls, He made me among the best of their souls. Then when He created the houses, He made me among the best of their houses. So I am the best of them in house and the best of them in soul." There are hadiths on this subject.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Ibn Mani', Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il reported through the route of Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The last verse revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ), and in another wording: the last of the Qur'an to be revealed, was ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾ to the end of the verse. Something similar has been narrated from him through another route, recorded by Abd Allah ibn Ahmad in Zawa'id al-Musnad, Ibn al-Dharis in his Fada'il, Ibn Abi Dawud in al-Masahif, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il, al-Khatib in Talkhis al-Mutashabih, and al-Diya' in al-Mukhtarah.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Medina, the tribe of Juhayna came to him and said: 'You have settled among us, so make a covenant with us: we will be safe from you and you will be safe from us.' He said: 'Why do you ask this?' They said: 'We seek safety.' So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿But if they turn away, say: Allah is sufficient for me﴾, that it means: the disbelievers turned away from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, who said: The Throne ('arsh) was so named only because of its elevation (irtifa'), and many hadiths have been related concerning the description of the Throne, its reality (mahiyyah) and its extent (qadr).

The completion of this third was on the afternoon of Tuesday, perhaps the twentieth of the month of Muharram, in the year 1227 AH.

Its hearing (sama') was completed in the presence of its author, may Allah prolong his life, in the month of Jumada al-Ula of the year 1235 AH.
